<meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s exploration of the soul (Anima), specifically defining its nature through the writings of Church Fathers and philosophers to demonstrate that it is a composition of divine light and a created spiritual vehicle.</meta>

# Mosaical Philosophy. Book 1.

*When God receives or withdraws His Spirit from the creatures, they expire; but by sending out His Spirit, they are recreated with life and goodness.* <note>original: "Deo recipiente Spiritum suum à creaturis, exspirant, emittente spiritum recreantur bona."</note> And now I will prove all of this using the definitions or descriptions that both the Fathers of the Church and the Philosophers (both Christian and Gentile) have made regarding the soul in general—both in its relationship to a body and in its simple and separate state. **John of Damascus** <note>original: "Damascene"</note> seems to define it this way: *The soul is a spiritual substance flowing from the divine fountains; it is simple, indissoluble, immortal, free, incorporeal, and indivisible; it lacks quantity, shape, weight, and color.* <note>original: "Anima est substantia spiritualis a divinis fontibus emanans, simplex, indissolubilis, immortalis, libera, incorporea, & indivisibilis; quantitate, figura, pondere, & colore carens."</note> **St. Bernard** also seems to agree with this.

<margin>Augustine</margin>
And **Augustine** defines it like this: *It is a divine mind that understands all things and conforms itself to the shape or likeness of all things.* <note>original: "Est mens divina omnia intelligens omnibusque se assimilans"</note> For this reason, certain Philosophers say that it is made after the likeness of the Spirit of Wisdom, which is known to be the Image of God; for it carries the likeness of every thing within itself. Therefore, it is defined by them to be the *similitude of all things*. And truly, it has this power within itself to apprehend and find out all things. Again, it is like all things, because it is the "one" within "all."

<margin>Agrippa, Book 3, Chapter 37.</margin>
There are some of the more divine type of Mystical Philosophers who seem to define the human soul more fully in this way: *The soul is a certain divine Light, created after the Image of the Word (the cause of causes and the first pattern), a substance of God, and shaped by His seal, whose character is the eternal Word.* <note>original: "Anima est lux quaedam divina ad imaginem Verbi, causæ causarum, primi exemplaris, creata; substantia Dei, sigilloque figurata, cujus character est verbum æternum"</note> Another defines it thus: *It is an incorporeal thing adorned with all beauty, made like the Holy Trinity, and made equal to eternal glory.* <note>original: "Est res incorporea omni decore adornata, Sanctæ Trinitati assimilata, aeterna gloria coequata"</note> Some describe it this way: *It is an intellectual Spirit, always living, always in motion, and according to its various duties and operations, it is called by different names. It is called **life** while it grows and animates; **spirit** while it contemplates; **sense** while it feels; **animus** <note>soul-mind</note> while it knows; **mens** <note>intellect</note> while it understands; **reason** while it discerns; **memory** while it remembers; and **will** when it desires. Yet all these are but one essence, differing only in their properties.* <note>original: "Est Spiritus intellectualis semper vivens, semper in motu... non sunt nisi una essentia sed proprietate diversa"</note> These latter descriptions are assigned to this vivifying <term>life-giving</term> Spirit as it interacts with the body.

Now, if we carefully examine all these descriptions of the essence and properties of this *Anima* <note>soul</note>—both in her freedom from the body and when she is enclosed within it—we shall find that they do not differ at all from the logic of my previous assertion. 

First, we observe that in its essential power, the soul is the offspring of the eternal emanation <term>a flowing out from a source</term> which came immediately from God to animate all things. Secondly, we see that it has for its substantial "vehicle" the thin, subtle, created spirit of the world. This makes it an *alterity* <term>a state of being "other" or composed of distinct parts</term>, or a composition of two things: the bright emanation from the eternal Fountain and the created spirit. 

Therefore, in the definitions mentioned above, the soul's interior is called:
1. A "Spiritual Substance" flowing from the divine Fountain; 
2. A "divine mind" (*mens divina*); 
3. The "Image or similitude of the divine Wisdom"; 
4. A "divine Light" after the Image of the Word; 
5. The "similitude of the Holy Trinity." 

Secondly, the soul participates in the "mundane spirit" <term>the spirit of the world</term>. For this reason, in the sixth and seventh definitions, it is called (regarding its substance) a "spirit that breathes in the body." It is the vehicle for the formal act of life, which is truly the divine mental beam. When considered in itself as the substantial and material spirit in its simple nature, it is that which shares in the created spirit of the world. The union of these two—the divine and the created—is called *anima* <note>soul</note>. Thus, the soul includes both the *mens* <note>divine mind</note> and the *spiritus* <note>created spirit</note>, or the divine and created natures joined into one, which fills, animates, and gives life to all things.

# Sect. 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

...according to the assertion of such Gentile and Ethnic <term>Ethnic: In this context, referring to non-Christian or pagan philosophers of antiquity.</term> Philosophers as I have cited before, which I will prove in no way disagrees or varies from the testimony of the holy Text. To make this plainer, I will compare them in order. 

First, I will begin my account with the Cabalists' <note>Cabalists: Followers of Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism that influenced many Renaissance thinkers.</note> great Angel, whom they call *Metatron* <note>original: "Mitattron"</note>. This name is interpreted as *the Gift of God* <note>original: "Donum Dei"</note>, which they say is the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> intellectual Agent from which all specific forms descend. <margin>1 Tim. 6:13.</margin> The Apostle Paul says *that the Lord gives life to all things.* And Solomon says *that the Spirit of Wisdom is the tree of life and the fountain, or beginning of life.* <margin>Prov. 3.</margin> If this Spirit is the fountain of life, then as the Son of Sirach says: *God poured it out upon all his works, and upon all flesh according to his gift.* <note>original: "effudit Deus illam supra omnia opera sua, & supra omnem carnem secundum datum suum"</note> 

And this was that universal angelic Spirit which God sent out as a spiritual Messenger from himself and out of himself, in the form of an emanation, to move upon the waters. <margin>Gen. 1.</margin> Its purpose was to shape and vivify them, giving life and being not only to the great world <note>The "great world" (macrocosm) refers to the universe as a whole.</note>, but also to every individual part of it. <margin>John 1, Eph. 4, Col. 3.</margin> This emanation was the Word of God, by whom all things were made and given life, because life was within it. I mean that *Christ who fills all things, who is all in all*, as the Apostle says, *who in the beginning made the earth, and the heavens were the work of his hands.* <margin>Heb. 1.</margin> After his creation of all things, he does (as St. Paul tells us) *sustain all things by the word of his power* <note>original: "portare omnia verbo virtutis suae"</note> through the life-giving virtue of this Word. 

David also confirms this: *By the Word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the breath of his mouth, all their power* <note>original: "Verbo Domini firmati sunt caeli, & Spiritu ab ore ejus omnis virtus eorum"</note>—namely, their life, preservation, and existence. <margin>Psalm 33:6.</margin> The Apostle therefore seems to conclude this: *God, needing nothing from anyone, gives life and breath and all things* <note>original: "Deus non aliquo indigens dat vitam & inspirationem & omnia"</note> to every creature. <margin>Acts 17.</margin>

Every Philosopher must acknowledge that the *Soul* <note>original: "Anima"</note> is nothing other than that which animates or gives life to a body or spirit. <margin>1 Cor. 12.</margin> Why then should not the universal divine Spirit—which fills all, operates all, and is in all—be termed the fountain of the world’s life? It is that by which the world lives, moves, and has its being, and consequently it is the essential life and the central or mental soul of the world. It moves the created "humid spirit" <note>A reference to the watery, primordial matter of creation.</note> of the world no differently than the spirit which God breathed into Adam moved and operated within the instrument of the created air. <margin>Wisdom of Solomon</margin> 

Should the eternal and life-giving Spirit of Wisdom—which is said to *fill all and be in everything*, and which has the nature of the universal and first-created Angel—be idle? (For the book of Ecclesiasticus says: *Wisdom was created before all things.*) <margin>Wisd. 12:1, Ecclus. 1.</margin> This Wisdom is, as it were, the universal soul of the world or the life of all things. It is the emanation of the brightness of the Almighty, the splendor of eternal Light, the pure mirror of the Majesty of God, and the Image of his goodness. <margin>Wisd. 7:22.</note> It is one, simple, subtle, permanent in itself, and the most piercing or movable of all things. 

All of these are properties assigned by St. Dionysius <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, a highly influential Christian theologian and philosopher.</note> to an Angel, and by the learned Fathers mentioned before to a separated soul. Shall this Spirit, I say, be in all things and fill the heavenly spirit of every world—meaning both the great world (the universe) and the little one (called Man)—and yet not operate? Shall it not act out the life-giving and multiplying effect of its nature, but instead be idle and empty within the creature? 

Did God send forth his operative Spirit to be still and not to act? Truly, the Father operates in it by His Will, and the Spirit carries out the Will of the Father in the creature’s spirit, which it possesses, animates, and guides in whatever way it pleases. For this reason, the Book of Judith says: *Let every creature serve God, because you spoke and they were made; you sent your spirit and they were created.* <note>original: "Deo serviat omnis creatura, quia dixisti, & facta sunt; misisti spiritum tuum, & creata sunt"</note> <margin>Judith 16.</margin> 

So the great world may say and confess, just as man does, that it was made after the Image of the Archetype (or God), and that *in him it lives, moves, and exists.* <margin>Acts 17.</margin> This matches what the Apostle said to man, who is the "little world" <note>The "little world" (microcosm) refers to the human being as a reflection of the entire universe.</note>. Thus you see that the Cabalists' *Metatron* or *Gift of God*, whom they make the universal intellectual Agent, is nothing other than that universal Spirit of Wisdom. God sent this Spirit out from his Throne (or as the Text says, even out of his own mouth) as the greatest gift and token of his kindness toward every world and its members. Its purpose is to lead them from deformity and non-existence into actual and formal being, endowing them with living features. It offers life and being to them explicitly, which before was only implicitly included and contained in the dark and gloomy shadow of death—I mean, out of the deformed Chaos into a beautiful shape; out of deadly sleep and dark rest...

# Book 1. Mosaical Philosophy

*When God withdraws his Spirit from his creatures, they die; but when he sends out his Spirit, they are recreated with life and goodness.* <note>original: "Deo recipiente Spiritum suum à creaturis, exspirant, emittente spiritum recreantur bona." <margin>1.</margin>
Damascene <note>John of Damascus (c. 675–749), a prominent monk and theologian.</note> seems to define it this way: *The soul is a spiritual substance flowing from the divine fountains; it is simple, indissolvable, immortal, free, incorporeal, and invisible, lacking quantity, shape, weight, and color.* <note>original: "Anima est substantia spiritualis à divinis fontibus emanans, simplex, indissolubilis, immortalis, libera, incorporea, & invisibilis; quantitate, figura, pondere, & colore carens."</note> Bernard <note>Saint Bernard of Clairvaux (1090–1153), a French abbot and mystic.</note> also seems to agree with this.

Some describe it this way: *It is an intellectual Spirit, always living and always in motion; according to the specific function of its work, it is called by various names.* <note>original: "Est Spiritus intellectualis semper vivens, semper in motu, & secundum sui operis officium variis nuncupatur nominibus." This section outlines the different "faculties" or parts of the soul.</note>
* It is called **life** while it animates growth;
* It is called **spirit** when it contemplates, being a spiritual substance that breathes in the body;
* It is called **sense** when it is employed in the act of feeling;
* It is termed **mind** (*animus*) when it operates in knowledge and wisdom;
* It is named **intellect** (*mens*) in regard to its divine understanding;
* It is called **reason** while it discerns;
* It is called **memory** as it remembers;
* And when it is inclined to desire anything, it is called **will** (*voluntas*).
Yet all these names describe only one *Anima* or Soul in essence, though they represent different properties or faculties. And these later descriptions are assigned to this life-giving Spirit as it interacts with the body.

Now, if we carefully examine all these descriptions of the essence and properties of this *Anima* (soul)—both in its freedom from the body and when it is enclosed within it—we shall find that they do not vary one bit from the tenor of my previous argument. For first, we shall observe that in its essential virtue, it is the offspring of the eternal emanation which came immediately from God for the animating <term>original: "inacting," meaning to put into action or give life to.</term> of all things. Second, we see that it has for its substantial vehicle the thin, subtle, created spirit of the world. This makes it a duality <note>original: "alteritatem," meaning "otherness" or a state of being composed of two distinct parts.</note> or a composition of two: namely, the bright emanation from the eternal Fountain, and the created vessel. 

Therefore, in the aforementioned definitions, the soul is called (in regard to its inner nature) a "spiritual substance flowing from the divine Fountain" in the first; a "divine mind" <note>original: "mens divina"</note> in the second; the "image or similitude of the divine Wisdom" in the third; a "divine Light after the Image of the Word, the substance of God whose character is the Word" in the fourth; and the "similitude of the Holy Trinity, equal to the divine Glory" in the fifth. 

Secondly, it participates in the worldly spirit <note>original: "mundane spirit"</note>. Therefore, it is termed by the sixth and seventh definitions (in regard to its substance) as a spirit that breathes in the body. It is the vehicle of the formal act, which is in truth the divine mental beam. When considered in itself as the substantial and material spirit in its simple nature, it is that which participates in the created spirit of the world. The union of these two is called *anima* (soul), so that *anima* includes both the divine mind and the created spirit in one, which fills, animates, and gives life to all things.

# Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy

According to the claims of those non-Christian <note>original: "Ethnick"</note> philosophers whom I have cited before—which I will prove do not differ or stray from the testimony of the Holy Scriptures—and to make this clearer, I will compare them in order. This emanation was the Word of God, <margin>John 1, Ephesians 4, Colossians 3</margin> by whom all things were made and given life, because life was within it. I mean that *Christ* who fills all things and is all in all, as the Apostle says: *who in the beginning made the earth, and the heavens were the work of his hands.* <margin>Hebrews 1</margin> After his creation of all things, he does (as Saint Paul tells us) *sustain all things by the life-giving power <note>original: "vivifying virtue"</note> of his Word.* <note>original: "portare omnia verbo virtutis suæ"</note>

# Mosaical Philosophy. Book 1.

...into a lively action and motion, moving out of obscurity into Light. Therefore, this was rightly termed in the eyes of wise men *Metatron* or the *universal Gift of God* <note>original: "Donum Dei catholicum"</note>, which transforms <note>original: "reduceth"</note> the universal Nothing into a universal Something.

But to better explain to you through a philosophical demonstration the angelic nature of this supreme intelligence called *Metatron*—and consequently the Soul of the World—I first want you to understand the true way philosophers demonstrate the harmony of the world and its spirit. The Platonic *Heptachord* <note>A seven-toned scale. In Plato’s *Timaeus*, these numbers (1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 27) represent the proportions used to create the Soul of the World.</note>, which Plato invented and adapted to demonstrate the Soul of the World, consisted of seven strings or proportions—some even and some odd—namely 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, and 27. Although Porphyry and Proclus drew these proportions in a single line, it seems to me that Adrastus and Calcidius expressed them more fittingly by adapting them to the sides of a pyramid or triangle in this manner:

<image-desc>A triangular diagram representing the "Heptachord" of the soul of the world. At the apex is the number "1". The left leg of the triangle descends with the numbers "2", "4", and "8". The right leg descends with the numbers "3", "9", and "27". Along the left side is the diagonal text "Material proportion in the kingdom of darkness" <note>original: "Proportio materialis in regno tenebroso."</note> and along the right side is the diagonal text "Formal proportion in the kingdom of light" <note>original: "Proportio formalis in regno lucido."</note>. Horizontal lines connect the corresponding even and odd numbers across the legs. Below the base of the triangle is the caption "In Creation."</image-desc>

->In Creation<-

At the summit or top, where both lines meet in one point, the figure **1** represents Unity. Because this Unity participates in material existence on one side and has a connection <note>original: "commerce"</note> with formal emanation on the other, it is clear that this point—the Unity from which both different lines or streams flow—is the fountain of both matter and form. Therefore, it is the opinion of Synesius <note>A 4th-century philosopher-bishop.</note> and other theosophers (which does not disagree with Holy Scripture) that *God is everything that exists; since from him, through him, and in him are all things. He is male and female, or, as Hermes Trismegistus says, most fertile in both sexes; he is power and action, form and matter. Indeed, there is nothing that he is not.* <note>original: "Deus sit omne quod est; quippe á quo, per quem, & in quo sunt omnia. Quod sit mas & fæmina, vel, ut Mercurius Trismegistus ait, utriusque sexûs fœcundissimus; quod sit potentia, & actus, quod sit forma & quod sit materia. Imo vere nihil est quod ipse non existit:"</note>

God (they say) is everything that exists, because all things are from him, by him, and in him. He is male and female (as Synesius says), or as Hermes Trismegistus <note>original: "Mercurius Trismegistus"</note> would have it, He is most abundant in each sex. He is power <note>original: "puissance"</note> and act, and finally, he is form and matter. Truly, they conclude that there is nothing which he is not. None of this seems to differ from Holy Scripture, which says that *God is all, and in all*, and above all, and that in him all things are contained, and in his Spirit and Word all things consist, etc. The six other figures correspond to one another from the material side to the formal side. Specifically, the even numbers directly relate to the odd numbers: the material number 2 relates to the formal 3; the 4 relates to the 9; and the 8 relates to the 27. These numbers most vividly express the general kinds of all creatures and their harmony.

### Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

...harmony. In the first place, it describes the symphonic levels <note>original: "Symphoniacall Degrees"</note> of the Soul of the World, as will be explained later. For first, following the example of the Archetype <note>The original perfect model or "Idea" of the world in the mind of God.</note>, the number 2 issued from 1. This number 2 is termed by the Pythagoreans the "confusion of units," and therefore it is the fundamental <note>original: "radicall"</note> or beginning imperfect number. Because of its confusedness and imperfection, it stands in the same relation to the Unity from which it sprang as the dark Chaos does to the bright, eternal Unity. This Chaos is a **raw and confused mass** <note>original Latin: *rudis indigestaque moles*</note>.

It is rightly termed "imperfect" because the eternal emanation, which is all perfection, had not yet made it perfect. For this reason, the watery matter that issued out of it is inherently imperfect, just as the number 2 is considered imperfect compared to the number 3. This is because all perfection consists of three terms: a beginning, a middle, and an end. If you take one of the units of 2 for the beginning and the other for the middle, then it lacks an end. If you put one unit for the beginning and another for the end, then you have two extremes but no middle ground <note>original: "mean"</note>; therefore, it is also imperfect this way. Or, if you place one unit for a middle and the other for an end, you still have imperfection because it lacks a beginning.

In the same way, if the Unity had not emitted its actual emanation as a bright Unity of life, the number 2—representing the deformed matter of the Chaos—would have remained in its dual, confused, or imperfect state. That is, it would exist without the form or shape of any perfect thing; I mean it would be a plain **Nothing** <note>original Latin: *Nihil*</note> or **Something in potential and not in act** <note>original Latin: *Aliquid in potentia & non actu*</note>.

So, I say that before matter was informed by the Unity of Light (which makes the third Unity), it was **Empty and void** <note>original Latin: *Vacuum & inane*</note>. It was a vacuity because it lacked the presence of the informing Unity—the actual emanation—which provides the title of "goodness." After the bright emanation was made, then emptiness was changed into fullness <note>original: "plenitude"</note>; potential into action; darkness into light; and deformed matter into well-formed and living <note>original: "vivified"</note> waters. In a word, imperfection was changed into perfection. Thereupon it was said that "God saw that it was good"—meaning it was replenished with His virtuous Essence, which was entirely good and only goodness.

By this reasoning—namely, the addition of the "formal Unity" to the state of confusion and imperfection (the "material duality" which symbolizes the Chaos, the mother of matter)—perfection is brought into the world. By animating the purest and subtlest waters, this perfection unites the mental Light with the heavenly Spirit in an Angelic essence, which afterwards animates and gives form to all things. This formal union is symbolically expressed by the figure 3, which for this reason is termed the first number of perfection, the number of the Soul, or the fundamental number of "form" in the course of nature.

From this point forward, the Platonists and Pythagoreans express matter (which is imperfect in itself) by even or "imperfect" numbers. In the Archetypal world (represented by the numbers 1, 2, and 3 in the form of the sacred Trinity), there appear to be three ideal dimensions in one divine nature or eternal essence. These present themselves in their progression as a **Root**, a **Square**, and a **Cube**. These terms signify a supreme soul, a spirit, and a body of the world, ideally mapped out in the Archetype. These three seem to be raised out of the number 1 or Unity. (For multiplying 1 by the root 1 produces 1 and itself, which makes 2 or a simple ideal square; and multiplying it again by 1, there rises only 2 and 1, which make 3 or a Cube). This argues for the perfection of the Ideal world which was in God.

If we take the two fundamental compounded numbers as roots, we shall produce the created or "exemplar" world according to this pattern. Namely, we shall find three dimensions—longitude, latitude, and depth <note>original: "profundity"</note>—within matter by searching for its Root, Square, and Cube. The root of matter, therefore, was 2. Even though the supreme Unity had multiplied or dilated itself into 2 (representing its first-born issue), all was dark **relative to us** <note>original Latin: *quoad nos*</note> because the holy Spirit of Illumination had not yet shone forth.

We must imagine that the multiplication of matter in the world is nothing but the variety of penetration of formal light into the watery abyss or material multitude. The thicker the matter is, the nearer it appears to its root (the number 2 or the dark Chaos). Conversely, the thinner and more transparent it is made by the rich presence of the formal emanation's bright presence, the nearer it appears to the root of the formal Unity. Once this mystery is rightly understood, all science—even in the most hidden <note>original: "abstrufest"</note> Philosophy—may easily be decoded. The root of matter, which is 2, represents the dark Chaos; the root of form, which is 3, signifies that the root 2 (the dark waters) is animated by the formal or bright emanati...

### Mosaicall Philosophy. Book 1.

...duality <note>The text continues from the previous page's discussion of the number 2.</note> of Unity or 1, and so the first duality <note>original: "2."</note> was accomplished, and the soul of the world was created, namely by the Angelic emanation. *Christ is the Image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation, in whom all things in heaven and earth, visible and invisible, were brought forth, whether they be Thrones, or Dominations, or Powers; all were made by him and in him, and he was before anything, and all consist in him.* <note>original Latin: "Christus est Imago Dei invisibilis, Primogenitus omnis creaturæ, in quo edita sunt universa in cælis & in terra visibilia, & invisibilia, sive Throni, sive Dominationes, sive Potestates, omnia per ipsum, & in ipso omnia sunt, & ipse ante omnes, & omnia in ipso constant."</note> Look here: the true vivifying Spirit is evidently described, which not only made all, and is all that he has made (since all are in him), doing the will of his Father in all that he has made. The Hebrew Rabbis call him *Metatron*, or the *Gift of God* <note>original Latin: "Donum Dei"</note>, and the Prophet calls him the *Angel of the Great Counsel*:
<margin>Isaiah 6</margin>
*And his name shall be called, the Angel of the Great Counsel* <note>original Latin: "Et vocabitur nomen ejus... magni concilii Angelus"</note>, etc. Thus, by multiplying 3 by itself, we have the created **formal square** <note>The number 9, representing the 3x3 structure of the angelic hierarchy.</note>, which signifies the nine Orders of the Angels. These vary according to the multiplicity of their properties, by which the outpouring <note>original: "effluxion"</note> or emanation sent out from this infinite fountain of light operates diversely in the world, according to the will of the Father of Lights who sent it forth. 

And the formal square of 9, being joined with the material square of 4 <note>The number 4, or 2x2, representing the material world.</note>, animates the heavens, which by thickening <note>original: "inspissation"</note> or multiplication are made physical or cubic. Thus, all bodies are made of those thin substances by multiplying each square by its root. Consequently, the **cubic form** <note>The volume or "solid" state of a number.</note> of the spirit will be 27 <note>3x3x3</note>, and that of matter will be 8 <note>2x2x2</note>, which represent every element-based or compound matter. Just as the more matter is multiplied in itself, the darker and thicker it will be, so the more that light is multiplied in it, the lighter, thinner, and more spiritual the creature will be. 

This means that the formal root, square, and cube signify the essence and souls of creatures—whether they are super-celestial, celestial, or elemental—which are more or less dignified with "form." For according to these multiplications in form, the creatures will be more exalted in excellence. You see now how far, and by what proportions (both spiritual and material), the Platonic harmony of the world extends itself. You may observe that where this harmonious proportion between form and matter is absent, there must necessarily be both spiritual and physical dissension, or discord, and consequently antipathy. 

We see also that the root of life is fixed in the angelic composition, which consists of simple, light, and pure spiritual matter. Thus, the eternal wisdom <note>original: "sapience"</note>, or essential soul, is the driving force <note>original: "act"</note> of the Angels; the eternal <note>original: "ævial"</note> angelic spirit is the driving force or essential life of the stars, or heavenly influence; and the starry influence is the soul and life of the winds. The spiritual emanation from the winds informs the universal sublunary element, or "lower waters," in a fourfold way; the element animates the weather patterns <note>original: "meteorological impressions"</note>, and from these, the compound creatures are formed. These creatures draw from the divine fountain of them all, being one spirit in essence, but multiform because of the variety of organs through which it works variously in the world. 

So it appears that God immediately animated the **Empyrean heaven** <note>The highest heaven, believed to be the realm of pure fire and light.</note>, or the intellectual spirit, which is the seat of Angels, and this we compare to the "root." The Empyrean heaven animates the stars, or the ethereal region, which we refer to as the "square." And the starry heaven is, as it were, the male—the multiplier and giver of life—to the elementary region and its creatures, which we compare to the "cube." 

Truly, not only the mysterious Cabalists but also the deepest Philosophers have left an everlasting memory of this perfect and formal root, or **ternary number** <note>The number 3.</note>, with its triple dimension. I do not mean the number used for trade, or the kind that common mathematicians use in their basic arithmetic <note>original: "Algorism"</note>, but as it is a spiritual and essential character of numbering, proceeding from a certain circular revolution and square and cubic multiplication. Therefore, the Learned have founded their formal and mystical **Arithmetic** and **Geometry** on this subject. These are not practiced upon common and vulgar subjects, but are wholly employed in the profound meditations of the true *Cabala*, natural **Magic**, and essential **Alchemy**. ### Section 2. Mosaic Philosophy.

These are otherwise termed by mystics as the sciences of the **Elementary**, **Celestial**, and **Super-celestial** <note>original: "Supermundane"</note> realms. These names are used because the study deals with separate spiritual intelligences and substances (as some call them), and because it is the most worthy of all subjects to be understood, as it is focused on the knowledge of the Creator. The greatest perfection in which a human being can glory is attaining the true knowledge of God. The Prophet testifies to this in these words: <margin>Jeremiah 9.</margin> *“Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, nor the strong man in his strength, nor the rich man in his riches; but let him who will glory, boast and glory in this: that he knows and understands me.”*

Indeed, these are the three mystical sciences that wise men assign to the knowledge of the three worlds: the Intelligible <note>The realm of pure spirit and angels</note>, the Celestial <note>The realm of the stars and planets</note>, and the Elementary <note>The physical world of the four elements</note>. According to the Cabalists, these are represented by the three letters of the name <term>Adam</term> <note>original Hebrew: אדם</note>. They also correspond to the three parts of man—often called the "little world" <note>Microcosm</note>—which are the Intellect, the Soul, and the Body (which is subject to change and corruption, just like the elementary physical world).

Building upon this foundation, the Rabbi *Zoar* <note>Likely referring to the author of the *Zohar*, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note> said that there are three things that correspond to one another in this triple dimension. They are framed after the pattern of the Archetype and the original Idea: namely, the Tabernacle that *Moses* erected, the Temple of *Solomon*, and the human body. These follow three types of numbers applied to them: 
1. The **vocal** or **operative**, which is derived from the measurements of the physical <note>elementary</note> world.
2. The **formal**, which is derived from the celestial world.
3. The **rational** or **divine**, which is extracted from the intellectual world.

I will make all of this clear by describing the Tabernacle. This Tabernacle symbolized the three worlds in its various parts. The first part of it was uncovered and exposed to the wind, rain, hail, snow, and all other weather effects <note>original: "impressions"</note> that are created in the world below the moon <note>sublunary</note> with its perpetual changes. Both common people and animals resorted to this part in a continuous cycle of life and death, because of the constant sacrifices that were killed and offered there. 

Therefore, this region—representing the solid foundation <note>original: "cube"</note> of matter—is rightly associated with the physical world, which is composed of dense waters as an unstable and fluid substance. For this reason, it is properly called the "world of darkness." This is why the Evangelist in one place calls the devil the "Prince of darkness," and in another, the "Prince of this world." This region also corresponds to the human body.

The second part of the Tabernacle, which was plated with gold and illuminated by a candlestick of seven lights, represents the starry heaven and its seven wandering lights, or planets. This heaven sits in the middle between two extremes: the bright fountain of the spiritual <note>formal or empyreal</note> heaven and the dark abyss of matter in the physical world. Thus, it participates in both extremes: fire and water. 

For this reason, the Hebrews call heaven *Shamayim* <note>original: שמים</note>, which is made of *esh* <note>original: אש</note> meaning "fire," and *maym* <note>original: מים</note> meaning "water." In Greek, it is called *Aether*, which means "as if it were fiery air" <note>original Latin: *quasi igneus aer*</note>. Its watery matter is incorruptible because its needs are so satisfied by the flow of heavenly nectar from above that it desires no change. Regarding its activity and motion, it receives it from that eternal flow <note>emanation</note> which *Solomon* says in <margin>Wisdom 7.</margin> is the most movable of all things. In truth, it is the first universal mover <note>original: "catholick mover"</note>, who is said to preside over the "first moved" sphere <note>original Latin: *primum mobile*</note>. By his action, all the lesser celestial spirits <note>intelligences</note> move their rolling and twinkling stars <note>fires</note>, just as many external wheels move and receive life from the motion of a central wheel.

Thus we may see, first, why this region of the world is called Heaven, or the sphere of equality—namely, because it is a balanced mixture of form and matter. We also see why it is called the sphere of the "world-soul": it is composed of the pure spirit of the waters (which is feminine and passive) and the bright fire or action of eternity. The divine Mind acts through this watery nature as its vehicle, showing its life-giving properties through this spiritual organ. Therefore, all life consists of "essential heat and radical moisture" <note>original Latin: *ex calido essentiali, & humido radicali*</note>; essential heat is the masculine or active principle, and radical moisture is the feminine or passive principle. This region refers to the vital soul in man and relates to the mathematical "square" of both form and matter, which sits in the middle between the "cube" (body) and the "root" (spirit).

This heaven relates to the intellect in man, which the Hebrews call *Neshama* <note>original: "Neffaniah"; likely a transcription of the Hebrew term for the highest level of the soul</note>, the Greeks call *Nous*, and the Latins call *Mens* (the mental beam), which holds dominion in the human soul. 

So we may discern that in the "Great World" <note>The Macrocosm or universe</note>, the angelic heaven, being the most formal and fiery, is essentially the soul of the ethereal heaven; for through it and from it, this region receives its life, motion, and being. By the same proportion, the celestial or ethereal heaven is the soul or active agent of the elementary region. For by means of the Sun, Moon, and Stars—which dart down their beams and influences upon the earth like arrows against a target—the earth, water, and all things within them act, live, generate, and multiply. Thus, the heavens are esteemed by all philosophers to be the Male, and the earth and other elements to be the Female. Between these two, all generations are made in and upon the earth and in the sea; for the earthly body cannot operate without a heavenly touch. Indeed, even man himself requires the heavenly act and aid for his generation. Therefore, **Aristotle** concluded that *sol & homo generat hominem*—**the sun and man produce a man.** Again, all philosophers generally agree on this: namely, that *superiora agunt in inferiora, more maris in foeminam*—**superior bodies act upon inferior ones, in the manner of a male upon a female.** And the maxim of all such **Cabalists** <note>Practitioners of Kabbalah, a form of Jewish mysticism</note> who are well-versed in mystical theology, asserts that:

<margin>Johann Reuchlin, *On the Art of the Kabbalah*, Book 3</margin>

*Omnes res inferiores sunt representativæ superiorum; & sicut fit inferius, sic agitur superius*—**All inferior things represent or are images of the superior ones; and as it is below, so it is acted upon above.** In truth, a notable person well-versed in this hidden learning asserts that the eternal <note>original: "æviall"</note> or angelic heaven is framed after the pattern of the eternal and ideal world. The temporal elementary heaven or region is the image of the celestial or ethereal one. Thus, the images and actions of the darker world have their ideal shapes in and from the lighter, starry world; the starry world’s shapes and actions were first outlined in the intellectual or angelic world; and these, in turn, proceed originally from the radical pattern without beginning in the **Archetype** <note>The original model in the mind of God</note>.

I conclude, therefore, that both Theology and mystical Philosophy agree that God is well pleased with the holy **ternary** <note>The number three</note>, which is the first odd number in arithmetic progression. We Christians honor a Trinity of Persons in one Deity, and **Aristotle** says that we are instructed by a natural kind of instinct or habit to honor God by the number three. In this, he speaks only reason, since in the ideal world there were three properties extracted out of one unity, and the real world was afterward made after that example. Thus, the Trinity in Divinity was the root of all the world's formal composition. For by the root 3, the intellectual or angelic world was defined; by the square 9, the celestial world; and by the cube 27, the elementary world, as we may gather from Platonic learning. 

But as for the Kabbalistic Rabbis, they consider the quantitative proportions of this Ternary in another way. Just as the cube of three consists of three nines <note>3x9=27</note>, they take these three nines and arrange them in this triple position: **999**, which makes nine hundred ninety-nine. According to the rule of **Algorism** <note>The system of Arabic numerals and place-value arithmetic</note>, the first 9 toward the right hand is a simple digit; because of its simplicity and essential nature, it is attributed to the nine orders of **Angels** belonging to the intelligible world. The middle 9, representing tens, partakes on one hand of form or simplicity and on the other hand of matter; therefore, they allot it to the nine orbits or spheres of the starry heaven. The third 9, in the place of hundreds, represents a deeper and more material composition belonging to the elementary world. All of these finally terminate in **Man**, who acts as a passage (represented by the figure of unity) from them to celestial things, and from there to the intellectual. 

To conclude, **Unity**—in which the philosopher **Leucippus** placed sovereign good and happiness—when added to the three nines <note>original: "novenaries"</note>, makes a complete thousand. This is the cube of ten and the end of all numbers according to the Hebrew calculation. Also, the square of 3 (which is 9), by the addition of ***Aleph*** (which is 1), produces a **Denary** <note>A group of ten</note>, or the number 10, beyond which (as **Aristotle** asserts) no man has ever found any number. Following the aforementioned pattern or image, the ancient Law divided the fruits and goods proceeding from the earth, ordaining the hundredth number as being more material and coarse...

### Section 2. Mosaic Philosophy.

It is rightly termed the Idea or image of a **unison**: and just as the **unison**, like one essence in Divinity, encompasses three Persons (representing the three accords in the **Archetypal** <note>original: "Archetypicall"; the original or divine model</note> harmony), so also the **Diapason** <note>original: "Diapason"; a musical octave</note> comprises the two other accords besides itself: namely, the **Diapente** <note>original: "Diapente"; a musical fifth</note> and the **Diatessaron** <note>original: "Diatessaron"; a musical fourth</note>. Now, I prove that this most perfect consonant, the **Diapason**, is planted in the midst of a **unison** and produces within itself two perfect chords or octaves contained within it, in this way: Take a Lute or **Bandora** <note>original: "Bandora"; a 16th-century stringed instrument similar to a cittern</note> and strike any of the strings open; then press that same string down exactly in its middle, and each half will sound a **Diapason** relative to that open **unison**. Thus, the **unison** made by striking the whole open string will be divided into two **Diapasons**, which are the most perfect consonants to the whole. This is a clear argument that the perfection of the **Diapason** resides in the "seat of the Sun." Consequently, the formal and living harmony of the entire world exists in that central or middle place, just as the heart, which is the seat of life, is located in a human being. And yet, by the rays of the Sun, this life of the world is made universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> and fills everything, just as the vital blood spreads itself universally throughout the **Microcosm** <note>original: "Microcosm"; the 'little world' of the human body</note> through the channels of the arteries.

But I fear I have pursued this point too far to prove and support the existence of the soul of this world. Therefore, I will leave it to come directly to the point, since in the fourth book of my *Mosaic Philosophy*, I have fully proved and maintained that the translation by **Jerome** <note>original: "Jerom"; referring to Saint Jerome's Latin Vulgate translation of Psalm 19:4</note> is correct: namely, *He set his tabernacle in the sun* <note>original: "Posuit tabernaculum suum in sole"</note>. I will proceed, therefore, to the second opinion of the Philosophers.

<margin>Wisdom 7</margin>
The ancient philosophers **Democritus**, **Orpheus**, and the followers of **Pythagoras** believe that all things are full of gods; and again, they refer all these gods to one **Jupiter**. By "gods," they mean the divine virtues infused into things, which **Zoroaster** called *divine attractors* <note>original: "divinos illices"</note> and **Bishop Synesius** called *symbolic charms* <note>original: "Symbolicas illecebras"</note>. Others term them "lines," and others "fortresses," upon which the virtue of things depends. They do not err much in this saying, except in appearing to divide the Godhead into various gods. But they seem to justify themselves for that error by saying that all those gods relate back to one **Jupiter**; and so, by that word "relation," they preserve the continuity and indivisibility of the Soul. They agree, therefore, with the Scriptures, in that their meaning is that this divine essence is in all things. For as the Scriptures acknowledge, the universal Spirit of **Wisdom** is one simple Spirit, and yet it is termed by **Solomon** as *multiple* or *manifold* <note>original: "multiplex"</note> in respect to its many actions or properties in the creatures it animates. For it is said to
<margin>
Wisdom 1.
Wisdom 12.
Wisdom 7.
</margin>
fill the universe, and the incorruptible Spirit of God is in all things, giving life and motion to all. This is because it is *more mobile and spirited than anything else* <note>original: "omni re mobilior"</note>; and being only one thing, it is able to do all things. It remains permanent in itself and therefore animates everything, since it is in all and everywhere. For this reason, the poets also say: *All things are full of Jove* <note>original: "Omnia Jovis plena"</note>. That is to say, the essential rays of this Eternal **Jupiter** or **JEHOVAH** are in every specific place of the world, making things live and exist through different properties. And for this reason, they conclude that *all things are full of gods* <note>original: "omnia diis plena"</note>, as was said. I come to the third opinion.

<margin>Wisdom 12:1</margin>
The **Platonists**, and all those philosophers who agree with them, differ in nothing from **Orpheus**, **Democritus**, and the rest, except that the Platonists call "the Soul of the world" what the others call **Jupiter**. The "gods" who possess all things they name as individual souls or mental beams, which depend on and have a continuous relation to the **World Soul** <note>original: "Anima mundi"</note>—just as the *incorruptible Spirit of the Lord that fills each individual part is not separated from that watery fountain which fills the universe*.

It is evident, therefore, by what has already been said, that all the following opinions of the philosophers regarding the **World Soul** can be fully confirmed and supported by these same reasons; therefore, I will say no more regarding this point at this moment.

I conclude, therefore, that since the Soul of the world has as its internal act the bright emanation of the eternal **Unity**, and the subtle universal created Spirit as its watery **vehicle** <note>original: "Vehicle"; a medium</note> or material **organ** (which is its external part), in which and by which it operates in and over everything, we must acknowledge that there is a kind of opposition <note>original: "contrariety"</note> in the very universal Soul itself. Otherwise, action and passion <note>term: 'Passion' here refers to the state of being acted upon by an external force.</note> would not exist in the created Soul—which is so called because it is made of "otherness" <note>original: "alterity"</note>, meaning it is made of two: namely, a created passive part, which is an offspring of the dark **Chaos**...

### CHAPTER V.

->*How all particular souls are said to spring forth or proceed, and then afterward to be preserved and multiplied by this general* Anima mundi <note>original: "Anima mundi"; the Soul of the World</note>, *or Soul of the world: and first, beginning with the soul of the most noble being, which is the little world or Man.*<-

<margin>Pimander, Book 1</margin> Hermes (also called *Mercurius Trismegistus* for another reason) rightly said that the world was made in the likeness or pattern of God. Therefore, just as one is called the *Archetype* <note>original: "Archetypus"; the original divine model</note>, the other is said to be the *Type* <note>original: "Typus"; the reflection or symbol</note>. For <margin>Pimander, Book 8</margin> this reason, he says in another place: "I know that the world is from God and in God, and that man is of the world and in the world; but God is the beginning and the comprehension of all things." <note>original Latin: "Scio mundum à Deo, atque in Deo, hominem vero à mundo & in mundo consistere, principium autem comprehensióne omnium Deus"</note> 

<margin>Pimander, Book 9</margin> And again, he speaks elsewhere in general terms: "God is the Father of the world, the world is the father of those things within the world, and the world is the offspring of God. It is rightly called *Cosmos* <note>original: "Cosmus"</note> because it adorns every kind of generation with truth, as well as with a never-ceasing operation of life and a perpetual speed of necessity in the mixing of the elements, which are brought forth in order. Whatever the Cosmos received from its very origin, it preserves through God forever." <note>original Latin: "Deus est Cosmi Pater, cosmus vero eorum, quæ in Cosmo; & cosmus quidem Dei filius, & jure Cosmus appellatus est, qui omnia veritate generationis exornat, necnon indefinenti vitæ operatione, perpetua necessitatis celeritate elementorum commistione ordine genitorum. Cosmus quacunque ab ipsa origine suscepit, a Deo perpetuo servat"</note>

In all this, he does not vary from the Scriptures. For in the beginning, God is said to have made the world from matter without form and to have adorned its watery <note>original: "humid"</note> nature or the heavens with his life-giving Spirit, which fills and operates in all things (as I have told you before). From the breath of that same Spirit of life, all creatures in the world are animated, and they receive their matter from the substantial elements in the world. 

Just as God, by pouring out his bright, life-giving, and all-acting Spirit, made the watery and passive nature of the world function—and that animated Spirit which is mixed entirely and in every part <note>original Latin: "secundum totum & in qualibet ejus parte"</note> with its uncreated animator is rightly called the Soul of the whole Universe—so we should have no doubt that every particular soul in this vaulted machine of the world depends on, and is produced, preserved, and multiplied from, that universal soul. For it is an infallible principle among philosophers that the whole contains every part, and every individual part derives its existence and being from the whole. 

But the world's universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> material spirit is activated and preserved by the universal Eternal Spirit, sent out from the Fountain of Life to activate and give life to all things. This uncreated Spirit of life is indivisible in essence. Therefore, just as it actually sends down or breathes forth the influences of life from its immense fountain—like an infinite number of beams from one Sun to an infinite variety of creatures, to give them form and life—so those beams of life are no less continuous and indivisible from that spiritual and indivisible Sun of life than visible beams are from the visible Sun. Nor was it enough for Adam to have been endowed with a "little world" <note>original: "Microcosmicall"</note> body—namely, a mass of earth...

Since God created and gave life to the watery Spirit of the world by adding his creating Spirit of life to it, that Spirit of life (which is one in essence with the Father), being sent into the world and filling the Spirit of the world, does vivify, multiply, and preserve not only man, but also every other animal, vegetable, and mineral in the world. This being the first point to be considered, I proceed as follows:

The variety of the species upon the earth radically proceeded from the very act of creation, when the word *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "Let it be done"</note> was spoken. Immediately, the will of the speaker was accomplished by his Son, who was sent into the world by way of emanation to do the will of his Father. And there are some who do not hesitate to say that all the species or kinds of creatures were expressed in and by the 22 Hebrew letters—not those external ones that are commonly painted with ink or art, which are but shadows, but the fiery, formal, and bright spiritual letters. These were engraved on the face or surface of the dark <term>Hyle</term> <note>original: "Hyle"; a Greek term for primordial matter or the substance of the universe</note> by the fiery word of the eternal Speaker in the beginning. Therefore, they are originally termed *Elementa quasi Hylementa* <note>original: "Elementa quasi Hylementa"; Latin meaning "Elements, as if they were Hyle-ments," or elements derived from matter</note>, or Elements, as they were engraved on the forehead of the dark abyss or Hyle. Because of the essence of that divine Word—which received the mystery of the typical creation, followed the archetypal pattern, and outlined it in characters of formal fire—the language framed from it was called *Lingua Sancta* <note>original: "Lingua Sancta"; Latin for "Holy Language," referring to Hebrew</note>. This is a language much spoken of by the learned Rabbis of our age but little known or understood by them; yet it is of infinite importance for the true explanation of sacred mysteries as well as all true <term>Cabalistical</term> <note>referring to Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism</note> secrets. 

But to proceed: each species or kind was framed according to the tenor of the divine Word and his formal characters, the effects of which passed unalterably into the world. Furthermore, every individual of each kind was made different and distinct from others in shape and proportion, as well as in condition and property. Now, as I said, this Spirit of the Lord carried out the will of his Father by creating everything differently, while being in itself only one and the same essence. So also did it, and does still, continue and keep every one of these species or kinds through multiplication or generation in their successive states. It preserves every individual during the time of its existence, by both an elementary and an ethereal kind of nourishment, which descends from heaven according to its spirituality to nourish the spirits of each individual according to its kind. 

For you must understand that just as the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> soul of the world is general to all, the air is made the chest or closet of its golden treasury of spiritual food. It swims hidden like a golden vapor, showered down from heaven into the air, filling and replenishing everything. While it is still in the open air, it is just as capable of sustaining and multiplying the life of a serpent, a sheep, a fish, or a bird, an oak, a herb, or the like, as it is of a man. As soon as the magnetic power or virtue of the creature—which causes a refreshment <note>original: "refection"</note> from this heavenly nectar every minute—has drawn in a portion of this universal spirit or nature, it leaves its universal or general nature and works specifically. That is to say, it works according to the individual nature of the kind that receives it. It converts itself into the nature of a dog if it is in a dog; in a whale, it becomes its nature; in a man, his; in an oak or myrtle, its; in wheat, it becomes the proper nature of wheat, and so in all other kinds. Consequently, it is the cause that every creature's spirit is nourished and sustained in itself. For this was the Creator's ordinance: that by whatever spirit the creature was first created in its kind, by that same spirit it should be maintained, preserved, and multiplied. Hence, the Philosopher breaks forth into this speech: *Est in aëre occultus vitæ cibus* <note>original: "Est in aëre occultus vitæ cibus"; Latin for "There is in the air a hidden food of life"</note>.

By this, he means that quintessential food which we receive from the general Spirit of life in the world, which by the appointment of God hangs ready in every part of the air to serve as the spiritual food of life for every elementary creature. Therefore, the Text says: <margin>Acts 17:25, John 10:12, Psalm 30:6</margin> *Deus dat vitam & inspirationem & omnia* <note>original: "Deus dat vitam & inspirationem & omnia"; Latin for "God gives life, and breath, and all things"</note>. And for this reason it was said, *And He saw that all things He created were good;* <note>original: "Et vidit quod omnia quæ creavit essent bona"</note> that is to say, they were not **void or empty**, but full of God’s essential being, which is God alone. Since, therefore, the never-dying fire of life is within the living creature, it is necessary for its preservation and growth that it be nourished by its like in the air every moment—or by the vehicle of the air—lest it should vanish and the creature perish.

This is because the form cannot be inhaled except by means of its airy vehicle; and by this very means, the quantity of the airy substance, as well as the quality of its form, is increased, which causes both growth and multiplication. Because of its growth and multiplication in substance, it is an easy matter to guess the manner of development and growth, and also the quantitative multiplication through reproduction in animals. We must therefore imagine that the air which is drawn into our heart by breathing is full of that divine treasure of life. Furthermore, we may gather that the heart is the precious storehouse of the active treasure of life from this speech of Solomon: <margin>Proverbs 4:23</margin> *Guard your heart with the best diligence and keep it carefully, seeing that from it proceed all the actions of life* <note>original Latin: "Cor tuum custodi supra omnem observationem, quia ab eo procedunt actiones vitæ"</note>. The nature and instruments by which the Spirit magnetically attracts—and then expels after attraction—that part of the moist vehicle of air which is useless and superfluous, is explained here:

Since without the sparks of life and generation that swim in the air, no creature (among which we consider Man to be the chief) can live for even a moment, it is most necessary that they should be drawn and sucked in by the creature every minute. Therefore, this three-leaved gate is fashioned in such a way that it opens inward and closes outward, so that what enters the Great Artery cannot return. Similarly, at the mouth of the pulmonary vein <note>original: "venal artery," an archaic term for the vessel carrying oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart</note>, there is a double gate composed of two valves <note>the mitral valve</note> that open outward and shut inward. # Section 2. Mosaic Philosophy.

...spirit, and you shall live. And the prophet said according as God commanded him,

From this way of speaking, we may gather first that it was the divine power <note>original: "vertue"</note> which shaped the external man before it had a living spirit; and then afterward, the spirit of life was breathed into the external man from the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> spirit of life in the great world; for he said, 
> Come O spirit from the four winds.

Furthermore, the world has a universal spirit by which it lives; for the four winds received their breath and life from this one spirit. Through this spirit, the universal sublunary element <note>The region below the moon, consisting of the four elements: earth, water, air, and fire</note> appears to live and is changed from one temperament <note>original: "complexion"</note> to another, producing a wide variety of effects in the complex creatures of this lower region of the world. Experience teaches us that the common air is of an earthy nature when the North wind blows, and of a choleric <note>Associated with heat and dryness in the system of the four humors</note> nature when the East wind dominates, and so on.

Regarding how a specific individual is shaped, one might ask why this universal life-giving spirit of the world—being only one—brings forth every fruit or birth according to its kind, rather than making them all the same. As I mentioned before, every specific creature was fundamentally <note>original: "radically"</note> created in its own kind, distinct and different from others according to the Creator's will. It was maintained and multiplied by the same spirit, always keeping the shape of the species or kind allotted to it at its creation. It seems that God appointed a certain secret mold to shape the potential creature before it became active. 

To understand this better, we must know that there are four seed-preparing <note>original: "spermatick"</note> vessels—two on each side. One is a venous vessel coming from the *vena cava* <note>The large vein carrying blood to the heart</note>; from here comes the bodily sperm, made of the refined matter of the body's four elements. This is the principle or root of the infant's external body; it is visible and is called *Sperma*. The other is an arterial vessel, the well-spring of the inward man, for it is the invisible fire of life called *Semen*. When these two are mixed, the *Semen* dwells centrally in the visible *Sperma*, just as the human soul dwells in the body. 

We should observe that since there are two vessels on each side—one spiritual and one elemental—as they descend toward the testicles, they form a wonderful and beautiful web or network <note>original: "plex"</note> through their subtle intertwining. The Greeks call this *Anastomosis* <note>A connection or opening between two things; here referring to the pampiniform plexus of the spermatic cord</note>. This embracing and secret weaving together of invisible parts is achieved by the skill of that great Builder [God]. This is not only (as anatomists believe) so that the red and bloody seed may be turned white, but first, so that it might separate the seed-substance in the venous vessels and the seminal substance in the arterial vessels from the blood mass—both the "natural" blood flowing from the liver and the "vital" blood springing from the heart. 

Secondly, it ensures that through this "Daedalian labyrinth" <note>A complex, maze-like structure, named after the mythical architect Daedalus</note>, the seminal form—which is the "heaven" of the microcosm <note>The human body viewed as a miniature version of the universe</note>—may be aptly mixed together according to the creature's true likeness. This is much like a form is spread through its elementary substance by a natural mixing. 

Undoubtedly, the structure of this network or *Anastomosis* acts like the impression of a notable seal: in a man, it is man-like; in a lion, it is like a lion; in an eagle, it takes the shape of an eagle. According to this hidden impression, which the imagination can scarcely perceive, the sperm is shaped like clay and moistened with its seminal nature like water. By the power of that divine spirit dwelling secretly within it, it becomes a living creature in the womb. These two natures are tempered together according to the law of this life-giving nature. The *semen*, or invisible spirit of the air, is agitated and moved by the divine nature within it (much as air is moved by the spirit of a person blowing into a flute), so that the visible bodily sperm is shaped into the image of its created species. This is similar to how we see a mole build its own house or dwelling under the earth. This is the work of the secret spirit after this compounded and well-mixed substance is cast into the womb.

In conclusion, everything we have spoken about regarding animals can also be easily applied to the plant <note>original: "vegetable"</note> kingdom. The entire plant or tree still lies hidden and folded up <note>original: "complicitly"</note> within the seed or kernel; by the same logic, it is unfolded <note>original: "explicitly"</note> and brought to light by the operation of the hidden and secret spirit...

The Author, having by diligent inquiry found out the essential root of Sympathy and Antipathy—as expressed in the first Book, where he proves it to be but one universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> simplicity in essence, though of a twofold property, quite opposite to one another in nature and condition, no differently than Willingness <note>original: "Volunty"</note> is to Unwillingness <note>original: "Nolunty"</note>—thought it not sufficient to gather evidence by circumstances and conclude *that it is so* <note>original Greek: ὅτι (*hoti*)</note>. Therefore, in this present Book, he attempts, with the tightest and highest stretched nerves of his understanding, to inquire and search out *the reason why* <note>original Greek: διότι (*dioti*)</note>: to wit, why, for what reason, and by what means this double act is spread <note>original: "disseminated"</note> throughout the Universe.

For this reason, he is content to be directed or guided into this difficult path of profound speculation by the light or North Star <note>original: "Pole-star"</note> of such sublime and purified <note>original: "rectified"</note> spirits—both Theological and Cabalistic <note>Referring to the Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism</note>—who have received the explanation <note>original: "enucleation"</note> of so great a doubt from that highest spiritual emanation who is the only revealer of deep and secret <note>original: "arcane"</note> mysteries (as the Prophet Daniel and the wise Solomon assure us). And the *aevial* world, in like manner, pours out those divine outflows <note>original: "effluxions"</note> or emanations of light through angelic vehicles into the temporal world, which has both a beginning and an end. ...elementary world, to effect His command or pleasure, either for the good and welfare, or the harm and damage, of the elementary creature. This allows things in this world to vary and differ from one another; the variety of properties in this manifold emanation—the flowing forth of the divine power <note>original: "vertue"</note>—establishes an angelic creature, or spiritual channel, of a differing action. Through these channels, the divine power operates centrally by a diverse nature. 

Consequently, he finds it evident that since there are properties of contrary strength in the divine emanations, it must follow that there are different angelic spirits. These correspond in nature and condition to each divine property under which they administer in this world. By these spiritual channels <note>original: "organs"</note> or angelic instruments, the beams and brightness of the eternal influence descend: first into the starry region of the temporal world, and afterward they are showered down into the elementary spheres. They penetrate even into the bowels of the earth and the dark abyss to carry out the will of that eternal and fundamental <note>original: "radicall"</note> essence which sent them forth. By this means, the spirit of wisdom <note>original: "sapience"</note> is rightly said to be in the heavens above and in the abyss beneath, filling or replenishing all things, and ultimately operating all in all.

Finally, the author takes into his consideration a specific object well known to the world. By experimentally inquiring into or searching out its hidden nature, he might practically maintain and visually prove to an incredulous world the mystery of *Sympathy* and *Antipathy*, which he had previously only expressed and verified theoretically, or by speculation. The Lodestone <note>original: "Loadstone," a naturally magnetized mineral</note> or mineral magnet <note>original: "calamite"</note> is therefore the mark at which he aims, or the subject he chooses for this purpose. By doing so, he might more quickly reach those experimental conclusions and comparisons between the magnet and other things, which shall be described at large in the third book of this history. Through this, the nature and condition of the animal may be discovered and demonstrated by that of the mineral.

He asserts confidently that the devil is able to effect nothing except by natural means, which were ordained for the use of man rather than the devil. Consequently, a person who uses natural creatures—even those the devil has practiced upon to work wickedness—is in no way guilty of black magic <note>original: "Cacomagy," from the Greek "kakos" (evil) and "magia" (magic)</note>, as vain men would claim. The righteous use of a creature for which God ordained it is not to be rejected simply because the devil and his followers unrighteously abuse them by converting them to mischief.

### Chapter 1

->*That Sympathy is the offspring of Light, just as Antipathy has its beginning from Darkness: The etymology, or true meaning, of both words, as well as the natures of them both, are described here.*<-

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'S' featuring a capital letter surrounded by intricate floral and vine-like scrollwork.</image-desc>

Since the fundamental and essential Unity—along with its two opposite branches or properties, which are the characteristics of His **Nolunty** <note>original: "Nolunty," a term used by Fludd to describe God's "un-willingness" or the contracting, negative aspect of divine power</note> and **Volunty** <note>original: "Volunty," the "willingness" or expansive, creative aspect of divine power</note>—have been clearly described to you in general terms, along with their two universal effects, namely love and hatred, and all those passions (both spiritual and physical) derived from them—whether they be good or bad for the creature experiencing them—I think it is now most appropriate to enter into our main discourse. We shall analyze the secret depths of that **Sympathy** and **Antipathy** which is made manifest through their effects in both natural and supernatural creatures. 

No learned person can be so ignorant or blind—being instructed by daily experience (which is the mother of even the simplest people)—as to not discern the hidden miracles of both heavenly and earthly things daily shining forth in sympathy and antipathy. These are the concords and discords caused by a secret bond or friendship between them, dating back to their very mixing during their first creation. But before we attempt to enter into this profound discovery, it will be necessary to explain the meaning or etymology of both words, so that we may better understand their distinct natures and essences.

**Sympathy** <note>original: *Sympathia*</note> is a Greek word, <term>sympatheia</term>, and is derived from <term>syn</term> (meaning "together with" or "one with") and <term>patheo</term> (meaning "passion" or "suffering"), which comes from the verb <term>pascho</term> (meaning "I suffer"). Likewise, **Antipathy** <note>original: *Antipathia*</note> is composed of <term>anti</term> (meaning "against") and <term>patheo</term>. Thus, the first term implies a passion born of unity, concord, and love—more properly called "compassion"—and the other implies a hateful <note>original: "odible"</note> passion moved by two resisting and fighting natures of opposing strength. 

I may therefore rightly define Sympathy to be a consent, union, or concord between two spirits that shine forth or have their fundamental source from the very same or similar divine property. For example: all creatures that share in those kindly <note>original: "benigne"</note> emanations or beams sent out from God—through His angelic channels <note>original: "Organs"</note> into the orbit of **Jupiter**—are from there sent down to the earth and bestowed upon a multitude of creatures created under this property. For that reason, these creatures shine and send their beams to one another here on earth lovingly and joyfully, because they all proceed from one root that descends through Jupiter. Also, those that are friends to Jupiter, or similar to him in condition, send down influences into creatures that are welcoming to those who live under Jupiter's influence from their birth, or whose physical makeup is sustained by him. Therefore, they send out beams of friendship or kindness to one another (as do those under **Venus**, etc.). 

But on the contrary, where influences of an adverse property (or of an opposite divine emanation) are sent down to the planet **Mars**—which is an enemy to Jupiter—and from there are poured out onto creatures below, there will be bad and unwelcome encounters between the secret emissions of those creatures' beams. By a natural instinct, one will seek to fly from and escape the encounters of the other, or to resist and fight against the other, as shall be more largely and plainly explained to you hereafter. 

But because the general cause of all Sympathy and Antipathy is a hidden and secret emanation—a shining forth of beams from one creature to another—it will be most necessary for us to unpack <note>original: "unloose the fardle," meaning to open a bundle or burden of items</note> this profound matter. We must clearly see and contemplate the fountain and root of all beams and radiations <note>original: "eradiations"</note> in general, and thereby reveal the mystical reason for their differences. We shall follow their reach even from the root to the trunk, and from there to the boughs and branches, and from those branches descend even to the individual twigs which nourish and foster an infinity of leaves and bring forth fruit in abundance.
