## CHAPTER II.

### *How and by what attributes or properties the Hebrew Rabbis and most profound Kabbalists prove that the contrariety of natures proceeds from one eternal Essence, as from the root of all things.*

It is most certain that, just as there are an infinity of creatures of diverse natures in the universal machine <note>original: "universall machin," referring to the universe as a complex, divinely-constructed system</note>; so also every one of them was first created, and then generated and maintained after generation—even until the day of their corruption—by various celestial influences or many thousands of varieties of beams descending from above. And therefore the wisest among the Kabbalistic <term>Kabbalistic</term> <note>referring to Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism that seeks to understand the relationship between the eternal, mysterious Infinite and the finite universe</note> Rabbis affirm: <margin>Reuchlin, *On the Art of the Kabbalah*, Book 3.</margin> *That there is not any plant or herb here below which does not have a star in the firmament to strike it with its influence and, as it were, to say to it, "Increase or multiply"* <note>original Latin: *Quod non sit ulla planta aut herba inferius, cui non sis stella in firmamento, qua percutiat eam & dicat ei, Cresce*</note>. Nor do the Scriptures appear to be opposed to this opinion of theirs, as will be clearly expressed hereafter in its proper place.

But because the fundamental explanation of this matter requires a more profound contemplation, it will be most necessary for the reader's better instruction to make a diligent inquiry into the depths of this mystery. Namely, we must first discover how all Creation was accomplished by the sending forth of the beams of God's eternal Light, and whether that emanation <term>emanation</term> <note>the process by which all things flow from the first divine principle or source</note> consists of one property or of diverse and manifold properties. I told you and proved clearly before that all things were in the beginning created by one eternal Spirit of Wisdom, which was sent forth from the infinite Fountain of Light in the shape of an emanation, radiation, or outflowing, to inform and activate all things explicitly which before were contained implicitly in the divine power of that everlasting Unity, which in itself is all in all.

I proved it by these express passages in Scripture: <margin>Wisdom of Solomon 7.</margin> Solomon calls this holy Spirit of discipline *the vapor of God's power, and the pure emanation and outflowing of his brightness, and the splendor or beams of his Divine Light, and the mirror without any spot of his goodness.* And Saint <margin>John 1:8.</margin> John says that *in the Word is the life of all things, and that this Spirit was Light in which was no darkness, and that by it all things were <margin>John 1.</margin> made, and without it nothing was made.* And the son of Sirach <note>referring to the author of the Book of Ecclesiasticus</note> says: *That it came <margin>Ecclesiasticus 1:24.</margin> forth from the mouth of the Most High.* And Solomon says: *That it was with Jehovah in <margin>Proverbs 8.</margin> the beginning of all his ways, in the creation; and was that holy Spirit by which he composed or made all things in the Creation.*

And therefore it is apparent that it was by the emanation or sending forth of the universal beam of divine Light that all particular things were diversely framed, shaped, and animated. This happened through many streamings forth of more particular beams of light, proceeding by multiplication from the root to the trunk or body—namely, from the Unity, fountain, or head, to the general emanation. This emanation may rightly be compared to the body of a tree, because from it all boughs, twigs, leaves, and fruit spring forth. And as in this progression the trunk of the tree issues immediately from the root and yet is continuous with the root (which is the beginning), so the divine emanation in like manner proceeds directly from <margin>Reuchlin, Book 3, *On the Art of the Kabbalah*.</margin> *Ein Sof* <note>original: "Ensoph," the Kabbalistic term for the Infinite or the Divine Origin before any self-manifestation</note> or the fountain of infinity. This emanation is not divided or separated from its eternal Original. By reason of this emanation, the Spirit is said *to be the first created before all things*, just as the trunk exists before the boughs, twigs, leaves, or fruit. So, in respect to his essential existence, he is eternal; but in regard to his emanation into the world, he is said to be aeviternal <note>original: "æviall," meaning having a beginning but no end</note>—that is, to have a beginning without end—and therefore becomes the head and Prince of all the aeviternal world (I mean the angelic creatures).

We proceed, therefore, in the progression and multiplication of this universal emanation as follows: from the trunk of the tree issue the general, special, and individual branches, of which the strongest (after the trunk) are the main arms of the body, then the boughs, then the twigs, and lastly the leaves, etc. To this we compare, in our angelic or aeviternal world, the various stations of the Angels assigned to them according to their dignity and riches through the mediation of their body, *Jesus Christ*. And for this reason it is said that <margin>Colossians 1:13.</margin> *He is the Image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creatures; for in him are made all things, both in heaven and earth, as well visible as invisible, whether they are Thrones, or Dominations, or Powers <note>original: "Potestates"</note>, all by him and in him are made, and he is before*

And though they gathered from the Word of God that the Divinity or Godhead is but one internal, unchanging essence and therefore has only one essential title to be expressed—namely, the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The sacred four-letter name of God in Hebrew, YHWH</note> or **Jehovah**—which is his inseparable name because it is assigned to him alone. For as Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>Moses Maimonides (1138–1204), the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher and astronomer</note> explains, it includes and proves by its pure meaning the substance of the Creator, without any respect or relation to the creature. Yet, they nevertheless found that the other names ascribed to him in Scripture note or signify God as he participates with his creatures, or as he relates to created things, and consequently, he is known by the effect of his works.

Regarding his essential name, it was held in such high esteem and reverence among the Hebrews or Jews that it was never uttered except in the Sanctuary, and only by such priests as were consecrated and made holy only unto the Lord; and then it was pronounced during the blessing which the High Priest spoke on the day of fasting. For this reason, that name was held in such honorable regard that it was never spoken or uttered carelessly, because (as the said Rabbi Moses says) **it denotes that God is and was above every essence, in so much as he existed before any thing was existent in the world** <note>original: *denotat Deum esse & fuisse super omnem essentiam quatenus, antequam ulla res esset, existeret*</note>. And this was that precious Name of God which Moses was so desirous to hear and know when he received this answer from him: **YHWH, this is my name forever, JEHOVAH is my everlasting name** <note>original: יהוה, *Hoc est nomen meum in æternum*</note>. This name is so pure and simple that it cannot be articulated, compounded, or truly expressed by the human voice. As for the other names assigned to God, they do not express him according to his essence, but only in respect to his works (as was said)—namely, as he appears as "all in all" and exists in all things.

<margin>Wisdom 16:13</margin>
We must understand therefore, for our better instruction, that since the Divine Nature is and operates in all created things, as well as outside of them (for he is the center of all his creatures, whose circumference cannot be found), in this regard his essential name, the **Tetragrammaton**, is the common agent in every bough or branch of the **Sephirotic** or **Kabbalistic** Tree. It has dominion or preeminence over the whole trunk or body of that tree. Consequently, all the other ten names are assigned to it as they relate to the properties or effects of his many virtues or actions within one individual essence. Therefore, all the rest are subject to it and are wholly contained within it; for it contains the properties of both **Refusal** <note>original: "Nolunty," from the Latin *nolle*, meaning "to be unwilling"</note> and **Will** <note>original: "Volunty," from the Latin *velle*, meaning "to will"</note>, of lack as well as presence, of death as well as life, of cursing as well as blessing, and of evil—in regard to the creatures—as well as good (though nothing is ideally bad in him), of hatred and discord as well as love and concord, and consequently of sympathy and antipathy. All these opposite effects are testified by Scripture to spring from one essential fountain, because it encompasses the power of life and death; it leads to the brink of the grave and restores or brings back again...

Now, because this essential Unity brought to light these contrary effects through opposite properties, the mystical theologians <note>original: "secret Theologians," referring to students of the Kabbalah</note> ascribed various general names to him. These names they gathered from Holy Scripture and appropriated to him according to the effects that follow them. Some of these names incline toward darkness and deprivation, while others incline toward light and presence <note>original: "position"</note>. Some point to severity, while others demonstrate the fruits of his kindness. Some, by a withdrawal <note>original: "deprivation"</note> of his action—which happens by a reflection of his beams back into himself—produce the effects of darkness: namely, an essential coldness <note>original: "frigidity"</note>, numbness <note>original: "stupidity"</note>, immobility, freezing <note>original: "congelation"</note>, contraction, and so on. Others, by an actual outflow <note>original: "emanation"</note> from the center to the circumference, generate the effects of light, such as motion, heat, expansion <note>original: "dilatation"</note>, refinement <note>original: "subtiliation"</note>, and so on. I will therefore list <note>original: "rehearse or reckon up"</note> for you those divine attributes which are ascribed to the sacred Essence, in the order they are numbered in the Kabbalistic Tree. From this Tree, the divine beams of different natures descend to accomplish the various will <note>original: "volunty"</note> of him who sends them forth into the world to act and produce a multiplicity of effects.

The first name of the Divine Attribute is *Ehieh* <note>original Hebrew: "I Am"</note>, and this attribute signifies the fountain or origin of all creatures and the foundation of mercy <note>original: "misericord"</note> and clemency. This is because the outflow <note>original: "effluxion"</note> or radiation that springs from this head is full of grace and spares all; for it represents the Father of pity and mercy, and the God of all consolation, to whom our Savior bids us pray in this form: *Our Father who art in heaven, etc.* And because of this, it is said elsewhere that the *Father judges no man*. Again, it is the part of a father to deal favorably and mercifully with his children; so God, under this attribute, is esteemed to be the Father of all and is therefore kind and merciful toward his creatures, according to this passage from Solomon:

For this reason, it is the ruler <note>original: "President"</note> of the primary or fundamental bright gate, branch, or number <note>referring to the *Sefirot*</note> called *Keter* <note>original: "Cheter"</note> or the Crown <note>original: "Corona"</note>. This is the root of the whole Tree, through which the clear beams—the lucid and sacred outflow of *JEHOVAH* in his creative expression or positive will—descend to the creation of all things. For *Ehieh* signifies the father and root of all creation.

The third name <note>original: "cognomination"</note> is *Elohim*. According to the Kabbalistic interpretation, this name *Elohim* signifies fear and terror. This is because they have observed that through this property or attribute of God, punishments and strategies happen to every <margin>Archang. cabal. de dog. cab.</margin> world. Under this name, JEHOVAH exercises his power for the sudden alteration of the world as well as for the punishment of the wicked. Therefore, the Spirits that receive this divine influence are called *Been Elohim*, the sons of *Elohim*; they are his instruments in the elementary world for carrying out his will through this property. 

By virtue of this name, the commotions of the waters were also made during the first creation and their production out of the dark Chaos. This was only achieved by the extreme contradiction and conflict <note>original: "oppugnancy"</note> that occurred between the fire and the water. Consequently, it did not happen without the dreadful dissention and war of the Elements, which caused terror and many thundering commotions in the dark abyss or deformed waters when each word "*Let it be*" was divinely uttered. For it was by the alchemical <note>original: "Spagericall," referring to the alchemical process of separating and recombining elements</note> or high chemical power of the Word and the working of the Spirit that the separation of one region from another, and the distinction of one formal virtue from another, was achieved. The Psalmist refers to this work where he says: <margin>Psalm 33:6.</margin> *By the Word of the Lord the heavens were made, and by the Spirit from his mouth every power thereof.*

You may therefore perceive that the whole power of the Kabbalistic Tree is contained in these first three branches, just as the physical <note>original: "typicall"</note> world is contained in the Archetype. This consists of a triple property, most aptly referred to the Trinity of Persons. In this, the intelligible world signifies what heaven does in this material and watery world. For the number 2 is the root of Matter, just as 3 is the root of Form. Therefore, as 1 is the formal root to 3 and the material root to 2, so 2 is the material root to 4. Consequently, 4 (which is the symbol or character of matter) and 3 (the figure of form), when added together, produce the universal substance of the world, consisting of form and matter. We must diligently observe that those first three names belong to those properties by which JEHOVAH created the first three days' work, wherein the whole world—with its heavens and elements—was created and placed in its proper positions.

The seven following branches of the Sephirotic Tree pertain to those various alterations or mutations, both favorable and unfortunate, that befall creatures in this world. These occur after the world has been completed and finished by the powerful properties of the three preceding emanations or "streamings forth" of the divine beams. Therefore, the fourth branch of this Tree has as its President the gentle and merciful attribute of God or JEHOVAH called *EL*. Its bright gateway, numbering, or channel, through which it pours its beams into the world, is for that reason styled *Chesed* in Hebrew. In Latin, this is *Clementia* <note>original: "Clementia," meaning Clemency</note>, and in English, *Clemency*. This is because the divine influence that shines out of it is full of grace, kindness, life, and goodness, as will appear by the consequences. The fifth name, which is assigned to the first branch <note>In the Sephirotic Tree, this refers to the Sephirah of Geburah on the left pillar.</note> of the Kabbalistic <note>original: "Cabalitticall"</note> Tree, is called *Elohim Gibbor* <note>meaning "God of Might"</note>. It is an attribute that sends malevolent and unwholesome influence down to the creatures, causing disturbances and troubles in the world through thunders, lightnings, comets, wars, contentions, anger, pestilence, and hot diseases, and so on. The celestial storehouse of this influence is the planet *Mars*. For this reason, the port or channel through which this fiery influx streams forth immediately is called in Hebrew *Geburah*, which signifies power, force, and violence.

The next branch or numeration <note>a Sephirah, one of the ten dimensions or attributes of God in Kabbalah</note>, being the sixth, has for its Lord the name *Eloach*. Its influences or emanations are full of life and golden beauty; therefore, the trunk or port through which it passes is termed *Tiphereth* in Hebrew, which denotes grace, ornament, beauty, and delight. By the golden emanation that flows from this channel, the visible sun of this world receives its bright beauty and is adorned with that admirable life-giving <note>original: "vivifying"</note> virtue, which in its effects manifests and testifies itself to the whole world. This is the grace and ornament that *Job* refers to when he says: *By his Spirit he has adorned the heavens.* <note>original Latin: "Spiritu suo ornavit cælos"</note>

The seventh divine name <note>original: "cognomination"</note> or attribute is *JEHOVAH Sabaoth* <note>original: "Seboath"</note>, which is to say, the God of Armies, the God of jubilation, rest, and perfection. Therefore, the port or channel by which his beams or radiations pass is called *Netzach* <note>original: "Netzeth"</note>, which signifies triumph and victory, as well as justice, charity, and love. Consequently, the influence of generation, multiplication, and delight issues from this emanation, which makes the rolling globe of the celestial *Venus* its storehouse.

The eighth name is *Elohim Sabaoth* <note>original: "Saboth"</note>, or the God of Armies. His port or channel, through which he sends forth the influences or beams of this property into his celestial treasury (the globe of *Mercury*), is called by them *Hod*, or praise, honor, and beauty <note>original: "formosity"</note>. Through this property, he afterward operates on the earth according to his will through changeable and mutable effects.

The ninth is *El Chai*, which is the Living God, or *Shaddai* <note>original: "Sadai"</note>, the Omnipotent God. His numeration, or the gate or channel by which he sends down his bright influences, is called *Yesod* <note>original: "Iesod"</note>, which is to say, the basis or foundation, redemption, or rest. These are received by the sphere of the Moon, which is, as it were, the celestial earth, into which all the influences in general fall. This is the reason it is subject to so many and various mutations, the effects of which—regarding both generation and corruption—are observed on the earth and in the sea.

The last name or attribute is *Adonai*, or Lord. His port or gate, through which he sends forth his illuminations or the active beams of his nature, is termed by the Hebrews *Malkuth* <note>original: "Mulchut"</note>, which is to say, Kingdom or Empire. This numeration brings severity and servility to the creatures through God's anger and wrath, and its influence flows directly into the elementary world.

By these collections and observations of the wisest Rabbis, we find that in these ten general properties of God—signified by the ten attributes of the Divine Essence—all things in the world descend originally from this fountain of Unity. Whether they are esteemed good or evil, positive or primitive, concordant and amiable, or discordant and odious; or, in a word, whether they are secretly or openly opposite, or else concurring in nature or quality with one another, they all come from the same source. Though the source is one in essence, it is nevertheless manifold in property. That property is diverse and changing according to the multiplicity of the Will <note>original: "Volunty"</note> of the Father, or the fountain that sent it out. According to His mind, all things, both concordant and disagreeing, are ordained in both heaven and earth. This happens through a multiplicity of special emanations of different qualities from that eternal, general, and universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> flow. Every one of those specific emanations branches out again into an infinity of individuals, just as ten may be multiplied infinitely. Thus, every one of those specific properties shines forth from a star in heaven—whether fixed or wandering—which acts as its receptacle or storehouse, reaching an infinity of earthly and watery creatures. # Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

The reason why the Divinity created or sent forth one specific emanation <note>original: "eradiation"</note> so contrary to another was for both the preservation and destruction of creatures. Just as the final effect of each of these contrary flows <note>original: "radious effluences"</note> is the creation, generation, and preservation of creatures of their own nature and condition, they are also to be applied either for the preservation or restoration of decaying creatures. This is seen when we apply any poisonous simple <term>simple: a medicinal plant or mineral used as a single ingredient in a remedy</term>—whether animal, vegetable, or mineral—to expel a dangerous disease or to poison a healthy nature. 

In the animal kingdom, this includes the poisonous viper, scorpion, toad, spider, or blistering *Cantharides* <note>original: "Cantharides," also known as Spanish fly beetles</note>. In the vegetable kingdom, it includes the sleep-inducing and numbing poppy or *opium*; the searching and burning *Flammula* <note>original: "Flammula," or spearwort</note> and *Euphorbium* <note>a caustic plant resin</note>; the harsh *Scammony*; the vomit-inducing *Groundsel*, *Daffodil*, *Asara Bacca* <note>original: "Assera Bacca," or European wild ginger</note>, *Bear's-foot*, *Tithymall* <note>original: "Titimall," or spurge</note>, and the poisonous *Aconite*. In the mineral rank, there is the corrosive *Arsenic*; the quick, piercing, and infecting *Quicksilver* and *Sublimate* <note>original: "Sublimary," a form of mercury</note>; the destroying *Realgar* <note>original: "Resalgar," an arsenic sulfide mineral</note>; the vomit-inducing *Antimony*, and similar substances. These all have the property to take away dangerous diseases as well as to cause them. 

In some cases, they remove painful <note>original: "dolorous"</note> maladies, and in others, they bring them quickly and hasten the creature's destruction. Thus, all things can both wound and destroy in certain cases, and heal and cure in others. Yet to Him who sent them—the beams and emanations of their form proceeding from some of His particular properties—they all appeared good, as they were ordained not only to heal in His kindness but also to destroy in His severity. In conclusion, they effect His will one way or another, according to the pleasure of Him who alone essentially works all in all. 

And therefore Solomon <margin>Wisdom of Solomon 11:25</margin> says: *Could anything exist which you would not have to be?* So, everything is good to God, even though they may appear bad to the wicked people who suffer from them. <margin>Ecclesiasticus 39:21</margin> *All the works of the Lord are very good* <note>original: "Opera Domini universa, bona valdè"</note>, says the Wise Man. <margin>Ecclesiasticus 39:25–30</margin> *Good things were created for the good from the beginning, just as for the wicked, good and evil things were made* <note>original: "Bona bonis creata sunt ab initio, sic nequissimis bona & mala"</note>. There are spirits created for vengeance, and in their fury, they execute their torments; in the appointed time, they pour out their strength <note>original: "virtue"</note> and fulfill the fury of Him who made them—namely water, hail, the teeth of beasts (such as the scorpion and serpent), and so on. All these rejoice to execute His commandments upon the Earth. 

For this reason—due to the secret opposition of natures in the world, which originally proceeds from the streams of those variable properties springing from that one incomprehensible Fountain—Love and Hatred, and consequently Sympathy and Antipathy, were created to jostle and, as it were, shoulder one another in this world. This happens generally under the titles of Light and Dark, and particularly in that friendship and hatred observed in Scripture to exist first between the very Angels themselves; then among the stars, which receive these opposite natures from the Angels; thirdly, among the winds and elements, which get their spirit of contention from the stars; and lastly, among those compound creatures made of those elements by the active spirits of the winds. 

But because Sympathy and Antipathy are the most occult and hidden of all opposite qualities—for while we can explain the conflict of elements through manifest qualities like cold, heat, moisture, or dryness, we find no such obvious elementary ground for this hidden opposition—we will dive as far into the depths of this mystery as our limited <note>original: "steril"</note> capacity allows.

For we must consider that the Angels are the direct instruments <note>original: "immediate organs"</note>, by which and through which the Eternal God carries out His will and pronounces His word *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be done"</note>, after His will is decreed within Himself. 
<margin>Psalm 104:4.</margin> 
For that very reason *David* says: 
> The angels of God are most strong in power, carrying out His word and listening to His voice; they are His ministers, who perform His will and pleasure. <note>original: "Angeli Dei validissimi robore, efficientes verbum ejus, auscultantes voci ejus, ministri ejus facientes placitum ejus"</note> 
So it is evident that nothing is accomplished in the world, whether in heaven or on earth, except by one of these organized spirits. 
<margin>Reuchlin:</margin> 
And therefore *Reuchlin* <note>Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a German humanist and scholar of Greek and Hebrew who studied the Cabala</note> says that all bodies, both celestial and earthly, have been assigned by the ordinance of God certain spiritual directors, rulers of their virtues, and presidents over their operations. This applies to those who are rational, namely Man, as well as the irrational, namely the stars of heaven and earthly creatures—including animals, vegetables, and minerals. 
<margin>In his commentary on Cabalistic Dogma.</margin> 
And therefore *Archangelus* the Cabalist <note>Archangelo de Borgonovo, a 16th-century Franciscan and Cabalistic scholar</note> establishes many degrees in the offices of Angels. For some (he says) stand before the divine tribunal of God, constantly praising Him; some minister unto Him, and unto us as well; some have the custody of the watches of the night, of which *Christ* makes mention: 
> *If he comes in the second or third watch of the night, etc.* 
Some have the government of the four seasons of the year, and these are Presidents over the four positions <note>original: "stations"</note> of the Sun; others are ordained rulers over the seven Planets; and some manage the influences and virtues of the fixed Stars and the twelve Signs of the Zodiac, of which St. *John* seems to make mention, saying: 
> *That in the twelve gates—that is, the twelve Signs, which (as Plato says) are the gates of heaven—are the twelve Angels.* 
Some are guardian <term>tutelar: acting as a protector or patron</term> Angels and are ordained for the protection of creatures; some have the custody of beasts, others of plants, others of precious stones and minerals. All these things the secret theologians and wise men affirm, asserting furthermore that God works everything in this lower world through the administration of Angels. And therefore St. *Paul* says: 
> *That all are ministering spirits, sent to carry out that office.* 
Thus far *Archangelus*. And again, *Reuchlin* argues that the flow <note>original: "influxion"</note> of angelic beams from the stars must be diverse and of various natures, because the Angels do not, by their own voluntary action, always move the celestial sphere in the same way, even though because of the forceful motion, it moves daily from East to West.

But what need is there for many words when the progression of the previously mentioned Cabalistic work opens and discovers all the mystical operations and variety of action in the Angels? From there, this mighty Archangel, who is called the "keeper of souls" <note>original: "Custos animarum"</note>, orders that they be hourly poured out into the elementary region to give life to and refresh those spirits which are formed after their own image and nature.

The seventh outflow <note>original: "effluxion"</note> or irradiation comes out of the Sephirotic port of *Netzach* <note>original: "Nezeth"; the seventh Sephirah, representing Victory or Endurance</note>, over which the attribute of God *Jehovah Sabaoth* <note>original: "JEHOVA ZEBAOTH"</note> is Lord, and they pass immediately into the angelic order of *Principalities*. From there, a similar vigor and force is sent out into the creation of elementary spirits, sharing the nature of these formal influences which are fundamentally sent down from the divine influence.

The next flux of divine beams issues from the conduit or channel called *Hod* <note>the eighth Sephirah, representing Glory or Splendor</note>, over which the attribute *Elohim Sabaoth* <note>original: "Elohim Zebaoth"</note> is president. These send down such mutable and changeable influences to animate those elementary spirits which were first created by this attribute, and therefore sympathize with the nature of such beams as are sent down from this Sephirotic gate.

The ninth outflow or irradiation springs out from the eternal fountain by the bright port of *Yesod* <note>original: "Jesod"; the ninth Sephirah, representing the Foundation</note>, whose ruler <note>original: "Rector"</note> or president is the attribute *Shaddai* <note>original: "Sadai"</note>. From there, they rain down showers of these influences upon such spirits or demons in the elementary world as have received their creation from the influences of this property in God.

Thirdly, according to the variety of his divine will <note>original: "Volunty"</note>, things were created so that some sympathize spiritually with one another, while others have an antipathy <note>a natural or deep-seated feeling of dislike or opposition</note> toward each other. This is due to beams of a contrary nature, based on whether the angelic radiation—the shining out of beams from one spiritual creature to another—is harmonious or opposing. This contrariety of conditions comes from the variety of properties within the will of the same fundamental <note>original: "radicall"</note> and eternal Essence. 

Thus, all creatures in the world, both spiritual and physical <note>original: "corporall"</note>, were composed; and thus were they given life <note>original: "vivified"</note> and animated by beams that were either contrary to one another or, because of their harmony and similarity of nature, rejoiced greatly when they met through the radiation of the same influence. We must understand that although every creature receives its fundamental information from these emanations <note>the flow of power or light from God</note>, they may vary from the condition of their parents during reproduction <note>original: "generations and multiplications"</note>. This happens because two different radiations unite at the moment of their birth. 

Therefore, it happens that a man might be unlike his parents in both shape and character; a horse might be more fierce or sluggish than its sire; or a plant or fruit might be more loose, watery, or unwholesome than the stock from which the seed or sap came. Consequently, by the application of angelic beams of an opposite nature at the birth of a man, it may happen that the radiation of a plant, flower, or beast will forever have an antipathy toward that man, even though it perfectly suited and sympathized with another. 

While the opposition between contrary elements is obvious—specifically in the conflict or discord between mismatched natures such as cold and heat, or moisture and dryness—the sympathy and antipathy of elements are well known to everyone (namely between water and fire, and between earth and air). ### CHAP. IV.

> ->**The astrological reason for sympathy and antipathy is expressed here. It is also proven that since all inferior spirits receive their natural influence from above, and since elemental creatures are merely the images of the celestial, it must follow that just as there are sympathetic and antipathetic aspects (or irradiations) between two or more heavenly bodies, there must also be an emission of essential beams from one earthly body to another. Depending on the nature of the creature, this emission is either sympathetic or antipathetic.**<-

I will now stop speaking fundamentally <note>original: "radically"</note> with the mystical Hebrew and Cabalistic theologians, and I will open this mystery of occult radiation—the streaming forth of hidden beams between two creatures—after the manner of an astrologer. This applies whether the creatures are celestial or terrestrial, of a similar and sympathizing nature, or of an unlike and antipathizing condition. I will treat the visible organ as the invisible agent, the external creature as the internal angelic virtue, and the starry influence as the hidden super-celestial emanation. This emanation is poured out into the spirits or intelligences which inhabit and illuminate the stars, and they send it down again from them into the elementary world to animate the winds. Through the winds, they animate the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> element, altered in a four-fold manner. By the element so altered, they inform the various meteorological <note>original: "meteorologick"</note> bodies, and through them, the various compounded creatures of both the sea and land.

We ought therefore to know (speaking like the astrologer) that there is a manifest opposition and agreement, not only in respect to the obvious qualities of the elements, which are observed to be in the fixed stars as well as the wandering stars <note>original: "erratick stars," meaning the planets</note>—for the watery signs of the Zodiac are contrary to the fiery, the nocturnal to the diurnal, the eastern to the western, the male to the female—but also in a more hidden regard. For the best astrologers have noted that as Jupiter, the Sun <note>original: "Sol"</note>, and the Moon <note>original: "Luna"</note> are friends to Saturn; so Mercury, Mars, and Venus are his enemies. Again, all the planets except Mars are friends to Jupiter. Moreover, there is not any of the planets that is a friend to Mars except Venus; the Sun and Mercury are especially his greatest foes. Also, Jupiter and Venus are friends to the Sun, while his enemies are Mars, Mercury, and the Moon. All the planets are said to love and favor Venus, except Saturn. Mercury’s friends are Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn; his enemies are the Sun, Moon, and Mars. The friends of the Moon are Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn; her enemies are Mars and Mercury. The friends to the Head of the Dragon <term>Head of the Dragon: the North Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of positive or increasing influence</term> are Jupiter and Venus; its enemies are Saturn and Mars. Lastly, the enemies of the Tail of the Dragon <term>Tail of the Dragon: the South Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of negative or decreasing influence</term> are Jupiter, the Moon, and Venus; conversely, its friends are Saturn and Mars.

Besides all this, we ought to note that there is another kind of friendship or enmity between the planets: namely, when one of them has its "exaltation" <term>exaltation: a specific sign in the zodiac where a planet's influence is considered to be at its most powerful and beneficial</term> or dignity in another's "House" <term>House: a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</term>. In this case, the things subject to the influence of one will lovingly embrace the presence <note>original: "aspect"</note> of the other. Contrariwise, the "detriment" <term>detriment: a sign opposite to a planet's home sign, where its influence is weakened or "oppressed"</term> or depression of one planet in the House of another causes the spirit of the creature born under that planet (the one in detriment) to view the other planet antipathetically. By this means, the presence of the person or thing born under the planet of that House will be unpleasant and hateful to the other person or thing whose detriment is in that same House. On the other hand, we must note that two creatures will sympathize well and joyfully agree with one another where their planets agree in nature, quality, essence, and strength—as are Mars and Venus, for these sympathize by a natural instinct. So also Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, and the Moon agree together; and likewise, the "unfortunate" planets <note>Saturn and Mars were traditionally known as the "greater" and "lesser malefic" or unfortunate planets</note> agree in the multiplying of misfortunes.

<header>*Mosaical Philosophy.* Book 2.</header>

We ought also in like manner to know that the Sign which has the most dignity of a Planet—such as its House, Triplicity, Face, Exaltation, Term, or such like—best sympathizes with the *geniture* <term>The astrological chart or position of the stars at the moment of birth or creation.</term> of that Planet. Conversely, the Signs or the fixed impressions of the firmament which are opposite in nature or full of misfortunes (such as the "fall" or "detriment" of a planet) cause a hidden hatred and repulsion through their rays when related things secretly influence one another through their astrological aspects. Also, the manner in which their rays are cast out creates a wondrous alteration in the two subjects; for as the rays of the stars were toward one another at the birth of the animal or the sprouting of the plant, so shall their true character remain and be expressed in the thing born or produced. I will therefore explain the nature of these rays or secret radiations that accompany the influence of the stars in a more thorough manner, because the secret astrological mystery of the sympathy or antipathy between things here below consists in this.

<margin>Al-Kindi, *On the Stellar Rays* <note>original: "Alkindus de Radiis"</note></margin>
First, I must have you know that the most deep and insightful astronomers are of the opinion that every star in heaven has a nature or condition specific to itself, which governs the projection of its rays with others. Just as every star has a unique nature not found in any other (in which the emission of rays is contained), so these rays are observed to be of a diverse condition, even as the stars themselves are diverse in nature; for every star has its position in the heavens, entirely distinct and different from another. Therefore, it follows necessarily that each of them has a different perspective from one another and toward all other things or places contained in this world. Now, it is certain that the variety of the *aspect* <term>The specific angular relationship between heavenly bodies that determines their influence.</term> varies the effect of the rays, just as various other properties of the stars do the same. Because of this, it happens that each star operates differently and affects things differently in various places and subjects, no matter how small or slight the difference may be, since the entire operation of the stars proceeds from the rays, which vary in every different aspect among themselves. For the rays that issue from the center of the star to the center of the earth are found—and proven by experience—to be the strongest in their manner of operation. However, the ray that is shot out or emitted obliquely <note>original: "ejaculated or emitted obliquely"</note> is weakened and diminished in effect according to the proportion of its slanted motion, unless it is strengthened and comforted by the meeting rays of other stars in the same place or point; for each particular star casts its rays to every place. Therefore, the diversity of rays being collected or gathered together alters the nature of each place or subject, since there is a different combination of rays in every different place and thing, derived from the general or total harmony of the stars. Because of this, in every place and at every time, a diversity of individual creatures is produced in this world. The celestial harmony is said to effect all of this by the projection of rays into this lower elemental region, which continually vary and diversify themselves. By this, therefore, it is evident that the radiations of all the stars have different operations in the things of this world according to the different properties of those things, because everything rises, springs, and exists by these emanations or streaming rays. Moreover, we ought to note that the condition of the heavenly harmony is such that, since all the stars are of different natures, and for this reason all their rays have different effects in the elemental world, it happens that the operations of these rays are assisted or aided regarding the same matter or subject; and again, in another matter, they are hindered by one another. Moreover, we must observe that over everything in this world, a predominant star is ordained. And again, there is some celestial Sign that holds rule above all others in the work and government of that same thing. From this condition of the starry rays among themselves, there arises so great a difference and diversity in the things of this world that two or more things can hardly be found which are alike in all respects to one another, although human senses may not be sufficient in some cases to perceive the difference.

To conclude, the celestial harmony works so differently in various places and times that it now generates or produces like from like, and at other times it brings forth things that are unlike. It also produces similar things at one time by a similar motion, and at another time unlike things by an unlike motion; now by a slow motion, and then by a swift motion. Thus, we see that by innumerable other kinds of ways, the things of this world and their motions are observed to vary according to places and times.

# Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

<margin>Al-Kindi, *On the Stellar Rays* <note>original: "Alkind. de Radiis stellarum"</note></margin>
When any wise person carefully considers this, and seeing it is evident that the earthly world <term>original: "Elementary world"; the realm of the four elements (earth, water, air, and fire) as opposed to the celestial realm.</term> is made after the pattern of the heavenly world—so that everything contained within it carries its image—we should not hesitate to affirm that all things in this world, whether they are physical substances or essential qualities <term>original: "essentiall accidents"; properties that belong to a thing but are not its core essence, like the heat of a fire.</term>, emit beams toward one another in their own way. They do this by imitating the stars from which they are derived. Otherwise, it would not be possible for them to fully contain the form of the starry world.

This is clearly and sensibly confirmed by certain examples. For instance, fire sends out heat to its neighboring parts; conversely, the earth breathes out or produces the beams of its coldness. Also, medicines taken internally or applied externally send out the beams of their power <note>original: "virtue"</note> into the body. We also observe that the collision or clashing together of two hard bodies creates a sound or noise, pouring out or dispersing itself through "beams" in its own fashion. Again, all colored things send out their beams, by which they are seen. Since this is the case, we may boldly state that everything that actually exists in this earthly world sends out beams in every direction, which fill the entire surrounding space in their own way. 

Therefore, Al-Kindi <note>Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi (c. 801–873 AD), a famous Arab philosopher and scientist.</note> asserts that every place in this world contains the beams of all the things that actually exist within it. And just as each thing differs from another, so do the beams of every subject differ in nature and effect from the beams of all other things. Because of this, the operation of beams from various things is diverse and different.

So far, I have expressed the opinions of learned astronomers regarding celestial radiations. Through this, it is also made clear to us that every creature in the earthly world is not only shaped <note>original: "informed"</note> by these celestial beams that have been poured out upon them, but they are also preserved by a continuous succession of this beamy influence. Consequently, everything created by this celestial influence is the "type" or image of those celestial spirits whose beams created them. Therefore, it must follow by Al-Kindi's rule that if they are the images of the celestial shapes that fashioned them, they must likewise emit their own beams—though invisibly—in the same way the stars do, from which they draw the influence of their being. 

For we must understand (as I proved in my *Radical Inquiry*) that the essential beams descending from God to the Angels, from the Angels to the Stars, and from the Stars to the creatures, are continuous because they are indivisible. For there is no created power <note>original: "formed Virtue"</note> issuing from God that can be separated from its Fountain. Since this is true, it must follow that these beams shine out of the body in which they reside toward other lights sent out from other creatures, just as one star in heaven "beholds" another through this or that astrological aspect. 

Therefore, pay close attention to what I say now: I told you that every star in heaven has its friend and its enemy. I told you that the reason for this opposition—among the Angels as well as the stars of heaven—was the variety of the Will <note>original: "Volunty"</note> of God, which was the cause of such opposite attributes as are expressed and affirmed by the Hebrew text (which the Cabalistic Rabbis approve of). I proceed, therefore, and say that if it happens in the heavenly harmony that there is a powerful aspect or streaming forth of beams that aligns with the irradiation of the ethereal or starry "Lord of Life" <term>The planet that has the most influence over a person's life and health in their birth chart.</term> of a produced thing—be it animal, plant, or mineral—and if, by emanation, the star interacting with that Lord of Life is an utter enemy to it, then the spirit of that creature will be subject to discordant passions, such as fear, anger, sadness, and suspicion. 

This happens especially when the enemy of the Lord of Life is more powerful in the celestial chart or horoscope and applies itself to the Lord of Life while it is weakened by a bad astrological aspect. In this way, a kind of insensible, antipathetic disturbance happens to the spirit of the thing produced. Also, if a creature begins its "nativity" <term>The moment of birth or creation, which determines its astrological character.</term> when its enemy was most powerful in heaven, then when its own "Lord" is joined with that first enemy in a bad aspect, and that creature is brought into the presence of another creature, there must be an antipathetic distaste in the spirit of the first. This is because the guardian spirit <note>original: "Genius"</note> of the latter is timid and afraid of the guardian spirit of the first, which is its enemy and more powerful. Therefore, when the two earthly subjects of these different stars are present and emitting the beams of their nature, those beams must necessarily work against one another, and the strongest must prevail no other-

But you must note and observe that although the stronger beams are antipathetic <term>original: "antipatheticall"; having a natural or instinctive aversion or opposition.</term> toward the weaker, it does not follow that the weaker beams are antipathetic toward the stronger; this is because the stronger "passion" (or being acted upon) is always in the weaker, while the "action" remains in the stronger. 

But if an object on Earth governed by a specific star is brought near an object governed by its celestial enemy, and if there was no "aspect" <term>original: "aspect"; the relative position or angle between two planets in the sky, believed to influence earthly events.</term> between them at the time of their birth or creation, they do not act antipathetically while in each other's presence. Yet, their natures or beams will be much more inclined toward actual opposition if, at the time of their meeting, those enemy stars in heaven look upon one another with a malevolent aspect. 

For example: If **Jupiter** is the "Lord" <note>The planet that has the most influence over a person's birth chart.</note> of a person's birth or the production of a thing, and **Mars** views him in a "quadrat" <term>original: "quadrat"; a square aspect, where planets are 90 degrees apart, usually considered stressful or unlucky.</term> or opposite aspect; and if this creature (suppose it is a man) meets a cat whose birth was ruled by a very powerful **Mars** in heaven, which views **Jupiter** with an evil radiation—then the sight of this cat will be unpleasant to that man. 

However, the truth is that there may be some fixed star which is the assigned origin or protector of the cat or animal of whatever nature, which may be antipathetic toward the fixed star and the planet within it that has dominion over the cat. 

But on the other hand, if the beams of two or more planets or signs meet or concur in the same generation or production of a thing—where the star with the most dominion is the "Lord" of the thing (whether animal, vegetable, or mineral)—and these planets are friends to one another, then if any other object presents itself that is fashioned by the beams of that other planet, these two subjects emitting their beams upon the earth will love each other. They will agree with one another through sympathy. Their sympathy for one another will be even greater the more they agree in nature, property, and the benevolence of their celestial aspect at the moment of their births or beginnings. 

For example: If **Jupiter** is the Lord of a man's birth and aspects **Venus**, and **Venus** aspects him in a "Sextile" or "Trine" aspect <note>A Sextile (60 degrees) or Trine (120 degrees) are considered harmonious and positive alignments in astrology.</note>; and again, **Venus** is the most powerful planet in the birth of a cat or dog and has a relationship through its beams to **Jupiter** in a good aspect—then I say that there will be a reciprocal affection and sympathy between both creatures. 

Also, if a similar friendship is made in heaven at the growth of any vegetable, the man or beast will be well pleased by the presence, sight, and taste of that vegetable; and if he eats it, it will agree well with his nature. All of this is to be understood regarding things which, from their creation, were not ordained to be entirely opposite and antipathetic to the creature (such as vermin and the like). Nevertheless, even these are made more amiable, less harmful, and more convenient for the use of human or animal bodies by these concordant radiations from heaven. 

Also, since the Fall of **Adam**, enmity has been set between the Serpent and Man; and yet, by a similar confluence in heaven, some people actually like serpents or snakes. Others, by the meeting of contrary beams, loathe and flee from them with exceeding detestation and abhor them beyond all measure. 

But to return again to the root of this business: the evident cause of the sympathy and antipathy of things proceeds from the radical Mystery of the opposite attributes or properties in God, which have the origin of their emanation from the secret and hidden "Volunty" <term>original: "Volunty"; the will or power of willing (from Latin *voluntas*).</term> of Eternity, as I have told you before. And yet, these astrologers have such strong reasons from their experiences with the stars that they all believe the origin of sympathy or antipathy comes from them. Based on this, philosophers in general concluded that:

<center>*Inferior things are governed by the superior, and the inferior world is contiguous to the superior bodies.* <note>original: "Inferiora à superioribus reguntur, & que Mundus inferior, sit corporibus superioribus contiguus."</note></center>

To return to our purpose: just as God ordained two principles of a completely contrary nature from his infinite fountain of Unity—namely, Light and Darkness—so the first-born of Darkness was *Litigium* <note>original: "Litigium"; Latin for "Strife" or "Discord"</note>, or the Prince of Darkness, who was named Satan. His rule is in darkness and over all dark things or privative properties. He has his four-fold angels or demons of a different nature who have dominion over the winds and elements; they are ready to carry out their Prince's commands in a business of darkness, and therefore of discord and deprivation, regardless of the property of whichever wind is blowing. This is according to the book of Revelation:
<margin>Revelation 7</margin>
*I saw four angels standing upon the four angles of the earth, acting as presidents over the four winds of the earth, unto whom it was granted to hurt the earth and the seas*, etc. Now each of these angels has many divisions and subdivisions of legions under them, who act at their will when they have dominion to blow and trouble the air. All these are animated by the influences sent down from the Olympic spirits <note>Olympic spirits: In Renaissance magic, these are seven spirits (such as Aratron or Bethor) who govern the world and correspond to the seven classical planets.</note>, just as they also have their life and times of dominion appointed to them by the Imperial Archangel. These are the immediate dispensers of the will of their eternal head and well-spring.

For this reason, just as we witness with our own eyes that the sunbeams completely illuminate whatever object they look upon—the object being enlightened by an infinity of beams united in and upon it—so also all emanations carried down to the stars fill them with an infinity of beams. These beams act as subdivided angels, possessing the nature of that entire emanation which gave life to the stars. Therefore, all the Olympic spirits of each star are alike in property. The same logic applies to the angelic beams that issue from each wind and fill the whole air, water, and earth with an innumerable number of harmful spirits of their own nature. 

And yet it is certain that as God made all
<margin>Wisdom of Solomon 1</margin>

This was *Michael*, to whom the government of the Sun and East is ascribed. This great and sovereign angel is said by others to be *Metatron*, whom we spoke of before, and whom others consider to be the image of eternal Wisdom <note>original: "Sapience"</note> by which all things were made. In any case, it was that imperial angel who had victory over the Dragon and his angels, and therefore holds them as his vassals. 

So, just as Satan is the Prince of Darkness and an enemy to light (and therefore to Christ and his creatures), this great angel is the Prince of Light. He is the one in whom is Jehovah’s Name (as the Scripture affirms), in whom is life, and in whom is light without darkness. He has power over light, existence <note>original: "position"</note>, and life, and is therefore an utter enemy to darkness and its Prince. For that cause, just as Satan has his armies scattered in the air by the four winds, so also the imperial and victorious Prince of Light has his conducting angels dispersed over the face of the earth and waters, and in every place throughout the universal element of the air, to resist the violent and subtle or invisible assaults of the army...

God created four Angels for the four winds, who are Rulers or Presidents over them in the daytime and in the night: Michael, who is of the part of clemency and mercy, is made the Lord and Ruler over the East wind until midday, and until night he governs the West; then Gabriel, in the power of judgment and severity, is established as Lord over the North wind; and Noriel or Uriel is made Overseer of the South.

No one should wonder that I derive such a variety of good and bad properties—which are carried out by the winds—from a single Divine Essence. That Essence imparts its Will through various living properties to the four Archangels,

This occurs when the benign stars and planets have dominion in heaven, and consequently send their influences below. On the other hand, bad and disastrous accidents, armed with destructive effects, sometimes strike the creatures of this elementary region. This happens because of "severe" emissions of beams from the winds, which animate those evil spirits that hover invisibly in the air in infinite multitudes. These spirits are gladdened and revived by the blasts that issue from the stations of their cruel Princes; these winds act as a summons and a call to arms to stir them to wrath and to blow the coals of their sleeping malice.

In the great world and its creatures, these manifest as stupidity or "congelation" <note>original: "congelation" — a thickening or freezing of vital energy</note>, discord, hatred, irritability, fear, and so on. Ultimately, this leads to Antipathy, which comes from contracting from the circumference toward the center. All of these are specific passions that either affect and revive the vital spirits with comfort by expanding those spirits with beams of joy and delight, or else they choke and suffocate them with the gloomy fog of darkness by contracting those spirits with the mist of grief or private sadness.

## Section 2: Mosaic Philosophy

...the dark Chaos (which act was brought about by the <term>spagyric virtue</term> <note>original: "spagerick vertue" — an alchemical term referring to the power of separating and refining elements</note> of the bright emanation, or the Word of the eternal Unity), the humid or watery nature of the world was created. That is to say, it was essentially formed by the lively presence of the aforementioned all-informing Spirit. Through that union of two contrary natures into one—namely, the informing essence (the "naturating nature") and the informed substance (the "nature naturated")—the spirit of the world was animated. 

It was afterwards termed by the wisest philosophers the *Anima mundi* <note>original: "Anima mundi" — Soul of the World</note>, which is that angelic composition of two parts. For this reason, it was called by the Sages *Alterity* <note>original: "Alteritas" — the state of being "other" or diverse</note>, just as God in his simple nature is called *Identity* <note>original: "Identitas" — the state of being one and the same</note>. Now, the passive portion from which "alterity" was made is said to be the humid created nature, or the "naturated" matter of the world. Its active essence is the ever-living emanation from eternity which (as the Apostle teaches us) gives life to all things, fills all things, and is all in all. The union of these two makes the universal soul of the world. In respect to the simple, creating, and life-giving emanation, it is called *Mind* <note>original: "Mens"</note>; in regard only to the informed spirit, it is called *Spirit* <note>original: "Spiritus"</note>; and when these two are united as one, it is called *Soul* <note>original: "Anima"</note>. 

Behold here the third degree of the sympathetic and antipathetic progression from the simple root of eternity: namely, the created matter or spirit in the soul of the world. Being the child or offspring of darkness (the dark Chaos), it is naturally prone toward the negative or privative effects of darkness. Consequently, in its own condition, it is apt to receive any discordant and antipathetic impression which the angelic spirits of darkness shall imprint upon it. 

The sacred light—which animates the humid spirit of the world and the entire mass of the waters from which the heaven and the earth were made (as St. Peter confirms)—is the most movable, agile, and active of all things. On the contrary, the matter that is informed (and therefore the created body and spirit) is most degenerate from it, in that it is in no way inclined by its own nature toward motion or life. As the philosophers say, "Matter is by itself ineffective toward motion, and falls away from the soul or light itself" <note>original Latin: "Materia est per se ad motum inefficax, & ab ipsa anima seu luce degenerans"</note>. 

Therefore, of its own accord, matter takes after the condition of its mother <term>Chaos</term> (or *Hyle* <note>original: "Hyles" — the Greek term for primordial matter</note>) and is inclined toward rest, immobility, darkness, cold, <term>spissitude</term> <note>original: "spissitude" — density or thickness</note>, and freezing. For this reason, it suffers the impressions and characters of both oppositions. That is to say, sometimes it inclines toward darkness, and then it grows dense, opaque, cold, immobile, thick, and heavy; in that state, it tends downward toward the cold center or the seat of darkness, which is its mother. Then it is in rebellion and opposition against light, motion, and heat, and so it is antipathetic to the actions of light and life. 

We see this in the airy spirit of the world: though it is naturally clear, light, <term>diaphanous</term> <note>original: "diaphan" — transparent</note>, thin, movable, and soaring upward, the operating power of the descending light can be overcome. By Northern cold, that spirit becomes congealed, opaque, thick, and immobile—fixed into snow, hail, ice, frost, and the like. Thus, by this antipathetic addition of the cold characteristics of the dark abyss, it becomes discordant with the loving union and harmonious connection it previously had with the region of light. 

On the other hand, the bright form of the soul (which is the essence of that eternal emanation) gives the matter or spirit of the soul its life, action, motion, heat, thinness, and transparency. This happens to a greater or lesser degree depending on how much power and dominion the light has over it. We must note that the more the spirit approaches the nature of light, the firmer the bonds of its sympathetic accords become. Since sympathy consists of things of a like nature, the nearer the spirit approaches "form" (light), the greater the sympathy and accord, the surer the tie, and the more powerful the effect. The more the created spirit is illuminated, the less it remembers that natural inclination and love it had for its dark origin. Indeed, through such an extreme, purified exaltation, it becomes, as it were, deified. 

Therefore, it was Plato's opinion that if the middle spirit—which exists between the mental beam of light and the dark bodily substance—adheres more to the divine or mental beam than to the dark body, it will become a good <term>Daemon</term> <note>original: "Demon" — here meaning a guiding spirit or minor deity, not necessarily an evil one</note> or Angel. But if it respects the body more than the divine beam, it will descend into the nature of a <term>Cacodemon</term> <note>original: "Cacodemon" — an evil spirit</note>, or spirit of darkness. 

We are also taught by Scripture that by adhering to this divine light—namely, to Christ—we shall be transformed into the same image, provided we forsake this dark world and the lusts of the obscure body or flesh. But to return to the soul of the Great World: if the airy spirit is given over to the power of darkness, it becomes bodily and turns into that same image (namely, frost, snow, hail, etc.). But if the hot effect or the formal act of light prevails even slightly over the stupid cold of darkness, it leaves its opaque quality and becomes diaphanous, and...

# Mosaical Philosophy. Book 2.

...returns from an earthly, fixed, and obscure nature, unto a clear, transparent, and fluid substance; and by another degree of the divine act, it is made more subtle, more expanded, more invisible and pure, and it is called **Air**; by a third degree, it is purified into **Fire**; by a fourth into **Ether**, at which point it loses all desire for change and forgets the <term>privative</term> <note>original: "privative" — relating to "privation," the state of being without form or light</note> source from which it came; by a fifth it becomes angelic or <term>empyreal</term> <note>original: "emperiall" — the highest, most fiery part of heaven</note>; and so it is exalted more and more in dignity, according as it is more and more obedient unto the actions of the eternal and <term>universal</term> <note>original: "catholick" — meaning all-encompassing or universal</note> influence of form, which shines forth from the fountain of infinity. 

For we must understand that the whole inclination of the eternal emanation is to reduce this child of darkness unto eternal light, unity, and life; just as, conversely, the endeavors of the potential darkness—which is the stamp of God’s <term>Nolunty</term> <note>original: "Nolunty" — the divine "will-not" or the negative aspect of God's will, as opposed to "Volunty" or "Will"</note>, or privative nature—are completely opposite. So, the entire goal of the creating light's action is to unite all things by the harmonious bond of love and unity, and consequently of sympathy—namely, by making the universal child of darkness like itself, and therefore causing two things to feel compassion for each other. 

But conversely, the nature of darkness is always inclined to create duality out of unity and to breed discord by violating the bonds of concord, thereby producing a new antipathy and hatred to destroy the fruits of love. Thus, the spirit which light has redeemed out of the dark Chaos is the intermediate subject between both extremes—that is to say, between light and darkness. Therefore, it is the passive subject ordained by the Creator to endure the impressions of each opposite extreme; whereupon it becomes sometimes the subject of **sympathy** (namely, when it is obedient unto union and light) and sometimes of **antipathy** (to wit, when it rebels against that light). 

Thus do we see the true subject of all passion in the soul of the world, and this was the only reason why the philosopher **Heraclitus** declared with such confidence that all things were composed of strife and friendship, and **Empedocles** claimed that the soul was made of amity and enmity. I will now, therefore, describe to you that harmonious order which that eternal love (who shone out from the Father of light and love) has put and placed in each region of this world, to distinguish the two different natures from one another by placing between them an intermediate subject which agrees with each extreme. And first, I will speak of the orders in the universal spirit of the world, and lastly, of every particular enlivened and active spirit, in the intellectual or empyreal realm, as well as the vital or ethereal, and the natural or elementary heaven, in their proper order.

<margin>
Ephesians 2.
Ephesians 6.
</margin>
We must place the two opposite principles in this world at the two extremes of its radius. First, we imagine the seat of the God of light, or of the divine act, to consist in the outer curve of the higher and purer sphere of the **Angels**, or the **Empyreal Heaven** (I speak according to common understanding), which is in the circumference of the vaulted world. Then we deem the throne of darkness, or the divine power of restraint, to be in its center, as the furthest place from its opposite in nature, which is light. Here you may see the two principles of concord and discord, of love and hatred, and consequently of sympathy and antipathy, with the effects of which all Scripture and every part of philosophy is full. 

The universal matter which was originally extracted out of darkness—namely, the waters, which were made the material substance out of which the heavens and the earth were framed by the divine word, occupying all that space which the world contains—was, by the celestial **alchemy** <note>original: "Alchimy"</note> or <term>spagyric</term> <note>original: "spagerick" — an alchemical term for the process of separating and purifying substances</note> power of the divine illuminating emanation, divided according to the contrary and discordant natures of the two said principles into the **upper waters** and the **lower waters**. Of these, the first or higher waters were good and obedient unto the bright Divinity, and were converted into a fiery nature, being thereafter termed the "Empyreal nature" for their obedience to the bright emanation; they were full of intellectual fire and angelic light. Therefore, this portion of the waters was ordained as the seat of the good Angels. 

The lower waters, conversely—being dreg-like, gross, impure, and therefore more rebellious against light and obedient by participation to darkness—were placed next to their dark beginning, namely, the earth. They occupied all that space between the starry heaven and the earth, which is called the **Elementary** region, and for this reason is subject to all changes of generation and corruption. This was ordained to be the seat of Satan and his angels, who for that reason is called the "Prince of this world" and the "Prince of the air"; and his primary subjects are called "Principalities," "Powers," and "Governors of this world." He has placed his seat in the center of the heavens so that by one most perfect harmony—specifically a spiritual *diapason* <note>an octave, representing a perfect musical interval or cosmic harmony</note>—he might illuminate the angels above and the stars around him. By a more physical *diapason*, he might penetrate into the center of the physical world to share his perfection with every creature, so they might be made beautiful by his bright presence and brought to life by the penetrating beams of his essence. Consequently, the spirits of darkness are weakened by the appearance of his Glory. 

It is as if a single musical string were stretched between the Fountain of Light and the abyss of darkness. When struck, it creates a single tone (a unison). But if it is pressed down and divided exactly in the middle, each half, when struck, will produce a double *diapason* relative to that original tone. This signifies a double perfection proceeding from the glorious universal radiation: one part focuses on decorating the lower waters with life and virtue, while the other creates a bond of friendship among the higher realms. 

Now, since the body of the Sun and the substance of the Ether consist of a middle or intermediate spiritual matter, it is clear that they are also subject to being changed by "passion" <note>external influence or impression</note>, both discordant and harmonious. If this were not so, the Sun would not be the immediate receiver of those opposite radiations that descend from the different divine attributes. But in practice, we find the opposite to be true: some stars are "friends" and harmonize in nature with certain creatures below, while others hate one another intensely. Consequently, they send down contrary influences into this lower world, which trigger opposing passions or impressions in the vital spirits or souls of certain physical creatures. Philosophers also testify that during sleep and rest, the spirits are drawn inward from the circumference to the center, in the same manner as the dark Chaos or the cold North wind. As for the elementary world, it clearly abounds with the effects of these two opposites. Therefore, to prevent any continuous, unnatural disturbance that might deprive this great formal workman <note>meaning God or the Divine Architect</note> of his goal—which was to place concord and peace within the machine he had ordered and framed—he divided each region in this lower world. He did this so that an impartial friend might be placed between two extreme enemies, which he achieved by "weight, number, and measure." 

Thus, to the heaviest portion of the lower waters, he gave the least amount of "form" <note>the active, spiritual principle of light</note>, so that by its coarseness and weight it might fall to the center and remain fixed there; this was called "earth." Then, to another portion, he granted a double measure of Light to make it reside in a higher region. Because of this, the matter next to the earth became thinner, lighter, and more movable. This increase of Light melted the frozen waters slightly and made them fluid and transparent. Because its matter is continuous with that of the earth, and because of its cold nature, water is a temperate friend to the earth and takes its place next to it. It is not as cold as the earth, nor as moist as the air. 

Matter is not sufficiently refined <note>original: "subtiliated"</note> until the bright Agent of the world <note>the sun or divine light</note> bestows three portions of his Light upon the dark, watery abyss above the water. This converted part of the coarse lower waters into a thinner and lighter shape than the element of water; this was the "air." Because of this triple proportion of formal light, the air was hotter and more expanded than the water. Therefore, just as the water was cold (but not as cold as the earth) and moist (but not as moist as the air), so the air is hot (but not as hot as fire) and moister than water. Because of its moisture, this portion of the universal element is friendly to water on one side, and because of its heat, it is friendly to fire on the other. 

Lastly, that uncreated Spirit of life multiplied a part of those waters by another, higher degree of refinement and purity. It became the most subtle and highest portion of the general elements—the fire—and is consequently hot and dry. Because of its dryness, it agrees on one side with the earth (which is its neighbor in the cycle of elements), and on the other side with the air, in respect to its heat. However, it is hotter than the air and not as dry as the earth. 

Here you see the effect of that Sympathy which the peace and love of God placed among the clashing enemies of this world. Because of this, water acts as a friend to both air and earth, becoming a mediator <note>original: "stickler"</note> and peacemaker between them. The air, as a friend to the two enemies fire and water, is made an impartial judge between them both. In this way, one opposite is kept from struggling and fighting with the other by the super-celestial and golden tie of peace.

Thus you may see that the very angels of heaven—since they are created of air, or the moist spirit of the world (which is their external part), and the bright emanation from Unity (which is their internal part)—are subject, by reason of their material substance, which participates in both extremes, to affections or passions, both sympathetic and antipathetic. Consequently, they are able, by reason of their contrary properties, to produce both sympathetic and antipathetic occurrences <note>original: "accidents"</note> in the spirits of the elementary creatures. 

For example's sake, we will compare the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> sympathy and antipathy in the soul of the great world <note>the Macrocosm</note> to that peculiar soul or spirit which is in man <note>the Microcosm</note>, seeing that every particular was framed out of the universal. We ought, therefore, to understand that the whole essence of the soul or spirit of man, though it be invisible, extends and manifests itself by her virtues and faculties. For by her irascibility <note>the faculty of anger or defense</note> she condemns and hates; by her concupiscibility <note>the faculty of desire</note> she does covet and desire; and by her rationality she distinguishes and discerns between them both. 

And truly, the whole effect of the soul's essence consists in these three powers, of which the first is compared to the action of the lower waters, which is apt to jar and disagree, and is the region of Strife <note>original: "Litigium"</note> or the Prince of Darkness. The second is referred to the nature of the firmament, which is the region of life and healthy love. The last is referred to the angelic and intellectual heaven, which discerns between things that belong to the lower heavens or regions of the world. 

From this it appears that from her rational property, every sense belonging to the soul of man proceeds, just as from the other two, every affection, motion, or passion of the mind arises and springs. Now there are known to be four affections of the soul: two proceed from her desiring <note>original: "concupiscible"</note> power, namely, **Joy** and **Hope** (for we rejoice and are glad at that which we love, or we hope for and expect that which shall rejoice us or make us glad); and the other two issue from her irascible faculty or virtue, namely, **Grief** <note>original: "Dolour"</note> and **Fear** (for now we grieve at that which we hate, or we fear that which would make us grieve or be painfully affected). Truly, we shall, after a proper investigation, find that these four affections of the microcosmic soul are not only the beginnings and common matter of all moral vices or virtues, but also the origins of metaphysical or hidden, and physical or elementary, and apparent sympathy and antipathy, as well in the little world of man as in the great world and every creature within it.

For I would not have you ignorant that since the soul in man is derived from the life-giving emanation dwelling in the world's spiritual vehicle, it must follow that the soul in the great world must necessarily have the same faculties that the little world’s soul has; for, *that which makes something a certain way, is itself even more that way* <note>original: "Quod facit tale, est magis tale"</note>. These faculties in the soul of man were derived from the great world and the eternal soul that gave it life. 

Therefore, it follows that there is a rationality, a concupiscibility, and an irascibility in the soul of the great world, though not made manifest to us. First, because it has attributes of irascibility and displeasure: for from his attribute of "God the Mighty" <note>original: "ELOHIM Gibbor"</note>, He sends down through the gate of "Strength" <note>original: "Geburah," the Kabbalistic Sephirah of judgment and severity</note> the fiery beams of his displeasure. This is done by his archangel **Samael** into the globe or sphere of **Mars**, who is for that cause the president of the irascible faculty of the greater world.
