It is also clear that there is an irascible quality within the elements, shown by the deadly hatred between fire and water, and between air and earth. 

It is equally evident that there is a love and attraction <note>original: "concupiscence"</note> between things, because every nature rejoices in its own kind. Therefore, by a natural inclination, everything moves toward and transforms itself into its likeness as much as possible; it is especially inclined toward its own nature. Thus, we see that fire naturally seeks and moves toward fire, water toward water, and earth toward earth. But above all, the life-giving <note>original: "vivifying"</note> spirit of every living thing is celestial, and therefore rises above the station of the elements. It fervently seeks and thirsts after its likeness and rejoices in its presence and cooperation. 

For this reason, this passion in any creature will be more truly sympathetic—and the sympathy between things will be much greater and more forceful—the closer the spirits of those things (whether present or scattered) are in nature and kinship <note>original: "consanguinity"</note> to one another. For example, if both things are of the same source or substance in number, or are individuals of the same species, they will sympathize across a distance <note>original: "ad distans"</note>. Thus, the *Uznea* <note>a moss-like growth found on the skulls of the dead, highly valued in Paracelsian medicine</note>, fat, or blood of one man sympathizes with another from afar. Similarly, the lodestone of one mine may harmoniously affect the iron of another at a distance. 

I told you before the true reason for this, both the fundamental and the immediate cause: namely, that both natures belong to one divine influence. They proceed from angelic beams or an emanation sent forth from one and the same star—whether a "fixed" star of the firmament (the eighth sphere) or an "erratic" planetary star. As I mentioned, there is not one animal, vegetable, or mineral on the earth or in the seas that does not have a specific star pouring its unique influence upon it, both to produce and generate its kind, and to sustain it in essence. 

Now, each angelic nature has its assigned beams from the fundamental emanation of a divine attribute, which conveys them to its designated starry storehouse. From the "Olympic spirits" of that star, the influence is sent down to the spirits in the elements, who act as inferior ministers. These operate according to that very same nature in every species and every individual. 

For example, the stars in the **Ram** or **Aries** of the Zodiac have the greatest influence over similar cattle on the earth; the **Scorpion** over creeping things; and the **Crab** (Cancer) over sea creatures. We find by experience that if a crab is harvested when the Sun and Moon join together at the same degree as the great star in the celestial *Crab's* claw <note>likely referring to the star Acubens</note>, it possesses great virtue and power against poison. If it is collected at another time, it will have very little effect. 

Again, we must note that each fixed star or constellation of the Zodiac has its own planet whose "house" it is; this planet joins in strengthening and altering that influence. The different positions of other planets in relation to it cause a variety of effects, even in the sperm of the same animal, the seed of the same plant, or the secret spirit of the same metal. Nevertheless, they sympathize in nature more or less, depending on how the beams of each planet allow them to align. If the alignment occurs between friendly planets of the same "triplicity" <note>a group of three Zodiac signs belonging to the same element: fire, earth, air, or water</note>—where their houses belong to friendly elements—then the sympathy will be even stronger.

### Section 2. Mosaicall Philosophy.

*The life and spirit of the world proceed through the very rays of the stars, which cannot be investigated by us other than by experience and conjecture. Therefore, you must know that every single thing moves toward its like and inclines toward itself according to its whole power:* <note>original Latin: "vita spiritusque mundi, per ipsos stellarum radios proficiscuntur, quae à nobis non aliter quam experientia, & conjecturis indagari possunt. Scire ergo debes quod unaquaeque res movet ad suum simile & inclinat ad seipsum secundum totum posse suum:"</note> 

The hidden properties in things—which are not implanted in them by their basic physical nature <term>Elementary nature</term> but descend from heaven—are hidden from our senses and scarcely known even to our reason. This is because they are derived from the life and spirit of the world through the beams of the stars, which we cannot investigate or discover in any way other than through experience, and even then only by conjecture or guesswork. 

You must therefore know that every thing moves toward its like, and by all possible means inclines toward itself. By this, the author argues that the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> angelic spirit—which gives life to the world and whose more divine part contains the **Sephirotic** power <note>referring to the ten Sephirot or divine emanations in Kabbalah</note> or virtue of all the divine attributes—is the main actor. This spirit (which, as Ezekiel testifies, contains the virtues of the four winds) operates through its various subdivided emissions of differently conditioned beams. It works in and through its "starry organs" to produce all these hidden and occult effects below. 

These effects are beyond the capacity of a common man’s understanding, even though we find through their effects that things are indeed so. There is not a single beam emitted from this spirit that does not have a secret, predetermined action. These actions vary from one another no differently than the effects we observe through experience. 

For whatever was originally decreed in the secret counsel of the **Archetype** <note>the original model or divine mind of God</note> is carried out from a general plan into many specific forms, and from each specific form into an infinite number of individual particulars. Thus:
*   The eternal or angelic effect <term>æviall</term> <note>referring to the "Aevum," the state of existence for angels that is between time and eternity</note> is the image of the eternal **Idea**.
*   The temporal world is the likeness of the angelic world.
*   In the temporal or symbolic <term>typicall</term> world, every stellar shape is the pattern of an angelic **Idea**.
*   The physical <term>Elementary</term> things are the shadows of the spiritual shapes or images in heaven.

Therefore, just as God sends out his emanation—which is his image—into the angelic world in a diversity of fashions and many different respects, so the angelic spirits send out their various different lights to each other. Every higher order sends light to its inferior, and every upper sphere to the spheres below them. This continues down to the stars, which also apply their lights to one another through various alignments <term>aspects</term>, infusing them into and upon all creatures by degrees downward, even to the very center of the earth. 

These creatures, following the manner of their heavenly pattern, also shine forth toward one another with beams that are either **sympathetic** and harmonious, or **antipathetic** and discordant. We should not doubt that such agreeing and disagreeing beams exist here below, seeing as we observe an opposition of properties even in the fountain of unity from which all things flow—namely, a negative refusal <term>privative Nolunty</term> and a positive will <term>positive Volunty</term>. 

Furthermore, we should believe that the passive spiritual matter of the world’s soul is the subject through which the divine virtue works. Within this matter, the divine virtue stirs up loving and positive (or good and sympathetic) passions by plentifully pouring out its positive and life-giving beams. This adds delight and joy, fulfilling the spiritual appetite of the created matter so that it forgets the dark nature bestowed upon it at its birth by its parents: **Mother Chaos** and the divine power. Instead, it is converted into a **child of light** by adoption. 

In this state, the creature sympathizes with those golden showers of charitable and life-giving light sent down from the benevolent attributes of God. It begins to hate, dread, and loathe all those negative influences poured down from the severe, unhealthy, and destructive attributes—just as light flies from darkness. Being delighted by the presence of more light and life, it avoids and hates the presence of its contrary: death and evil. 

From this it follows that the "children of light"—those who are grafted into this universal illuminated spirit—flee from the "children of darkness" and their works as if from a plague. The reason is that this "moist created spirit," having now found the pleasure, will, and happiness of its illuminated state, is afraid that the negative beams of darkness (the dismal emanations of God’s wrath) might dim its light and obscure the brightness of life. That is to say, it fears they might turn its sympathetic passions of joy and gladness into antipathetic storms of sadness and mourning by pulling the beautiful emanations of joy and love from the outer edges <term>circumference</term> back into the center of the spirit. This would deprive it of that healthy and lively radiance of love and life caused by the hiding of God’s face, which he had previously shone from the center to the circumference of the creature.

Because of this, the sun lost its beauty and became dark, contrary to the common course of nature. Thus, the pleasant sympathy which it produced by its presence—both for the creatures below and in the heavens above—was changed entirely into antipathy for a time. This was a "negative passion" in the heart of the great world, or, as one might say, a fainting <note>original: "Syncope"</note> or swooning of the world, occurring when **Eloah** <note>Hebrew: a name for God</note> chose to stop pouring out his influence of beauty through the gate of **Tiphereth** <note>Hebrew: "Beauty," the sixth Sephirah in Kabbalah, often associated with the Sun</note>. 

Also, that palpable darkness which happened in Egypt was a negative passion, caused by God hiding his face or by contracting the beams of light within himself. Such negative passions are also threatened against the Sun, Moon, and stars toward the end of the world. For if the world was made by the sending forth of God's bright emanation (for by the Spirit of the Lord the heavens were adorned, as Job tells us), it follows that by taking it away, all will return again to darkness and plain nothingness or deformity, just as it was before. 

But this production of good and sympathetic passions—by emitting light from the center to the edge—and the effects of antipathetic passions—which oppose the harmony and sympathy of life—is excellently described by examining the vital actions in man. Generally, two distinct active virtues are noted in man's spirit. The first is voluntary, which is the master over the other; it commands and moves the inferior actions, just as the divine angel **Metatron** <note>In Jewish mysticism, the highest angel who governs the outermost sphere of heaven</note> does in the **First Mover** <note>original Latin: "Primum mobile," the outermost sphere of the universe that moves all others</note> of the great world. This is linked to the **Will** <note>original: "Volunty"</note>, and by it, he moves the celestial spheres and the world of the elements. 

In the same way, in the human structure <note>original: "Microcosmicall Fabrick"</note>, the first mover is that divine mental beam which is the head of man's soul. The other kind of action is involuntary, because it is commanded by and rules according to the will of the intellectual or rational beam. This is no different than how all the lower spheres are forced to move according to the will of the mover in the *First Mover*. Thus, the vital action in man is one of those branches that is involuntary. It is subject to the will of the mental beam in the same way the starry heaven is commanded by the Imperial Spirit. (The starry heaven is the seat of life, because the Sun, which is the heart of the world, resides there.)

Now, we find that according to the will of the Divine essence poured out into the heavens (and consequently here below), joyful and compassionate effects spring from the expansive <note>original: "dilative"</note> property of **Unity** to recreate and stir up pleasure in the creature. We also find sorrowful and sad outflows proceeding from the contracting virtue, by which God hides the face of his kindness from his creatures. Because of this, both desiring <term>concupiscible</term> and hateful or angry <term>irascible</term> passions are caused in the world. 

We find this manifested both by experience and by the observations of the most learned in medicine and philosophy: the vital action, which is ruled by the mind of the superior Will, is either opened and enlarged by the expansive property of the first mover's will—thereby opening the cabinet of the heart to produce those good passions in the vital spirit which sympathize with life and light, namely gladness, hope, confidence, love, mercy, and friendliness—or it is contracted. Through contraction, the spirits are gathered together in the heart, which creates bad, negative passions in the vital spirit. These antipathize with the good passions that rejoice and comfort life. These passions are called "antipathetic" because they are wholly contrary to the nature of those which are good. This group, proceeding from the heart's contraction, includes sadness, care, despair, fear, hatred, anger, fury, bashfulness, and so forth. 

So, just as in the former case the spirit looked up toward the Fountain of Light through expansion and rejoiced to see its pleasures, in the latter case, the spirit was forced by contraction to be deprived of the vision of light. It was forced to look downward into the abyss of darkness and to participate in its dark passions. And by this deciphering and opening of the two opposite passions in the

For example, the lodestone <term>a naturally magnetized piece of iron ore</term> is to its mother earth as man is to the whole world. For this reason, man is called the "Son of the World" by Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary father of Hermeticism</note>, just as Cardanus, Giambattista della Porta, Dr. William Gilbert, and others have described the lodestone as the child or son of the earth. I say that we find in the lodestone all the passions—both sympathetic and antipathetic—that affect its mother earth. It has its poles in alignment with the earth's, it avoids anything that is not in conformity with the earth, and it flies from that which is contrary to its nature. Again, it sympathizes with that which is like itself. It has its equinoctials, colures <note>circles on the celestial sphere passing through the poles</note>, meridians, and tropics, just as the earth has. In conclusion, this suggests not only a physical sensation in its motion but a kind of reason in its actions: namely, its refusal of what is contrary to it, and its embracing and desiring of what agrees with its own harmony. This will be explained in greater detail in both the second part of this present book and in the magnetic experiments which shall be set down in the third or last book of this treatise.

To conclude, the way this mental beam <note>the divine spirit or intellect within man</note> receives the commands or influences <note>original: "influxions"</note> of kindness or severity from above is expressed in my previous discourse: namely, by the permitting of evil spirits of darkness to rule and have dominion, or by helping the good spirits to carry out their offices of joy and delight. Behold, here is contained the sum of all mystical and hidden sympathy or antipathy in the world. Because of the depth and difficulty of investigating this, some people rightly attribute it to the secret actions of an angelic power, which is a middle power <note>original: "vertue"</note> between God and the created world. For this reason (as was said before), an angel is defined as: "As it were a middle power between God and nature, by which certain operations are effected in things, which their nature (that is, their elementary form) would not produce, or at least would not produce in that way; which some say arises from a hidden <note>original: "occult"</note> property, and others say simply 'because it is so'" <note>original Latin: *Tanquam inter Deum & Naturam virtus media, à qua fiunt operationes in rebus quas vel natura eorum non faceret, non vel sic faceret: quas alii provenire dicunt à proprietate occulta, & alii quia tale*</note>.

# The Second Part of this Second Book.
## *In which the Magnetic Nature is truly analyzed, and the reasons for Sympathetic and Antipathetic actions are laid open.*
### CHAPTER I.

*The Author makes a preamble in this Chapter to this his Magnetic Discourse, and then proceeds to the chaos of opinions regarding the origin and attractive power of Magnetic Bodies.*

<image-desc>Decorative initial letter 'I' featuring ornate foliate and scrollwork patterns within a square border.</image-desc>

I showed you in the preceding part of this book the principles and origins of Sympathy and Antipathy. However, because it is not everyone's gift to soar so high at first as to be capable of a theory or speculation that penetrates into God's storehouse or treasury—contained in the hidden depths <note>original: "abstruse bowells"</note> or center of His created nature—I will lower my tone a little for your better instruction and clearer information. I will clarify the hidden subject we have in hand by some common or visual demonstrations, which may guide and persuade people to believe that which might otherwise seem incredible. 

Therefore, so that I may proceed more methodically, I will in this section only lay down the chief foundation on which I purpose to build such experimental conclusions. These shall direct the skeptics—and even those who, through their ignorance, remain stubbornly in their mistaken errors—into the more assured haven of faith and solid belief. As the proverb says, "Experience is even the teacher of fools" <note>original Latin: *Experientia est etiam stultorum magistra*</note>. 

Because the acts of sympathy and antipathy in every thing are brought about by a magnetic power—which acts both to repel by a hateful or angry expulsion <term>irascible: related to anger or repulsion</term>, and to allure and draw toward itself by a desiring attraction <term>concupiscible: related to longing or attraction</term>, as shall be shown to you hereafter—I think it most fit to search out diligently. I will do this with the hundred eyes of Argos <note>Argos: a giant from Greek mythology with a hundred eyes, symbolizing all-seeing alertness</note> or penetrate deeply with the sharp eyes of Lynceus <note>Lyncean optick: referring to Lynceus the Argonaut, famed for sight so sharp he could see through stone</note> into the dark mystery of the lodestone's <term>a naturally magnetized piece of mineral</term> or magnet's nature. This is so we may, with more assurance, begin our practical demonstration of such a secret and hidden contemplation. 

We see that many secret operations are termed "magnetic" because they imitate the active virtues of the magnet or lodestone. These include:
* The operation of the weapon-salve <term>a controversial medicinal ointment applied to the weapon that caused a wound, rather than the wound itself, believed to heal via sympathy</term>, which is so criticized by the ignorant; 
* The extraction of the "mummy" <term>mummy: in this context, the vital life-force or spiritual essence of a living being</term>, both physical and spiritual, out of men or beasts; 
* The transplantation of a creature's vital, sick, or healthy nature into any plant or animal; 
* The manner of stealing the virtue and strength from one animal and infusing it into another; 
* And the secret binding of a plant's spirit with that of a human or any other animal, so that whatever happens to one—such as moisture, dryness, cold, or heat—the other shall also experience. 

Because these are all magnetic, I will bend all my endeavors to create an open passage toward the "anatomizing" <note>analyzing by taking apart</note> of all those mysteries. I will do this by unpacking the spiritual bundle of the lodestone to look into the fountain of its formal, interior, or central and essential actions, and to see the grounds of both its repelling and attracting passions. For if we are able to find, by the subtlest use of our reason, the invisible passages and lurking places of these forces, and can then observe the precise root of their essences and discover the internal cause of each action, we shall easily conquer and surpass all the rest. This is because things that appear alike in their external effects must surely prove to be of the same kind <note>original: "homogeniall"</note> and identical in their internal and hidden natures, as shall be proved more fully to you.

But alas, why should I, being the least of a thousand <note>original Latin: *minimus Apostolorum*, literally "the least of the Apostles"</note>, presume to make so dangerous a voyage to that unknown island where this hidden magnetic nature dwells, among or in the middle of such dangerous and inaccessible rocks, when so many wise philosophers have failed and wandered

Some do not hesitate at all to stay on the solid earth <note>original: "continent of the earth"</note> but imagine it to be numbered among those stars that have the Sun as their fixed center, around which they move perpetually. Thus, they pretend that the earth has the form of a star, which is very different from the Peripatetic <note>original: *Peripateticall*; referring to the followers of Aristotle</note> view. In conclusion, everyone has an opinion that differs somewhat from the next. To show you that all this is true, I will describe and recite some of their reports regarding this inquiry, which they have recorded after their long voyages in the muddy seas of serious contemplation. They have registered these in their writings as if they were the chronicles or histories of their studious adventures or their speculative and spiritual travels. 

Among these, some soar upwards and call the heavens to witness to confirm their claims; some sail to the far northern <term>hyperboreall: relating to the extreme north</term> mountains, and others to strange northern islands, to find the basis of this miracle. Others send their spirit of inquiry down into the bowels of the earth and find it to be the universal starry form of the earth itself. Some claim the origin springs like atoms out of the stone and the object to be attracted. But among all these rational persons, I dare hardly rank one of another kind; for this man is surely to be numbered among those "Elders" who have traveled in the "ship of fools." Much like another Gryllus <note>original: *Gryllus*; a companion of Odysseus who was turned into a pig and preferred to stay that way, symbolizing someone who chooses ignorance</note>, or like the "eighth wise master of Greece," he claims this virtue is evil magic <term>Cacomagical: related to harmful or black magic</term>, or the work of the devil.

Now, among those who have traveled in their spirits to heaven to find this mystery, one argues that the reason for the direction of the lodestone <note>original: "Load-stone"</note> is to be sought in the tail of the celestial Bear constellation <note>Ursa Major or Minor</note>. He affirms that the power of this starry Bear prevails and has dominion over this stone, and that this power is transferred from it into the iron; this is the view of Marsilio Ficino <note>original: *Marsilius Ficinus*</note>. But I reply that this is not so, because experience teaches us that iron itself has its own poles, just as the lodestone does. Through proper alignment, it will seek out and, by its own natural instinct, turn and direct itself toward the location of its proper poles. Peter Peregrinus <note>original: *Petrus Peregrinus*</note> is also of this opinion; following the rules of Friar Bacon <note>original: *Frier Bacon*</note>, he sought the arguments for magnetic direction from the poles of the heavens. Also, Girolamo Cardano <note>original: *Cardanus*</note> claims the immediate cause of the variation in this stone’s power springs from the rising of the star in the Bear's Tail. Lucas Gaurico <note>original: *Lucas Gauricus*</note> is also of their opinion, but he also includes the influence <note>original: "vertue"</note> of Saturn and Mars in this operation...

...confessing withal that the main constellation in the Zodiac <note>original: "Zodiack"</note> to which this stone is subject is *Virgo*. *Albertus Magnus* <note>a 13th-century German philosopher and bishop</note> says that the lodestone <note>original: "Load-stone"</note> and iron are directed toward the Northern stars, and follow them no differently than a plant called the *Heliotrope* <note>original: "Heliotropion"; a plant that turns toward the sun</note> follows the Sun. *Bessardus* holds a separate opinion, making the pole of the Zodiac the fountain of the lodestone's virtue. Again, the *Conimbricensian* College <note>Jesuit scholars from the University of Coimbra</note> derive the cause of this from a part of the heavens not far from the Pole. But *Martin Cortesius* claims this attractive virtue descends from a place beyond the Poles or the movable heavens.

On the other side, *Gaudentius Merula* tells us that the lodestone draws iron with the intent to direct it toward the North, because it is an order superior to the iron, associated with the constellation of the Bear <note>Ursa Major or Minor</note>. I must confess that beams which are spread out are quick to deliver their "brethren" who are imprisoned, and to direct them to their native home. However, I cannot understand *Merula's* mind in this sense. Others make the heavens in general the fountain of this stone's virtue; for *Paracelsus* says that it is the stars which, being full of the lodestone's power, draw the iron toward them, etc. And this would seem probable, because the iron moves toward its poles even in the absence of the lodestone. *Fernelius* wavers: for sometimes he confesses the cause of this action to be hidden; in another place, he makes the heavens the author. 

*Scaliger*, boring nearer to the point of truth, also assigns to it a celestial cause unknown to himself, averring that terrestrial lodestones are derived not from the globes or mountains of the stars, but from that essential power or essence which was their creator, which reigns in that part of heaven hanging over the Northern <note>original: "Septentrionall"</note> point. And *Plato* seems to adhere to this opinion where he confesses the magnetic essence to be a Divine power. And truly, they speak well, but in such a broad sense that their assertion appears to their disciples, when rightly examined (as I said), to be explaining the unknown by something even more unknown <note>original Latin: *ignotum per ignotius*</note>. For in such general terms, we may say that all things are from God. 

We will come down from our celestial speculations and look at the humility of those who—being too wary and listening overmuch to the proverb, "Do not seek to know things that are too high" <note>original Latin: *Noli altum sapere*; literally "be not high-minded"</note>—have their regard more downward, namely upon the earth and its effects only. Of this rank is *Fracastorius*, who, searching after the reason and beginning of this attracting faculty, imagines that the Hyperborean <note>far Northern</note> mountains, which abound with rocks of this nature, draw these iron-natured subjects toward them. And this fictional idea <note>original: "figment"</note> seems so plausible to various learned persons that they follow it in their astronomical writings, geographical tables, descriptions of the world, and sea-charts or maps; yet, if it were true, they would easily draw toward them all such ships as pass in the Northern Seas. *Olaus Magnus* and some others who follow his traditions say that the attractive force comes from some Northern islands which abound in that magnetic substance. 

But leaving their fancy to the empty wind, I proceed to others. *Lucretius Carus*, a poet of the Epicurean sect, dreams that the attraction of iron is caused by an outflow <note>original: "effluxion"</note> of atoms. For, he says, according to the Epicureans' opinions, just as most subtle atoms emanate and flow out from everything, even so do atoms fly out of the iron as magnetic seeds. By a certain joining <note>original: "coition"</note> of it with the lodestone into the space that is between them, and by the union or complication of both bodies, the iron is drawn, etc. To this sense also *Aphrodiseus, Joannes Costeus, Plutarch*, and even *Thomas Aquinas* incline. Yet indeed they ought to know that no attraction is made by emission from the center to the circumference (that is, by expansion <note>original: "dilatation"</note>), but rather by sucking in and contracting from the circumference to the center. Therefore, the emission of atomic seeds out of the iron can be no reason for its union with or movement to the stone. Instead, it must be the lodestone that must draw the beams or spirits out of the iron: for it appears that the iron does not draw itself to the lodestone, but is drawn to it. 

*Thales* and *Anaxagoras* think that the lodestone has life in it because it attracts a substance like itself, as living creatures do. *Lucretius* and *Orpheus* think there is that sympathy between the magnet and the iron which exists between the male and female; and in this they do not err much. *Averroes, Scaliger*, and Cardinal *Cusanus* would have iron move toward the lodestone as toward its original womb or source <note>original: "Matrix"</note>. *Galen* thinks that it draws by its substantial form. 

And now I must come to the opinion of my renowned fellow or colleague,

# Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

Doctor William Gilbert, known for his magnetic skill and deep search—both theoretical and experimental—regarding this subject, believes that this attractive power in the lodestone <note>original: "Load-stone"</note> springs from formal actions, or original and primary virtues or powers. He concludes that the magnetic force proceeds from a specific or unique form, differing from that formal and specific cause in mixed bodies mentioned by the Peripatetics <note>original: "Peripateticks"; followers of Aristotle's philosophy</note>. Instead, he says it is a certain form which is the proper entity and existence of the starry globes and their homogeneous, incorruptible parts. He calls this the Primary, radical, and astral <note>original: "astreall"</note> Form—namely, the same kind as is found in the Sun, the Moon, and other celestial stars. He further asserts that, in a similar way, there is one in the Earth, which is that true magnetic power <note>original: "Magneticall Puissance"</note> called the "first act" or "vigor." He says this is not derived from the whole heaven, affirming that it is not created by sympathy through influence or hidden <note>original: "occult"</note> qualities, nor is it from any particular star; rather, it has its magnetic virtue from the Earth itself. 

This is the opinion of my learned former <note>original: "quondam"</note> fellow colleague. While I cannot help but commend and extol his pains and industry in researching the practical conclusions of this subject, reason will not permit me to consent to his theoretical foundation or the "root" of the lodestone's virtue. For who can believe that the Earth itself—much less its specific parts—can have any virtue radically from itself, when it is evident that both the Earth and the heavens came radically out of the waters? Therefore, as the heaven was before the Earth, it must follow that the formal virtue of the Earth descended entirely from heaven; consequently, the Earth had no such property from itself. But I will discuss this later at greater length. 

Among the Pagan <note>original: "Ethnick"</note> philosophers, Plato, and among the Christians, Scaliger and Fernelius, believe that the cause of this attraction is Divine and from above; however, they do not explain how or in what manner. Therefore, though they have spoken the truth in general, they seem not to know exactly what they mean by these common words. In particular, I will conclude with the last opinion, which is the most lazy and insufficient of all the rest; it is therefore worthy to be the final and most unworthy part—namely, the tail or waste product of them. Francisco Rueus <note>original: "Franciscus Rucus"; a 16th-century physician and writer on gems</note> expresses great doubt concerning the wonderful property of the lodestone. Because the reach of his capacity can attain no higher than superficial things subject to the senses, he judges all effects beyond his reach to be evil magic <term>Cacomagical: from Greek "kakos" (bad) and "magikos" (magic); referring to dark magic or sorcery</term>. Consequently, he wonders whether the cause of these actions in the lodestone might be an imposture or a subtle trick of evil spirits <term>Cacodemons: from Greek "kakodaimon," an evil spirit or demon</term>. Yet this man is more tolerable than those who boldly assert that the act and wonderful effects of the *Weapon Salve* <note>A controversial 17th-century medical treatment where an ointment was applied to the weapon that caused a wound rather than to the wound itself</note> are evil magic. He does not speak as absolutely as they do; they seem to attribute all hidden effects to the Devil without any further doubt, and so deprive God of His due. This man only questions whether it might be so.

## CHAPTER II.

->*In this Chapter, the Author's opinion regarding the original, intermediate, and immediate action or virtue of the lodestone is explained in detail <term>enucleated: literally "to take out the kernel"; to explain or clarify something difficult</term> and set down at length.*<-

I am sure you remember how, in my previous discourse, I demonstrated that God generally operates all in all. I then showed how the self-same Unity in the Divine essence is manifested in its properties according to the multiplicity of His sacred Will <note>original: "Volunty"</note>. This Will is proved to be manifold because the particular effects of His actions—which are only executed by His Will—are infinite in variety. For this cause, I showed you that ten several denominations or Attributes are attributed to one and the same sacred essence.

...celestial heaven, or sublunary <note>earthly; literally "below the moon"</note> spirit, which is between these two Poles, the middle of which—in Figure 1—the <term>Equinoctial</term> <note>the Equator</note> cuts through, being midway between the two Poles. We find constantly that when the air included in the top of the **matrass** or **bolt's-head** <note>original: "Mattras, or bolts-head"; types of long-necked glass flasks used in early scientific experiments and alchemy</note> is cold—specifically when the northern blasts are sent forth—it will be contracted. Consequently, it will suck or draw up the water. 

Through this, we are taught the reason for the attractive nature found not only in the northern or <term>septentrional</term> <note>northern</note> winds, but also in the **lodestone** <note>original: "Load-stone"; a naturally magnetized mineral</note> and all other things which draw and suck toward themselves by the contraction of air. Namely, they have that property from the power of God’s Spirit, which blows from the north by His angelic organs. By this, it is also made evident why one Pole in the lodestone sucks and attracts from the other: it is due to the continuity of the spiritual axle-tree <note>axis</note>, which is created and animated by one "corner-stone" or essential central spirit. As previously stated, although this spirit has two opposite conditions, it works through many different degrees. Therefore, Solomon terms it **simple** or **unique** <note>original: *simplex* or *unicus*</note> in regard to its divine nature, and **manifold** <note>original: *multiplex*</note> in respect to the fact that it works and operates in a variety of ways. 

For just as it works around the poles of the axis by attracting and sucking toward itself through cold and drought, so it also works around the Equator. As one approaches from the poles toward the Equator, the spirit varies in ten thousand proportions of **dilatation** <note>expansion</note>, due to the manifold degrees of heat which this central Sun of life imparts to the air. 

This is not only manifested in the previously mentioned <term>weather-glass</term> <note>an early form of thermometer that used the expansion and contraction of air to move water in a tube</note>; for we find that the more the heavenly Sun (with its divine central agent) approaches us, the more the external air is expanded by its heat. This, in turn, expands the air contained in the neck of the flask or bolt's-head and drives down the water. That is, it repels the cold of winter, which arrived via showers of rain sent from the south toward its proper pole. 

So we see that just as the nature of the cold pole is to draw or suck toward it by **condensation** (which is caused by contraction, or produced by a <term>Saturnine faculty</term> <note>a quality associated with the planet Saturn, traditionally linked to cold, contraction, and weight</note>), the nature of the hot Equator and its adjacent parts is to expel its opposite by **dilatation** (which is caused by a refining heat). 

This is the reason, as already demonstrated, that the Equator of the lodestone refuses to be joined to the pole; just as, conversely, the pole reciprocally avoids the Equator. This is also the reason why there is such great power of attraction in the pole of the said stone, and why it sucks iron toward it **at right angles** <note>original: *ad angulos rectos*</note>—that is, in a perpendicular manner. Then, the nearer the needle, piece of steel, or iron wire approaches the Equator of the stone, the more slanted its **coition** <note>joining or magnetic attraction</note> or conjunction with the stone will be. So, when it comes directly to the Equator, it will lose all angular contact and lie flat, as it were, on its belly, as you may see by the following true observation.

# Mosaical Philosophy: Book 2

...without the air, because everything lives and exists by breathing (for by that means they suck in the celestial influence). Similarly, the airy element feeds the inward spirit of the earth and conveys all the heavenly influences from above into her body, making her the mother of all minerals and vegetables. I told you before that all inferior things and their operations are the types or likenesses of things above. God animated the Angels, the Angels informed the stars, and the starry demons (or Olympic spirits) send down influences into the winds. The winds then inform the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> element of the air in a four-fold way—that is to say, according to the nature of the four winds. This four-fold information gives or assigns a name to the four elements. 

And although in the universal air there is only one single substance in essence, it varies in nature according to a four-fold condition, based on the will and property of that one Spirit. This Spirit is the only active agent in this metamorphosis, or Protean <note>shape-shifting; from the Greek god Proteus</note> transformation from one nature or form to another, even though he uses angelic and starry organs as his tools. He is said "to ride upon the cherubim and to glide upon the wings of the winds." For this reason, <margin>Ezekiel 37</margin> the Prophet says, *“Come, O spirit, from the four winds, and breathe upon these slain bodies that they may live.”* He did not say, "Come, O spirits," but, "Come, O spirit." By this, he argued that it is only one Spirit which blows essentially from the four winds. Consequently, this one spirit in essence is only one thing, though four-fold in regard to its properties. 

Just as in this archetypal spirit the whole world was ideally divided into poles and portions distinguished by spiritual circles, so also in all the regions of the world, he constantly observes the very same character of position—namely, in the starry world as in the airy, and in the airy as in the water and earth. For in the heavens, the North Pole is pointed at and marked out by the starry character found in the tail of the Great Bear <note>Ursa Major</note>. In the air, it is manifested in that very point from which *Boreas* <note>the North Wind</note> blows, which exactly corresponds to the Pole Star. Again, that the earth observes the very same order in the direction of her pole is confirmed by the turning of the lodestone <note>a naturally magnetized mineral</note> and iron toward the North Star. 

Thus you see that it is only one spirit in essence that "works all in all." I proceed, therefore, to my demonstration, which is so familiar to every person that no one in their senses can deny it. I am sure no man can be ignorant that when the North Wind blows, the air is by nature cold and dry. It is therefore converted into the condition and consistency of earth—namely, from a clear, transparent, light, subtle, dissolved, and expanded consistency of air into a troubled, opaque or dark, heavy, and contracted substance. Experience teaches us that it is transformed <note>original: "transmuted"</note> into snow, hail, frost, and ice; <margin>Psalm 147:16 and 148:8</margin> that is, from an airy spirit into an earthly and solid body; from an invisible and mobile state into a visible and fixed disposition. 

In conclusion, the whole air is changed into a spiritual and physical earth. This transformation comes from that cold, dry, and attractive form which it borrowed from the Northern wind, or northern <margin>Job 37:10 and 38:22, etc.</margin> property of the divine Spirit. This Spirit orders all things and alters them from one form to another "by the breath of his nostrils" (as the Scriptures speak allegorically) or by those windy emissions or angelic emanations which it sends from the four corners of the earth. So, by his breath from the North, he exercises that property in the lower world by which he draws or attracts from the circumference to the center. In this way, he congeals, thickens <note>original: "inspissateth"</note>, and hardens soft spirits by the contraction and squeezing together <note>original: "coarctation"</note> of those parts which before were porous and expanded.

How could such a motion toward the center be made?"

For when God will not show the light of his countenance, he reflects his light into himself; that is, he withdraws it from the circumference to the center and leaves only darkness to the creatures. ## Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

The property of God is opposed to those parts of the world and to all such creatures that derive their life from a natural heat. This heat had its beginning from God’s benevolent emanation [outflowing]—that is, from the act of unity, through an emission or dilation [expansion] from the center to the circumference; I mean, from unity into many. It follows, therefore, that although the emission of winds from the north is direct, their essential property—proceeding immediately from God’s angelic instrument—is contracting and attracting from the circumference to the center. This is because it is an emission which, by the divine Spirit’s emanation and action in the nature of Elohim <note>original: ELOHIM; a Hebrew name for God often associated with the power of creation, judgment, and the laws of nature</note>, is cold, dry, coagulating, or congealing, and prone to rest. It is therefore opposed and resistant to the nature of the air, because the air is hot and moist, and is consequently animated by the dilating action which the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> spirit sends or breathes out of the celestial Sun and other life-giving stars, such as *Jupiter* and *Venus*. 

For this reason, it follows that when the Northern <note>original: "Boreall"</note> spirits are sent forth into the air, it must necessarily happen that, at the opposing contact of these cold spirits, the natural heat or life of the air flees or withdraws itself from its circumference to its center. This is caused partly by that contracting motion within itself, brought about by *antiperistasis* <note>original: *antiperistasin*; a philosophical concept where a quality is strengthened by being surrounded by its opposite, such as heat being concentrated in a cellar when the outside air is cold</note> (due to the meeting of its contrary), and partly by the mingling of a new earthly form. Thus, it is congealed and falls to the earth as if it were dead because it is immobile, taking the form of snow, hail, frost, and ice. 

In like manner, we see that the airy life in other creatures—whose formal being consists of God’s expanding property—is forced to flee from the circumference to the center, leaving the external parts chill, cold, and prone to a deadly freezing or lethal rest. We observe this not only in animals but also in plants, seeing that their blood (as I may call it) or vital sap <note>original: "vitall suck"</note> is congealed by the winter and northern cold and is, as it were, lifeless, until it is dissolved and melted again by the life-giving and expanding force of the ensuing Vernal [Spring] or Southern <note>original: "Australly"</note> power, and the severe bond or icy knot of the northern nature is undone. 

For this reason, you may discern that there is but one universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> element, which is partly vulnerable <note>original: "obnoxious"</note> to the depriving and dark contracting (and consequently attracting) property of God's Spirit, and partly capable of receiving his positive and light-expanding nature. This common subject is the spirit or air of the world below the moon. By a lesser thickening or contraction caused by the west winds, it is made water; by more compression and constriction caused by the northern and winter blasts, it becomes snowy or icy earth. Conversely, by lesser expansion and refinement it is made airy or vaporous, caused by the spring season and the south wind; and by a greater thinning and elevation, it is made fire by the dominion of such spirits as are sent out from the east and the summer's heat. Both these main, two-fold, divided properties belong to one and the same Spirit, as was previously related. 

Truly, this general observation can deceive no one, since even irrational creatures [animals] are moved by a natural inclination either to sympathize and rejoice with the mildness and comfort of the one property, or to flee from and avoid the harsher afflictions of the other, which oppose their nature. 

But to our main business. It is manifest by what has already been said that the northern breath is contracting, attracting, thickening, and prone to darkness, immobility, and rest. The south wind, or rather the wind from the Equator <note>original: "Æquinoctiall"</note>, is contrary in nature to it, being ready to undo all that the north wind did—namely, to dissolve the frozen air (which was made snow, frost, hail, or ice) into water, and water into air; to make transparent that which was dark, and to make thin what was previously thick. Therefore, between these properties there is no more sympathy than I have shown you to exist between the lodestone's equator and its pole. And again, both these opposite natures proceed and spring from one and the same divine and universal spirit, which works all in all, everywhere, and consequently in earth as well as in heaven. This testimony of the true Philosophy clearly confirms and implies:

These alterations are called distinct "Elements" by the Ancients because they could never yet thoroughly determine the essential form of the Elements. 

But if they had well considered the four Elements they spoke so much about—and yet, it seems, understood so little of their essence—or if they had well understood that heaven and earth were made of water and by water through the Word (as Sacred Philosophy <margin>2 Peter 3</margin> teaches us), then they would have also known that the common substantial subject of them all was but one created watery spirit. They would have known that this spirit’s fourfold formation <note>original: "information"; in this context, giving form or shape to matter</note> was effected by one increasing formal essence or Divine Word, acting upon and shaping that universal Element through a fourfold emanation. Thus, the will of one creating Spirit, working through four angels of opposing natures, makes, arranges, or changes this one spiritual watery subject into one element or another every day, according to the Will of the Creator. 

All of this is clearly demonstrated by the weather-glass <note>An early type of thermometer or barometer used to observe the expansion and contraction of air</note>. For the air enclosed within it, through contraction or expansion, converts itself into the form of any of the Elements and is altered according to the nature of the great world's <note>original: "Macrocosmicall"</note> blast or wind that blows. 

Now, one might ask: "Where, then, did the earth and waters that reside permanently here below come from?" I answer that they are the *effects* which the winds—by the Will of God, or the Spirit of God <note>original: ELOHIM RUACH</note>—originally produced. These were first framed out of the air: specifically, by thickening the air by one degree into water, and solidifying it by another into solid and fixed earth. This appeared during the third day of Creation, where it is said that *the dry land appeared out of the waters* <note>original: "Aridum apparuerit ex aquis"</note>. 

The Divine Philosopher *St. Paul* confirms all this when he affirms *that we ought to believe by Faith that those things which are visible were first made from things invisible and unseen* <note>A reference to Hebrews 11:3</note>. Furthermore, if the two lower bodies [earth and water] did not gradually and imperceptibly resolve themselves back into air, it would be impossible for the earth or water to contain the abundance of water, stones, and brimstone (caused by lightnings and the like) that falls from the air. Yet we see that neither the air, water, nor earth are ever found to be larger than their usual natural proportions. 

By this, I have sufficiently explained to you the attractive and contractive property of the Northern Pole in the air. This implies that since Northern blasts are enemies to life—because they contract from the circumference to the center, which is contrary to the action of human life—all things reduced to a chill, cold, and Northern property (whether airy, watery, or earthy) draw things strongly toward them. This is proved by the weather-glass: for the air inside, being animated by the effects of a strong and persistent North wind, sucks and draws the water upward—namely, from the "Equinoctial" point of the glass toward the Center of the North Pole (represented by the head of the flask <note>original: "mattras"; a round-bottomed glass flask used in chemistry</note>). 

By the same reasoning, congealed spirits in any earthly substance suck or draw from the exterior to the interior. We observe this when Armenian Bole <note>original: Bole Armoniack; a reddish clay used in medicine and alchemy for its astringent properties</note> sucks moisture into itself, as does all other earth when it is thoroughly dry. This is because, being of the quality of the North, it strongly sucks and draws in watery moisture due to its dryness.

The Pole Star has a similar relationship to the loadstone as the loadstone has to iron, which is its like. But when it is committed to the earth, and the earth has loosened its bonds through decay <note>original: "corruption"; in early science, the breakdown of a seed was seen as a necessary stage for new life to be released</note>, its spirits suck down the sunbeams and celestial influences of its fixed constellation and wandering planet in great quantity. Experience teaches us that the enclosed celestial form or vital beam creeps upward out of the earth, tending with all its appetite toward its ethereal native home from which it came. However, because the element of fire is right next to the ethereal spirit, it will not permit these ethereal or sunny beams to ascend without it. Again, the water claims the very same privilege—namely, to ascend with the air. But because the earth is heavy <note>original: "ponderous"</note> and cannot ascend, she holds the spirit fast below and will not permit it to soar higher. And so those "beamy" spirits, which seemed to descend for the freedom of their brothers, are detained by these elemental ties—or rather, by the fourfold disposition of one Element—and made to hover and hang in the air. There, instead of flying upward to heaven, they multiply into many grains of corn. 

I have noted by my own experience—specifically by analyzing <note>original: "anatomizing"</note> corn with the "fiery knife" of distillation <note>A chemical process of heating a substance to separate its components</note>—that the "female" principle in corn, which sucks down the celestial influences of a similar nature, is a pure volatile salt of a refined or airy-terrestrial condition. It is rich in celestial fire and therefore made volatile and airy by the union of both extremes. It is this "female" principle that magnetically allures and draws down beams from above, holding them fast to multiply its own nature, much like a fowler who uses a captured bird to lure others of the same kind into his nets. 

As for the female mineral nature, because its body is more compact and does not decay, it sucks toward it for the very same reason—namely, by the attractive power of its astringent <note>original: "stiptick"</note> and attractive salt—the essential beams of iron from afar, as if they were of its own nature, to solace and redeem its spirits. Consequently, along with the spirit, it also sucks in the masculine body, since the one cannot be easily divided from the other. Once it has them, it retains them, partly for consolation and strengthening <note>original: "corroboration"</note>, and partly to multiply its own essence. 

Therefore, those philosophers are mistaken who claim that the loadstone <note>A naturally magnetized mineral; a magnet</note> does not secretly feed upon the formal spirits of iron. Yet it nourishes "formally"—that is, it multiplies in its formal essence, even if it does not increase in material substance or quantity.

This is caused by an antiperistatic <note>original: "antiperistaticall"; the intensification of a quality when surrounded by its opposite, such as heat concentrating in the center when surrounded by cold</note> reverberation and contraction, triggered by the penetration of the Northern cold.

Its movement is therefore more formal than material. <note>original: "formall than materiall"; Fludd is arguing that iron's natural magnetism is a result of its internal "spirit" or "form" rather than its heavy physical "matter."</note>

I conclude, therefore, based on what has already been said, that two similar things which belong to the nature of the Equinoctial <note>original: "Æquinoctiall"; the Equator</note> and the temperate zone, attract and embrace one another through a sympathetic emission of beams from the center outward to the circumference. Such is the love of those creatures that live by the property of a positive emanation, such as animals, which have a hot disposition (whether dry or moist). These do not visibly draw one spirit into another, but rather work through a union made by the coming together of lights after their formal beams have been emitted. These have a relationship to the property of the spirit that issues from the east and south winds, whose natures are to expand from the center and therefore not to contract from the outer edges.

Contrariwise, two similar natures that embrace the property of the Poles and the cold Zones attract and hug one another by contraction—namely, by sucking and drawing each nature from the circumference toward their center. We see this when a Loadstone, divided in the middle, will draw and suck the other part back to itself until both parts are perfectly joined together at the very place (or "equator") of their division. In this same fashion, the attractive affection is created between iron and the Loadstone, which are creatures subject to **Saturn**, **Virgo**, and the **Pole-star**.

The chemical <note>original: "Chimycall"</note> perspective does not vary much from these physical and astronomical assertions of ours. In conclusion, we shall perceive that their mixture is achieved in this manner: The Mercurial liquor—of a stony, earthly, or Saturnine nature—was still in its "first matter" or shell, as it were. Being a near neighbor to the "Mercury of Mars" (for these two natures are most commonly found near and in each other's company), it acquired a slight transmutation. Thus, they appear to be joined together by a tight, direct, and almost continuous union. So, the composition achieves an existence halfway between the nature of a Martial metal and a Saturnine stone; it may well be termed a **Mercury** metamorphosed by halves, or a kind of hermaphroditic Saturnine-Mercury. I may well presume to compare the Loadstone in its disposition with Man, considering the admirable virtues and dignity of the one in the animal kingdom, and the miraculous operations and mystical properties of the other in the mineral region. As for Man (for the sake of his dignity, I will speak of him first), there is such a super-eminent and wonderful treasure hidden in him that wise men have judged that the perfect wisdom of this world consists in the knowledge of a man’s self—namely, to find out that secret mystery which lurks within him. 

For man is said to be the center of every creature, and for that cause he is called the *Microcosm* <note>original: "Microcosmus"; the "little world"</note> or the little world: *the center and miracle of the world* <note>original: "Centrum & miraculum mundi"</note>, containing in himself the properties of all creatures, celestial as well as terrestrial, and consequently those of the Loadstone. He is *the Temple of God* <note>original: "Templum Dei"</note>; *the Body of Christ* <note>original: "Corpus Christi"</note>; *the Dwelling Place of the Holy Ghost* <note>original: "Habitaculum Spiritus sancti"</note> (as the Apostle has taught us). Neither truly may it be imagined that God would make choice of an unworthy dwelling place. 

And therefore, in consideration of this, and in our inquiry after so great a mystery, we need to proceed with our most exact discretion and judgment, moving from the visible things of man to the invisible; that is, to penetrate with the sharpest edge of our wit by demonstrating from effects back to causes <note>original: "à posteriori"</note>, or from the external man into the depths of his secret, mystical, and internal being. 

Therefore we proceed thus: seeing that Man is rightly reported by *Hermes* to be the Son of the world, just as the world is the Son of God, being framed after the image of the Archetype <note>the original model or divine pattern</note> (for which cause he is termed the "little world"), it will be necessary to understand that he is likewise divided into a heaven and an earth, just as the great world was. Consequently, he contains within himself his heavens, circles, poles, and stars no differently than the great world does. 

And also, just as we find that the spiritual image of the heavens, with their circles and poles, are delineated also in the earth and every part of it (as appears in the Loadstone and Iron), so the character of the inward man is deciphered and portrayed in the outward man—no differently than we may judge the fashion of the sword by the scabbard, or the kernel by the shell. 

Concerning the research or inquiry after the world's poles within man, no small difference has arisen among the Philosophers. *Pythagoras*, *Plato*, and *Aristotle* have ordained the eastern part of the world to be man's right hand; their reason is because the daily <note>original: "diurnall"</note> motion of the heavens, which proceeds from the *First Mover* <note>original: "Primum mobile"; the outermost sphere of the universe in Ptolemaic astronomy</note>, is effected from east to west. Consequently, the west must be his left hand, or sinister portion. In placing man according to this position, his face must look toward the north, and his back toward the south. But

It follows, therefore, that man's right hand, or right side, must face the south, just as his left hand faces the north. All of this is all the more apparent because it agrees and harmonizes with philosophical reason. Indeed, it even causes the heart to suffer the effects of fainting <note>original: "syncopes"</note> and palpitations.

Conversely, Form (being derived from Light) is busy with expansion <note>original: "dilatation"</note> and therefore with the animation and stirring of Matter, which would otherwise be put to sleep <note>original: "sopified"</note> and essentially killed by its mother’s Northern cold. For that reason, its greatest power of attraction lies at its Pole. 

A living man's attraction, however, proceeds from an expansion of living heat from the Center to the circumference. This causes the material instruments—designed for attraction, retention, and expulsion—to perform their duties. Yet sometimes it operates mainly through contraction (moving from the circumference to the Center) when it receives, by God’s permission, the beams of a privative emanation. This happens when the heart is contracted, leading to "bad" passions such as sadness, melancholy, despair, envy, fear, and the like, as we have mentioned before. But conversely, it expands itself from the Center to the circumference when it wants the animal spirits to stay awake and perform their functions.

The loadstone greedily sucks or draws them in by means of its own internal, earthly **Martial spirits** <term>spirits associated with the planet Mars, which traditionally governs iron and magnets</term>, even into its very center. By attracting the iron’s formal beams, the loadstone draws the entire body of the iron that possesses that starry or Martial influence. In the same way, a strong magnet acts as a female toward a weaker one. 

It is no different with a living man and the dead corpse of another. For although many bodies appear to be dead, the natural magician knows that within the flesh and bones there remain wonderful spirits. These spirits perform wonders no less significant—and indeed far greater—than those of the loadstone. 

Therefore, I would advise every self-conceited person, who is so quick to feel envy toward the mysteries of God in nature, to learn more discretion and experience. They should do this before they so vaingloriously judge the strange and marvelous effects of man's royal nature, and before they pronounce so boldly, without hesitation or doubt, that there are no spirits in any amputated limbs or parts of a man, nor even in a dead corpse. This is what **Casmann** <note>Otto Casmann (1562–1607), a German philosopher</note> and **Foster** <note>William Foster, a parson who attacked Fludd's theories on the "weapon-salve"</note> assert—claiming that even the Devil himself cannot bestow any spirits upon them. 

I want both these men and other reckless and bold judges to know that just as the loadstone (though appearing to be a dead mass) is observed to suck and draw the beams and body of another loadstone into its center with a lively appetite—and just as every piece broken off from a loadstone will do the same in its own proportion—even so I can prove it. I can confirm by a visual demonstration that by a proper application of the fleshy parts of a dead man’s corpse to a living man (if the contact is long), it will make the living man faint and feeble. However, a short while after that material or physical magnetic **mummy** <term>in 17th-century medicine, "mummy" referred to the vital essence or "balsam" extracted from a body</term> is removed, he will regain his usual strength. 

Furthermore, lest this account seem like a fiction or a groundless fantasy to Mr. Foster and the rest of his **Cabalistic** <note>here used dismissively by Fludd to mean mystical or secretive</note> sect—for he might claim that the application of the object only works on the living man's imagination, causing him to persuade himself he is faint without any true cause—I answer: it will suck or draw forth the "spiritual mummy" from the living man in a visible manner. 

Because of the coldness of the dead part, the extracted spiritual mummy will condense itself on the surface of the physical magnet, just as air condenses into a cloud or a cloud into **manna**. In this way, it may be gathered and converted into a very precious and wholesome **panacea** <term>a universal medicine</term> (provided the person from whom it is extracted is healthy and of a good complexion). Conversely, it may prove to be a corrupt and **antipathetic** <note>harmful or repulsive</note> medicine if the body from which it is drawn is infected with any venomous or contagious disease—namely, the **French pox** <note>syphilis</note>, **plague**, **leprosy**, and such—as will be explained more fully in the next book. 

Now, the reason for this action in the dead man’s magnetic parts is this: when the body was alive, it was animated by light and enjoyed all the properties of light. That is, it was hot, active, mobile, and expansive—in short, it was in a "Southern" or **equinoctial** <note>equatorial; associated with heat</note> condition. Once the natural fire is extinguished, it takes on the properties of darkness. It is killed by cold and becomes congealed, latent, fixed or immobile, and contractive. In fine, it takes on the nature of the frozen poles and the rigid zones. 

So, whereas before, while it lived, it emitted its beams from the center to the circumference and enjoyed the blessings of God’s life-giving and positive **emanation** <note>a flow or radiation from the divine source</note>, it now takes on the condition of His contracting, depriving, and mortifying emanation. And yet, I would not want wise men to think that because a living body is turned into a dead corpse, it is therefore void of all spirits of life. The Scriptures confirm that the "incorruptible spirit is in all things," and consequently, it is in those things that are dead as well as those that are alive. ### Mosaic Philosophy. Book 2.

...the variety of its properties in the four winds is sometimes in motion from the center of the thing in which it is, toward the circumference. In this way, he [the Creator or vital spirit] gives life and causes the creature to act and live through a southern or equatorial faculty. So, I say, it operates from the center of the celestial sun to give life to lower creatures. Specifically, it calls forth their incorruptible spirits from their center to their circumference. These spirits were previously driven back by the **boreal** <note>original: "Boreal"; northern or arctic</note> cold into their center during winter. 

This is visible in plants, which seem dead during the winter season because the spirit of life leaves the outer parts of the plant and retreats to the center to escape the assaults of cold, which is its opposite. But when the spirit perceives its fountain of light [the sun] approaching to send help, the spirits begin little by little to spring forth again from the center to the circumference. Being united with the external beams that have come to their aid, they expel dark deprivation and congealing cold from their dwellings. They then proceed to act and grow through vegetation and multiplication, just as we see in corn buried in the earth. 

In the same way—and no differently—the loadstone's **Martial** <term>Martial: related to the planet Mars, which was traditionally associated with iron and magnetism</term> nature, which was originally contracted into its center by a **Saturnine** <term>Saturnine: related to the planet Saturn, associated with cold, lead, and contraction</term> spirit, is stirred up. With similar joy, it sucks in the formal beams of the iron, from whose Martial, sulphurous spirit they originally sprang.

Likewise, the spirits of a dead body are driven by mortifying cold from the outer surface to the center. Resting there without any action, they make the body and every part of it fixed and unmovable. But when these spirits are applied to the living surface of their own kind, they spring forward in their watery spirits toward the circumference (as if they were almost starving in the center). They rejoice to meet their like in the living person, whose own spirit expands and streams out from the pores to assist them. Being partly congealed in the center of the dead limb, they greedily suck in these living spirits along with the **spiritual Mummy** <term>spiritual Mummy: a vital essence or life-force believed by early modern physicians to reside in the body, even after death</term>, which acts as their vehicle, drawing it toward their central home. This serves to endue the part with life as it had before and to refresh it with their presence. 

However, this oily spiritual Mummy—which is full of bright spirits resting upon the surface of the living man—is thickened <note>original: "inspissated"</note> by the cold and mortifying contact of the dead flesh or part of the carcass. It is then congealed and may be kept for private use. 

Can we confirm this better than by looking at the contracting or binding power of the smoky growth issuing from the salt contained in a dead man’s bones? By applying the **Uznea** <term>Uznea: a moss or lichen that grows on the skulls of those who died a violent death, highly valued in "sympathetic" medicine</term> (the mass which grows on dead men’s bones) to the eruptions of blood or **hemorrhages** <note>original: "hæmorrhoigy"</note> in a living man, the warm blood—as if moved by an **antipathetic** <note>original: "antipathe-ticall"; acting through natural repulsion or aversion</note> reaction—returns back and is denied passage by the congealing and binding operation of these northern-influenced growths.

Leaving aside these conclusions regarding the dead man’s magnet and its virtues for a while, what would you say if there were a **microcosmic magnet** <term>microcosmic Magnes: a magnet derived from the human "microcosm," often used in Fludd’s theories of sympathetic healing</term>? This could be selected and gathered from a living man without any harm to his life. Its virtues are strange, both because of its unusual generation—being composed of unlike "parents" and compacted of two different substances, much like a **mule** is—namely, of an earthly **mercury** <note>the fluid or metallic principle of a substance</note> and choleric, sulphurous human spirits. It also acts by attracting the spiritual Mummy out of a living man. 

Even more remarkably, through the **transplantation** <note>the process of transferring a disease or vital force from a human into a plant or animal to effect a cure</note> of it into either animals or plants, it works in a strange fashion, either **sympathetically** or **antipathetically**. I know that this news will immediately be considered "diabolical" by some who are quicker to judge wrongly than to investigate rightly. And why? Simply because it exceeds the scope of their understanding. Yet I know this to be true, and I know those who have put it into practice, much to the wonderment of many. Yes, I know this microcosmic magnet and its use. When it is tested by wise men and well-pondered by them, it will appear as natural as its effects seem strange and its reasoning deep. 

But if what I have said before is well understood and seriously considered, the cause of this will not seem so hidden that it exceeds the limits of nature. I intend, by God’s grace, to discourse more at length on this kind of magnetic action—both sympathetic and antipathetic—in the third and last book of this treatise.

Sect. 2. Mosaic Philosophy.

## CHAP. V.

*In this Chapter is expressed the secret cause why both the **Microcosmic** <term>Microcosmic: relating to the "little world" of the human body</term> and **Macrocosmic** <term>Macrocosmic: relating to the "great world" of the universe</term> **Load-stone** <note>original: "Load-stone"; a naturally magnetized mineral, here used as a metaphor for spiritual attraction</note> operate at a distance, and even unto an unknown dimension or unlimited interval.*

Mr. Foster has sufficiently expressed the shallowness of his Philosophy where he claims that, because the light of the Sun and Stars cannot penetrate thick clouds and **opaque** <note>original: "opake"</note> bodies, the spiritual essence of a man is therefore unable to pierce and penetrate directly in its course without being stopped or hindered by castles, hills, woods, and such things. But had he been a little more deeply learned, or immersed in the depths of true Philosophy, he would have known that the ethereal seeds—the astral influences—are of a far subtler nature than the vehicle of visible light. Indeed, they are so thin, so mobile, so penetrating, and so lively that they are able to (and continually do) penetrate even to the center or inward bosom of the earth without any manifest obstacle or resistance. There, they generate metals of various kinds according to the nature of the influence, as the ancient Philosophers testify. The subtlety of this spirit, according to Plato's mind, is fully expressed by Plotinus in these words: <note>original: "Tanta est Ætheris tennitas ut omnia corpora penetret universi tam supera quam infera, & cum ipsis conjunctus aut implicitus, ea majora minime reddat, quia spiritus iste interior cuncta opera eorum mole minima nullum prorsus augmentum recipiente, alit atque conservat."</note> "The thinness of the Ether is such that it penetrates all the bodies of the universe, both those above in heaven and those below on earth; and when this heavenly substance is joined or entwined with them, it does not make them the slightest bit larger. This is because this inward spirit nourishes and preserves all their workings within their smallest mass, without the substance receiving any increase in size." 

Because of the purity or subtlety of this heavenly nature, the heaven, or *Cœlum*, is called by the wiser Philosophers and mystical Poets the husband to the earth (which they term *Vesta*). Indeed, the very stars of heaven—among which the **Copernicans** <note>Those who follow Nicolaus Copernicus’s model of the universe where the Earth moves around the Sun.</note> rank the earth—are likened to his wife, because they are extracted out of the ethereal substance just as Eve was out of the side of Adam. They are destined to be the densest portions of their spheres, and for that reason, they are considered the members of heaven; consequently, there is nothing so thin, subtle, and piercing as the spirit from which they are derived through condensation. 

This is the reason that true Alchemists tell such wonders of their *Cœlum*, which they call their **Quintessence** <term>Quintessence: the "fifth element," a pure, celestial substance thought to permeate all things</term>, arguing that by reason of its purity and subtlety, it is able to penetrate all things. And the Philosophers say that this is their "nature," <margin>Concerning the Art of Chemistry.</margin> which they define to be: <note>original: "Vis quædam rebus infinita, omnia permeans entia, cunctas generans res, easque augens alensque & ex similibus similia procreans."</note> "A certain infinite power in things, which penetrates and passes through all things, engendering every thing, and increasing and nourishing them, and procreating like things from their like." 

And truly, if you will please consider what I have spoken before, you will remember how I told you that angelic virtue proceeded from the archetypal emanations and are the types of the divine Idea. Furthermore, I said that the ethereal spirit was filled with angelic influences, which had their essential root from God. So in truth, it is not the starry light that penetrates so deeply or operates so universally, but that eternal central spirit. With his divine and irresistible essence, he penetrates all things—both in heaven above, and in the earth and waters beneath. All of this the mystical Philosophers seemed to verify (though darkly) when they called **Saturn** <note>In this context, Saturn represents a foundational or "fatherly" cosmic force.</note>—who was also the father of Jupiter, or the head of the universal emanation—the father of *Cœlum*, or Heaven. By this, they argued that in the sending forth of the spirit of wisdom, he produced, created, or informed the heavens, according to the words of Job: <margin>Job. Psalm.</margin> "You adorned the heavens by your Spirit." And David said: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and by his Spirit every virtue within them." And St. Peter: <margin>2 Pet. 3.</margin> "The heavens existed long ago, and the earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God." It is certain, therefore, that the entire essential action of the ethereal spirit is the divine emanation, or the bright incorruptible Spirit of the Lord.
