# Mosaical Philosophy. Book 2.

The immediate vehicle of such an irresistible and emanating influence must match it in purity and subtlety. This vehicle is the "Informer" (the spirit that gives form and life), who is described by the wise <margin>Wisdom 7</margin> Solomon: *“She is more mobile and subtle than any other thing; she reaches everywhere because of her purity, renewing all things and filling the whole world.”* <note>original: "Omni re mobilior & subtilior & attingere ubique propter suam munditiem, & innovare omnia & implere orbem terrarum"</note> <margin>Wisdom 1</margin> This is what led some of our Christian Philosophers to declare: *“God is Nature, and Nature is God.”* <note>original: "Deus est Natura, & Natura Deus"</note> By this, they meant that the "naturating" <term>naturating: (Natura naturans) the active, creative power of God acting as the source of nature</term> or radical informing nature was the eternal emanation that created and shaped the "humid" <note>original: "humid": referring to the watery, passive primal matter of the world</note> nature of the world. For this reason, the world was called *Natura naturata* <note>Latin: "Nature-natured"; nature as a created object or effect</note>, or the nature which was made natural by the presence of the "Naturating" nature or the Spirit of the Lord. This Spirit moved upon the waters and shared its fiery, life-giving vigor and essence with them—as we find both in Sacred Scripture and in the writings of St. Augustine <note>original: "St. Austin"</note>.

We must therefore conclude, after considering what has been said, that if this influence is completely animated by the incorruptible Spirit of the Lord, it must possess the properties of that Spirit or Divine Nature. Consequently, it must be the most subtle, quick, movable, and penetrating of all spirits. In that regard, it will be able to pass through all solid bodies without resistance. It also has the power to generate, increase, and nourish all things. Once it is "specificated" (incorporated into a specific type of creature), it reproduces similar individuals from their own kind. Furthermore, in terms of our human capacity to understand it, it has an infinite extension and therefore cannot be limited. I intend to prove all of this through experience or visual demonstration in the following way: 

We find in practice that the **loadstone** <note>original: "Load-stone"; a naturally magnetic mineral</note>, by virtue of the subtle spirit that internally animates it, possesses such a potent attractive power that it can transmit the beams of its active influence right through the hardest stones and the most solid, fine-grained wood. It passes through thick plates of copper, tin, silver, or gold. It even penetrates "impenetrable" glass itself and other such dense materials that have no visible pores or openings <term>spiracle: a small breathing hole or vent</term>. This is clear evidence that this spirit is of a far more piercing and subtle nature than the air around us, since air is denied passage through even a thin piece of paper or a bladder. 

In the same way, the inward or celestial spirit of man—which carries this life-giving beam—is so subtle that nothing can resist it when the inward mental beam aims at a target, no matter how distant or inaccessible the physical mind might think it to be. Since this celestial or ethereal spirit in man is made after the pattern of the Divine Image it carries, its actions must also resemble the Divine. <margin>Pimander 4</margin> The subtlety of the Divine act within man's spirit is expressed by Hermes [Trismegistus] in these words: *“Those who rely on this Divine Nature can comprehend with their understanding all things on the earth and in the sea; they can even understand what is in heaven above. They can elevate themselves so high that they may behold the face of Goodness itself.”* <note>original: "Quicunque hac Dei Natura fulti sunt, intelligentia sua cuncta complectuntur quæ in terra sunt, & in mari, & siquid est præter ea supra cælum, atque adeo seipsos erigunt ut ipsum quoque bonum intueantur"</note> 

By this, he means the all-powerful penetration of the mental beam. Through its irresistible action, the celestial influence penetrates and operates through all things without any intermediate resistance. From this, it is evident that every individual creature is endowed with this essential spirit and is founded and built upon it, as if on an essential cornerstone. Therefore, the emission of its beams is not to be limited by a fixed "sphere of activity," as some philosophers—who are more focused on the senses than the intellect—have claimed. Rather, it is an *infinite power in things* <note>original: "Vis in rebus infinita"</note>, and is therefore not finite or restricted. Just as the influence of a heavenly star shines down to the center of the earth, each "terrestrial star" <note>the spark of divine/celestial spirit within an earthly creature</note> can project its influence back to the center of the celestial star from which it originated. ## Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

We see that every astral influence in a creature, by a natural inclination and through sympathy, looks toward <term>aspect: an astrological term meaning to gaze upon or be in a specific geometric relationship with</term> the star or celestial fountain from which it sprang. Likewise, that star in heaven, with a fatherly respect, sends down its influences to feed and nourish its corresponding "filial fire" <note>original: "filiall fire"; the spark of life within a creature that corresponds to a specific star</note> or form in the creature here below. Both of them, through a mutual relationship, rejoice together at the spiritual presence of each other. This is why it is said: *Nature rejoices in nature and contains nature; O celestial nature of truth, multiplying natures by the will of God.* <note>original: "Natura natura letatur & naturam continet ; O natura cælestis veritatis , naturas Dei nutu multiplicans"</note> 

Likewise, each kind or species that is endowed with the same influence sends forth beams of the same nature through a sympathetic consent because of its likeness to another. This creates an harmonious symphony in the meeting of their beams, by which they agree in a union of love. For this reason, the axiom of the philosophers mentioned before runs in this strain: *Nature usually procreates like from like.* <note>original: "Natura ex similibus similia procreare solet"</note> This is the reason why each specific form rejoices in its like and is ready to produce its own kind, and does not usually pass the limits of its kind. For example: a man's nature produces a man, a horse produces a horse, a fennel seed produces fennel, a bean produces a bean, wheat produces wheat, and so on. 

Also, the nature of each created thing is most friendly toward the nature of its like. It sends forth the amiable and sympathetic beams of its affection to join with similar beams emitted from its like, so that both of them easily consent and rejoice in each other. By the contraction of these beams, they endeavor to cause a union. For this reason, the loadstone <note>original: "Load-stone"; a natural magnet</note> rejoices at the sight of its like; for if one loadstone meets another, each will look toward the other by their Saturnine <term>Saturnine: related to the planet Saturn, traditionally associated with lead, weight, and deep internal properties</term> sulfurous spirits and embrace each other. Through their application, they will centrally suck and draw one toward the other with a sympathetic embracing. 

Furthermore, because iron is subject to the very same constellation and has its "central star" corresponding in all points to the loadstone (for which essential kinship they are both found in the same terrestrial vein of ore), they are both observed to entertain and hug one another so lovingly. Experience tells us that the feminine loadstone embraces the masculine iron beyond all measure, like a lustful harlot <note>original: "luxurious harlot"; in this era, "luxurious" meant lewd or lecherous</note>, rather than the iron embracing the loadstone, as Averroes, Scaliger, and Cardinal Cusanus have erroneously guessed. They claimed that the iron moves toward the loadstone as if toward its beginning or the womb from which it came. If that were the case, the North Pole in the iron would move by itself more swiftly toward the Pole Star—which is the fountain of both their central influences—than the magnet would; yet experience proves all of this to be quite the opposite.

Now, to confirm the infinite extension of these central beams between two similar bodies, let us first grasp some theory so that we may afterward better descend into practice. <margin>Al-Kindi, *On Stellar Rays*</margin> *The beam,* says Al-Kindi <note>original: "Alkindus"; a 9th-century Arab philosopher and scientist</note>, *which proceeds from the center of the star to the center of the earth is proved to be strongest in its kind of operation.* <note>original: "Radius... quia centro stellæ ad centrum terræ procedit fortissimus esse probatur in operationis suæ specie"</note> By this, he signifies at what an immeasurable distance the hidden starry beam, or beamy influence, works with and in its image on the earth. For he says elsewhere: *It is manifest that the starry beams create and engender diverse individual creatures in this world.* <note>original: "Liquet quod Radii stellares diversa constituunt individua in hoc mundo"</note> 

Again, regarding the central stars or starry influences of lower bodies and the extension of their beams, he speaks thus: *The elementary world is the image or pattern of the starry world, so that everything it contains comprehends the form or likeness of the starry world. It is evident that everything in this world emits its beams in its own way, just as the stars of heaven do; otherwise, it would not fully take on the figure of the starry world. Indeed, this is made manifest to our senses in some things: for fire sends forth the beams of its heat to nearby places, and the earth sends forth the emanations of its cold.* <note>original: "Mundus Elementarius est exemplum mundi Syderei... ignis enim radios caloris ad loca proxima transmittit, & terræ radios algoris."</note> 

We affirm, therefore—

# Mosaical Philosophy. Book 2.

...therefore, it is certain that everything which has an actual existence in this elementary world <note>the physical world made of the four elements: earth, water, air, and fire</note> emits or sends forth its beams into every part, which fill the elementary world according to their nature. Moreover, the distance of one thing from another makes a difference in the effect of the beams in the things of this world. By this, he makes it plain, first: that there is nothing in the lower world that does not have its counterpart in the starry world, whose beams and influences it receives. 

And again, just as the aforementioned star in heaven darts forth its beams even to the very center of the earth—and therefore has so large a sphere of activity that it searches every place of the vaulted world—even so, and in the same manner, those starry scintillations <note>original: "scintills"; tiny sparks or flashes of light</note> or beaming sparks which it sends down into its subject creature (being one in essence with its fountain, and therefore connected with it and indivisible) search in like manner each angle or corner of the sublunary region. Indeed, it penetrates even to the very celestial fountain from which it is derived, as shall be more clearly demonstrated hereafter; for every portion or small part of a large loadstone <term>loadstone: a naturally magnetized mineral, used here as a primary example of "sympathetic" action</term> has its poles and circles just as the whole does. 

It is made apparent by this that the action of each elementary thing is effected both by the separation of their bodies—that is to say, *at a distance* <note>original: "ad distans"</note>—and when they are joined together by a mutual contact with one another. However, the action of elementary things when they are separated from one another is performed by a fit application and infusion of their beaming influences into each other. This would hardly be believed, because of the hidden nature of the action, if experience did not guide us through the observation of the loadstone’s attraction of iron to itself at a distance. 

We also observe that the images of things are seen far off in mirrors or optical glasses; and it was no small artifice of the Pythagoreans, and some others of our Christian philosophers, to express their minds to friends in far-off countries by reflection, using prepared mathematical glasses directed at the circle or compass of the Moon. 

But unfortunately, our external philosophers—who will only be guided by their physical senses—dream of a certain limited sphere of activity. They ascribe bounds to the action of this mystical nature as they please, or according to what their exterior senses observe. As for example: because the loadstone draws iron only at half the distance of a table, *therefore* <note>original: "Ergo"</note> they think and conclude that the vivifying act of its virtue penetrates or extends itself no further than that distance in the air. Consequently, being led by their bodily eyesight, they limit the loadstone’s spiritual extension according to this external and visible action. 

But if they would duly close their bodily eyes in this inquiry and look as true philosophers ought—searching for such an abstruse action with the gaze of their mental intellect—they would find that the extension of the beaming spirit in the loadstone matches that of its proper celestial star, since they are both of one essence. The same is true for the spirit in the iron, and every scintillation or spark of fire has the properties of the whole, as is said of the loadstone. But there are many things which may hinder the evident effect in the loadstone: namely, the heaviness of the body of the iron, which prevents it from being drawn beyond the circle of the magnet's sensible emanation; and another thing is the dispersing and dilating of the union of beams in the loadstone. For the beams, after they are emitted, are more dispersed the further they pass, as it appears by this demonstration:

Thus, its effect or power is too weak to pull such a heavy object from so far away. 

However, because its celestial star meets and embraces its emissions and strengthens them, it is evident that the Pole Star acts within the loadstone <term>loadstone: a naturally magnetized piece of the mineral magnetite</term> to stir up and animate a similar power within it. Once the loadstone is so energized, it responds to the action of the star, penetrating—by a sympathetic and harmonious agreement—even to the center of its source. This is easily achieved since they are both of the same essence. 

Do we not perceive this to be true through external observation when we notice the northern pole of the loadstone, as if out of natural duty, steadily watching the Pole Star? Even though the star is far from the body of the loadstone, they are close and joined by the radiant affection of a single essential spirit. We can see that this is so by looking at a magnetized needle. Do we not learn from astronomical practice that the distance between these two bodies—the celestial star and the earthly stone—is so vast that we cannot imagine a greater distance? The space stretches between the starry heaven (the eighth sphere <note>in the traditional Ptolemaic system, the sphere of the fixed stars</note> where the Pole Star resides) and the Earth. Yet, we find them aligning and meeting in their aspect, and operating and sympathizing with one another. 

Why, then, must the action of this hidden spirit be limited by some imaginary "sphere of activity" dreamed up by people who have little skill and are far too superficial regarding the hidden treasures and secret <note>original: "arcane"</note> or central actions of God in nature? In the same way, there must be a sympathetic meeting of hidden radiant light between the iron and the loadstone, because they both contain "central stars" or radiant influences of the same nature from the very same source. Only God knows how far these hidden emanations can travel, even if their effects only occasionally appear to our senses—much like the celestial influences that descend from heaven upon minerals, plants, and animals. 

Nevertheless, if we believe historical accounts, we are told by Serapio <note>an 11th-century Arabic physician</note>, Olaus Magnus <note>a 16th-century Swedish writer</note>, and the Moors that in the Indies and toward the North Pole, there are rocks made of this stone that pull ships toward them from a great distance. They even pull the iron nails out of the ships, which is why (they say) those people fasten the planks of their boats with wooden pins instead. 

Furthermore, what should we say about the opinion of Fracastoro <note>Girolamo Fracastoro (1478–1553), an Italian physician and scholar</note>? This learned physician and well-grounded philosopher was not ashamed, after a long investigation into the loadstone's secret nature, to conclude that the reason the magnet points north is that in that corner of the world, there are mountains of loadstone that draw iron toward them. Truly, if that were true, this magnetic rock would be operating over a massive distance—from the equator <note>original: "Æquinoctiall"</note> to the frozen North Pole. After all, sailors use the magnetic needle at the equator to determine their position. While some find this strange, many learned men—skilled in geography, map-making, and describing the world—firmly hold this opinion. This shows us that the "limited sphere of activity" assigned to the loadstone by the Peripatetic <note>followers of Aristotle</note> philosophers and the Christian Scholastic theologians of his school is empty and foolish.

But to move up from minerals to the vegetable and animal kingdoms, we observe an amazing relationship between the fixed stars and the planets, and likewise between different plants, between plants and minerals, and even between animals and plants.

They are observed to turn and follow his daily movement, even on the cloudiest day. Also, the onion, as Plutarch <note>a famous Greek historian and philosopher</note> testifies, turns green and grows when the moon is waning, but withers <margin>Plutarch.</margin> when it is waxing. Furthermore, to express the exceeding sympathetic relation between the nature of plants and minerals, let us diligently observe the hidden <term>occult: hidden or secret; here referring to natural properties not immediately visible</term> property of the hazel tree. If at certain times forked twigs are cut from it, and each prong of the forked branch is held in each hand so that the joint where they meet points directly upward and perpendicularly: if the person holding the stick in this posture passes over a mountain that contains some rich mineral or metallic vein in its depths, the perpendicular joint will forcibly—and regardless of the bearer's will—bow downward toward the earth when the man walks right over the location of the mine. But if there is no mine or vein, it will not move. 

I can witness that this is true myself, as can more than a thousand others who have seen the effect and will justify this claim. Even among us, certain Germans performed the same feat in the silver mines in *Wales*. In *Germany*, it is a common practice in those mountains of *Saxony* and *Hungary* where there are mines of silver and gold. Besides, lest my assertion be doubted by the incredulous, I would have them know that *Georgius Agricola* and *Munster* vouch for this to be true. 

Lord, what a stir the enemy of the weapon-salve <note>weapon-salve: a controversial 17th-century medical theory that a wound could be healed by applying ointment to the weapon that caused it, based on the idea of "sympathy" between objects</note> would make to behold such a sight! What? An unfeeling branch of a tree, consisting of only two twigs, can discover hidden metal? Can it penetrate with its invisible beams more than six hundred fathoms <note>one fathom equals six feet; 600 fathoms is 3,600 feet</note> into the solid earth, through craggy rocks and stony veins? 

"What," they will say, "is it possible that a plant—which is less active, movable, and hot than an animal—should perform this act, when it is impossible (as they claim) that an animal's radiant influence or emanation should pass or cooperate at any great distance with its like, because of castles, rocks, woods, hills, fogs, and such things?" 

Surely they will conclude that this wonder must be done by the act of the devil, or not at all. For if an animal spirit cannot effect such a union of sight at so great a distance, how should the senseless plant move and incline of itself? Such will be the judgments, I know, of those who are apt to judge before the facts are known. In truth, it is that proportioned harmony in all these lower creatures by which they correspond to the celestial bodies—or rather to the divine influences within them. These influences spring from one primary, universal <note>original: "catholick"</note>, and eternal emanation, who immediately infuses his virtuous beams of both sympathy and antipathy into each starry globe. They, in turn, pour them down into this elementary world, causing a harmonious and symphonic

Of all beasts, the elephant also hates and detests the little mouse; if any of the food given to them is eaten or <margin>Pliny, Book 8, Chapter 10.</margin> touched by mice, they will abhor and loathe it immediately. A similar antipathy is noted between the natures of the <term>Catoblepas: a legendary creature from Ethiopia, described by Pliny as having a heavy head always looking down, whose gaze or breath was lethal</term> and the weasel, for weasels are like poison to them. The cock has an antipathetic abhorrence for the fox. <margin>Ibid. 12.</margin> All snakes and adders fear and fly from the ash tree, so much so that they are <margin>Pliny, Book 16, Chapter 13.</margin> careful to keep themselves out of both its forenoon and afternoon shadow. Again, Dioscorides reports that the <term>Taxus: the Yew tree</term> <note>original: "Taxus"</note> is so venomous that if anyone merely sits under it, he is harmed by it, and it often costs him his <margin>Dioscorides.</margin> life. And Caelius Rhodiginus says that the adder is afraid of a naked man. It is well known and confirmed by many authors that the Catoblepas, though it is a very <margin>Caelius Rhodiginus, Book 15, Chapter 25.</margin> small animal, kills with the beam of its gaze from a thousand paces away. Also, one blear-eyed person is able to infect another from afar by the secret emission of his contagious beams. We see that onions draw tears from a person at a distance <note>original: "ad distans"</note> by the emission of their beams. Again, we observe that just as a healthy and sound person commonly embraces his like through a sympathetic affection, so also a corrupted person, through antipathy and at a distance <note>original: "ad distans"</note>, poisons and infects his like. For example, we see that a blear-eyed or ophthalmic <note>related to eye inflammation</note> person infects no member of another person except the eye; and one with <term>phthisical: related to phthisis, an archaic term for tuberculosis or lung consumption</term> <note>original: "Ptyficall"</note>, ulcered, and consumed lungs wounds only the lungs of another, even at a distance, by the application or meeting of two beams of the same nature that are antipathetically affected and poisoned. 

But to return again to our magnetic purpose <note>original: "Magnetick Scope"</note>, which is as much spiritual as it is physical: I say there is such a spiritual respect of sympathy between creature and creature that the beloved, in an admirable manner of attraction, allures and draws the spirit of the lover toward it. I myself have seen this marvelously demonstrated by a water spaniel of my own in France. As I rode by post to Lyon, I lost my valise or mailbag on the way, in which my letters of exchange were kept. Seeking to return, I found my hired post-horse was of such a nature that he would by no means turn and go back. I was then forced to send my dog back to search. After he had been absent for half an hour, he brought the <term>bouget: a leather pouch or bag, from which we get the modern word "budget"</term> in his mouth. This is strange, considering that I was on horseback and he could not discern any of my footprints; nevertheless, he came to the bag I desired, and finding my scent upon it, he brought it back. 

But to come more pertinently to the matter: a friend of mine, being in my company, lost his dog at night. We entered a private house where the dog had never been before, and while we were in a chamber with the door fastened, the dog arrived about half an hour later. He violently scraped and bounced at the door to find his beloved master. From this, it is evident that the beams of the dog's affection did not forsake the master's beams during his absence, but guided him directly to the unknown place until he found him. Is it not also a wonderful sympathetic emanation that the pigeon called the "carrier" makes toward the place or dovecote where he was bred and fostered? For that reason, the bird loves it so dearly that even if he is conveyed 500 miles from his nursery in an enclosed basket, he will fly directly back again with a letter about his neck. This is a clear argument that he is guided justly and straightly by the emitted beam of his affection, which is continued in a spiritual manner with the place he most delights in. What shall we say of two persons, where one loves and feels affection without any reason, and therefore pursues the beloved with the beam of his affection, even though the other altogether abhors or neglects them, failing to respond with similar beams...

This causes the clotted blood to flow and move, as if it would meet and attack the murderer's emitted spirit once more. <note>Fludd is referring to "cruentation," the historical belief that a victim's corpse would bleed in the presence of their murderer.</note> 

Therefore, we must surely admit that where one spirit joins in sympathy with another of the same nature, the power must be even greater, and the action performed over a larger distance. This is clearly shown in the mysterious operation of the **magnetic cure**, which takes place between the weapon (or ointment) and the wounded person. I have spoken much on this topic during that heated debate between Mr. *Foster* and myself, in the book where I was provoked to "squeeze his sponge." <note>This refers to Fludd's 1631 book, *The Squeezing of Parson Foster's Sponge*, written in response to William Foster’s attack on the weapon-salve.</note> Furthermore, in this present treatise, I intend to explain that point even better by comparing the magnetic virtue in humans to that of the **loadstone** <note>a naturally magnetized mineral</note>.

The argument of Mr. *Foster* rests on the supposed impossibility of a healing power operating at such a large distance as some claim. He doubts that living blood can emit its exciting, spiritual beams or influences toward dead or clotted blood. If such an action were truly impossible in the animal kingdom—which is the most expansive and the least restricted by physical bonds—then I wonder why it would not be far more impossible and unfeasible in mineral bodies. Minerals are characterized by a firm and tight solidity, making them more likely to keep their influential beams inside than bodies that are loose and porous. 

Furthermore, the animal body is hot and fiery, and consequently more ready to expand and send its virtue further out; but the mineral is cold, and therefore less active and powerful in projecting its beams. And yet, despite all this, experience teaches us that the loadstone looks toward the North Star and sends its spiritual gaze toward it. Similarly, the star sends its beams down to its northern mineral target from an immeasurable distance, as mentioned before. Since this is the case, why should the "animal star"—derived from its celestial fountain—not also send its beams to the chilled and frozen blood in its "greasy earth" (by which I mean the **weapon-salve**), or to the blood's invisible spirit which has been sucked into the iron weapon by its attractive, sulfurous nature? 

Experience teaches us that even if no physical blood is found on the iron, the wound is still cured through a similar sympathetic gaze if the part of the weapon that caused the injury is anointed. Country surgeons <note>original: "Chirurgions"</note> have tested this when they did not dare to examine the wound with a probe. They found by experience that by putting the weapon into a fire, the specific part of the sword or tool that caused the wound will reveal itself by changing color, looking different from the rest. In this way, they can see how deep the wound is by observing which part of the weapon penetrated the body. 

Therefore, this is a clear argument that bloody spirits enter the wounding instrument. Consequently, it proves that there are essential spirits that flow out of the blood and leave the body entirely. This also demonstrates, against Mr. *Foster*, that if the thicker spirits of the blood are able to pierce through solid steel, then its finer and more subtle spirits are certainly able to penetrate all other things like a spiritual influence, without any resistance. But we will approach our purpose more closely and move our argument from mineral demonstrations to the plant kingdom <note>original: "vegetable"</note>, so that we may illustrate "like with like" regarding our animal subject. I will therefore focus on a grain of wheat. Even though it is dead and rotted in the earth, it is resurrected <note>original: "suscitated"</note> by the beaming influences of the sun. For "like draws like" by a magnetic power, and like rejoices in its like. One thing is revived and quickened—or called out from its rest or center—by its calling, alluring, or embracing "like." By this means, the beaming spark or atom of solar influence inside the grain, which was idle and doing nothing in its center, is stirred up by its external "like" (the sun) to work toward its own delivery out of the elemental mud or slimy bond

It was as if the mineral spirit, which held onto the human spirit, was terrified and stood in awe of the human spirit that struck it, thereby losing its power of attraction; or perhaps the spirits trapped within the metal, which were in harmony with the spirits of the bleeding man, had rejoiced in a kind of revenge taken on the weapon. For know that there is a sympathetic and antipathetic radiation between animals and minerals, just as there is between two animals or two minerals.

But please note a second remarkable observation regarding this point: Sir Bevis Thelwell told me that as a trial, after anointing and wrapping a wheel-maker's ax that had severely wounded his leg, the person—who had been unable to sleep from pain for five nights before—fell asleep immediately after the ointment was applied and was at rest. When Sir Bevis Thelwell saw this, he felt he had to test something he had heard confirmed by many: He opened the anointed ax and scraped off the ointment from one corner of it. Immediately, he was informed that the patient was complaining of a sharp pain, which he felt exactly in the part of the wound corresponding to where the ax had been made bare by scraping. Whereupon he anointed that portion over again, and suddenly the party felt ease. The same experiment was conducted and found to be true by the said Lord, Captain Stiles, and Sir Nicholas Gilbourn.

I can also speak from my own knowledge of a widowed gentlewoman on Bread Street Hill. She had a box of this ointment and cured many of the toothache by pricking the aching tooth with a sharp stick until it bled, and then putting that stick into her box of ointment. Among the rest, one of her neighbors—a quarrelsome woman—asked her for a cure or some ease for her toothache. Her teeth were pricked, the stick was put into the ointment, and she recovered. But within three or four days, she got into an argument with the gentlewoman’s maid and spoke rudely to the mistress. The maid told her mistress all about it. The gentlewoman, being in a playful mood, said she would make her regret it, and went to the box and took out the stick...

Therefore, whatever distress befalls the trapped and congealed spirits on the weapon also happens to the patient's wound, by a kind of "report" or return-echo of the emitted beams.

Again, we must consider that separated blood contains every aspect of the Microcosm <note>original: "Microcosm," the "little world" or man as a reflection of the universe.</note>. This is no different than how a portion of a lodestone <term>a natural magnet</term>, when divided from the whole, still possesses all the proportions of the world—namely the poles, the equator, and so forth—just as the whole does. So, the "Idea" of the wounded limb exists within the spirits of the emitted blood and maintains its relationship to every part of that limb, just as the poles of a piece of lodestone relate to the whole magnet. There is a similar hidden attraction and emission of beams between the small amount of blood outside the body and the entire volume of blood retained in the veins, just as there is between a small cut piece of lodestone and the whole stone. 

I conclude, therefore, that the congealed spirits of the blood on the weapon (or any separated blood) use the shared heat and oiliness <note>original: "unctuosity"</note> of the salve or ointment to ripen and breathe out, little by little, back toward their source. This is just like a spark in a grain of corn: when it is kept and preserved in the "earthly womb" <term>matrix</term> away from the cold, raw air, it aspires upward toward the heavenly Sun. In the same way, the wound heals and mends in the wounded creature little by little. This explains the manner of action between the wound and the weapon-salve. Now, let us say a word or two concerning the interval or distance between the wound and the ointment.

The distance between the Pole Star and a lodestone is unknown, yet one operates upon the other by sending out reciprocal beams upward and downward; therefore, no certain, limited "sphere of activity" can be assigned to their action. The Sun and the spirit in a grain of wheat operate in a similar manner, through a continuation of one and the same nature. Here, too, the idea of a limited sphere of activity is abolished, as no man can accurately determine the extent of the solar influence. The beam within the grain participates in the nature of the Sun, just as a small lodestone cut from a large one has parts, poles, and circles that correspond exactly with the large one. 

Man has a most subtle influence, or vivifying spirit of life, sent down and infused into him by divine inspiration. In this spirit is the property of the "four winds" (as the Prophet *Ezekiel* tells us) and, consequently, the "Idea" of every nature. But the essence of this spirit is indivisible. Therefore, the vivifying spirit sent from God into man has all the properties of the spirit that infused it, just as a smaller lodestone cut from a larger one possesses the property of the greater. Consequently, the spirit of the one is no more divided from the other than the sunbeams can be divided from the Sun. But the Spirit of the Lord fills all things (as *Solomon* says) and makes the scale of His operation in man greater or lesser according to His will. Therefore, it will not admit any such "fantastic limited sphere of activity" as man’s invention—by which I mean the subject of pagan philosophy, which is folly before God—would suggest. 

<margin>Pimander 11. <note>The "Pimander" (or Poimandres) is a foundational text of the Hermetic tradition, attributed to Hermes Trismegistus.</note></margin> For this reason, *Hermes* says, "The soul, being full of Mind and of God, fills the inner parts of the world, embraces the outer parts, and provides life to all things." <note>original: "Anima mente Deoque plena, intima mundi replet, complectitur extima, vitamque hæc omnibus suggerit."</note> The soul or vital spirit, being full of divinity, fills the world and embraces external things; it gives life to all things without; it gives life to the "great and perfect animal" (the world) and breath to everything that lives within it.

...reason; and, to conclude, that wills or refuses <note>original: "willeth or nilleth"</note>. Since this is the case, is it not a sinful thing for ignorant people to claim that the hidden <note>original: "occult"</note> actions of this mysterious <note>original: "abstruse"</note> spirit—by which they live, move, understand, distinguish between good and evil, remember, see, feel, hear, touch, and taste—are the work of the devil? Instead of thanking her for her help, they irreligiously and falsely attribute her secret <note>original: "arcane"</note> operations to the devil. And why, I ask? Simply because they cannot grasp the depth of the power of that spirit by which they themselves live, move, and exist. Furthermore, they try to limit her activity according to their own whims, even though (though they do not realize it) they receive their life and will from her. It is she who limits them as she pleases, for she is infinite in her being, since she is a portion—not divided—of that Divine Emanation which is infinite in its reach.

It is evident, therefore, that this life-giving <term>vivifying</term> Spirit can send its influence toward any target in the world from any specific nature, but especially from the human <term>Microcosmic</term> creature. This is even more effective if the target shares the same nature and involves the "vehicle" of the spirit—namely, shed blood—once the distance between the wound and the ointment is accounted for.

Moreover, we shall find this confirmed by other operations of the soul performed within the same human <note>original: "Microcosmicall Mine"</note> source, from which it emits its beams at an unlimited distance. For example: it is found by experience—and through natural means, without any suspicion of evil magic <term>Cacomagical</term> devices or superstitious tricks—that if the urine of a person who has jaundice <note>original: "Yellow Jaundis"</note> is carried a hundred miles away (as I am informed by an honorable person of high rank and deep religious faith, who has often tested this), it can be used for a cure. At that distance, a composition is made of the urine and the ashes of a certain tree commonly found in this kingdom, along with certain blades of saffron (as I have described in my book, entitled *The Squeezing of Parson Foster’s Sponge*). This often cures the disease when the best medical <note>original: "Physicall"</note> experiments have failed; indeed, this medicine rarely fails when the disease is curable.

I will now relate a true story that happened this past year, 1630, concerning a surgeon’s <note>original: "Chirurgion’s"</note> wife who lived near the Tower of *London*. She fell desperately sick with jaundice and suffered from painful cramps and sharp pains <note>original: "gripings and shootings"</note> around her stomach. I was called to see her after many others, but our medical treatments <note>original: "Physicall means"</note> prevailed very little over the disease. Therefore, hearing me speak of the many cures this Noble Earl performed by using the patient’s water <note>urine</note>, she sent her servant to me with her water to request that I approach the nobleman on her behalf. 

I sent the fellow with a letter four miles into the country. When he arrived at the house, he found two people there who had come to give thanks for their recovery, for they had been cured by that very method. The urine was accepted for my sake, and the fellow was sent away. But mark the consequence: as soon as the fellow had left the urine there, the sick woman was gossiped to by "pious" busybodies <note>original: "demure Gossips"</note>. They told her the cure was done by witchcraft and the devil, and was therefore dangerous for her soul. This made her rage and cry out against witchcraft; she became very discontented. When I heard this, I stopped visiting her, considering her ungrateful. Furthermore, the Ladies, his daughters, have cured many of this disease—both rich and poor—who sought their help. This worthy Lord assured me that he had performed cures from a hundred miles' distance.

## Sect. 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

...asked me to send her urine <note>original: "water"</note> once more; and he told me that a lady was with him on the aforementioned noble patient's behalf the day before. I sent her urine again, and from that time forward she recovered quickly and was perfectly cured. There are a hundred people who can testify that this is true. Nor can it be claimed that it might have been done by some medicine used in the meantime. To eliminate this objection, she was prohibited from taking any medicine for that entire season, consuming only plain food. 

Now, the reason this cure is effective is no different than that of the weapon-salve <term>weapon-salve: A famous "sympathetic" remedy of the 17th century where an ointment was applied to the weapon that caused a wound rather than the wound itself, believed to heal the patient at a distance.</term>. The spirit of the blood in the infected person has a continuous relationship with its salt—indeed, its home is in the aerial salt of the blood. This salt is a subtle earth in whose center the spirit is concentrated. Because this salt is partly dispersed in the urine (which is the "whey" or watery part of the blood), it draws and attracts its likeness from the infected body. By this process, the spirit is, as it were, resuscitated and newly revived; it emits new beams to meet, comfort, and correct the infected beams sent out from the sick body. 

Furthermore, the infecting spirit of the jaundice-causing fluid <note>original: "icteritious humour"</note> is conquered and tamed by the power of the salt in the ashes and saffron. So, as that spirit dies, the insulting fluid and its poisonous spirit decay and fade in strength bit by bit, until it is finally quite extinguished. From this, it is evident that by one and the same medicine, the spirit in the urine's salt and the spirit in the sick person’s blood are both sympathetically refreshed and purified. The flame of the evil, infecting spirit of the disease—in both the urine and the sick body—is antipathetically quenched and destroyed. In this respect, therefore, we compare the composition of urine, ashes, and saffron used in this cure to the weapon-salve used in the closing of wounds. We compare the urine carried from the sick person to the mixture to the blood or spirit found on the weapon. Finally, we compare the reawakening of the congealed spirit in the salt of the urine to the reviving and stimulating of the spirit in the "dead" blood that was sucked up by the porous substance of the weapon. We see here a total agreement: for just as the dead blood came from the living fountain of blood, so the urine was the watery substance of the same wellspring, and it was not left destitute of the "bloody" spirits.

What shall we say about the wonderful effects seen in the transplantation of the spirits of human blood into other animals or plants? Truly, it is a thing well known to those who are well-versed in the mysteries of natural, microcosmic (human-scale), and macrocosmic (universal-scale) magic that the spiritual Mummy <term>Mummy: In early modern medicine, this refers to the vital life force or "balsam" inherent in living tissue, which could be extracted or manipulated.</term>—whose seat is in the human blood—may be sucked or drawn out of a man’s body by a Magnet <note>original: "Magnes"</note> extracted from the same subject, and transplanted into a beast, tree, or herb. By this means, the sick person's disease may also be conveyed from them into those things using this microcosmic magnet; the practice of this will be explained more fully in the next book. 

Also, **Johannes Rumelius Pharamundus** <note>A German physician and author known for his works on Paracelsian medicine.</note> claims that he has cured several people of the **Gout** by cutting off the hair of the feet and thighs and paring the nails, then thrusting them into a hole bored into the very pith of an **Oak** tree. He then closed or rammed the hole shut with a peg or pin made of the same tree, afterward daubing it and covering it with cow dung. Then, he says, if the **Gout** does not return within three months, the **Oak** will be sufficient to magnetically draw the disease to itself; but if the **Gout** returns within three months, it indicates the insufficiency of the **Oak's** magnetic power. 

Wherefore, he then proceeds in this manner: He bores a hole in another **Oak** as before, and keeps the pieces of wood that came out during the boring. He bruises them, stitches them up in a bag, and applies them to the aching limb; he does this exactly three days before the new moon. Then, at the very hour of the new moon, he removes the bag, takes out the bruised wood, puts it into the hole in the tree, and rams it in with a peg or pin from the same **Oak**. And if, despite all this, the **Gout** is felt within three months after, he then cuts off the hair and nails of the feet, ties them to the back of a **Crab**, and throws it into running water; then the gouty person will be cured. 

This Doctor of Physic claims in a certain book of his, published in the **German Tongue**, that he has cured many by the first experiment, many others by the first and second one after another, and finally, many desperate cases by the first, second, and third. And he says that this method of cure is commonly found to be certain for those **Gouts** which happen from a sulfurous cause; but in those **Gouts** which arise from a **Mercurial** and salt nature, it often fails. And therefore, leaving this magnetic method of cure, he turns himself toward a more external kind...

So, if the two stars in heaven are friends, they both sympathize with one another in the occurrences of their emanations; but if they are enemies to one another in heaven, they will, in the meeting of their beams, feel antipathy and turn away from one another. And regarding the distance they maintain in their mutual action upon one another, we must imagine it to extend as far as their beams are able to reach each other. I would have those men who are only concerned with things perceived by the senses know that the action of these creatures by "aspect" <note>aspect: An astrological term referring to the angular relationship between celestial bodies.</note> toward one another operates secretly <note>original: "occultly"</note>, even though the effect does not always manifest itself to our senses. But they also ought to understand that the closer in natural affinity the stars in heaven are (and consequently the things below which are subject to those spirits), the more powerful the sympathizing effects will prove to be, because then their beams will meet directly—that is, without any swerving or deviation.

### CHAP. VI.

->*That the devil does make use of natural things to carry out his strategies among men, without which he can effect nothing truly, but only through trickery <note>original: "prestigiously"</note> or by delusion; and whether those natural things are therefore "cacomagical" <term>cacomagical: From the Greek "kakos" (evil), referring to black magic or evil sorcery.</term> and to be avoided by mankind because their secret effects sometimes conform themselves to the will <note>original: "volunty"</note> of the devil.*<-

<margin>Psalm 121:5.</margin>
We read in many places in Scripture that the devil makes use of God's creatures to bring to pass his secret devices and strategies against mankind. For example, to impoverish and ruin the fortune of patient <term>Job</term>, Satan made use of the winds and called (as the Text says) the fire of God from heaven to consume his cattle. God forbid that we should, for this reason, consider these creatures of God to be "cacomagical" or diabolical just because God made them act to accomplish the will of the devil. God also made him a Prince of the air, so much so that he has the power to stir up tempests in the seas and storms in the elementary heavens; for this reason, the air is called by some "The Synagogue of Satan." What! Must we therefore abhor the air and winds because the devil sometimes performs his mischievous feats through and in them? On the contrary, the air is cleared and purified from all corruption (as <term>Aristotle</term> rightly says) by the agitation of the winds; for if it were not stirred and moved by the winds, it would rot, just as standing water does. Again, if we should flee from and loathe the air, how should we live, since the airy spirit is the spiritual food of our life? We read also in the Scriptures that God causes the Sun to rise indifferently upon the good and the bad, and that the Sun and Moon harm or hurt some, just as they are comfortable and favorable <note>original: "propitious"</note> to others. Therefore David says, *The Sun shall not harm you by day, nor the moon by night.* The Moon, which is called <term>Hecate</term> by the poets, is the goddess of witches, for it was to her that the famous enchantress <term>Medea</term> made her prayers <note>original: "orisons"</note> for the furthering of her purposes. And yet the air, the water, and the earth are seasoned with her moist <note>original: "humid or madid"</note> virtues, and plants—yes, and animals—acknowledge her as the patroness of growth <note>original: "vegetation"</note>. She makes the seas swell, and again, by another kind of position or aspect, the seas' pride is abated, and fluids <note>original: "humours"</note> are more scarce in every living or growing thing. Indeed, we find that all malignant watery spirits are subject to her influences;

...and that Satan also takes advantage of the stars' diverse positions, or their conjunctions and alignments with other stars—both fixed and wandering <note>original: "erratik"</note>—to perform his feats. He is a veteran expert <note>original: "old beaten Souldier"</note> in astrology and knows the effects of every celestial arrangement. Therefore, he can exploit their strongest influences upon animal, vegetable, or mineral creatures that are subject to them. He knows the exact times when these influences are poured down upon them and is an expert in their virtues. These virtues are only at their peak efficacy and force when the powerful point of their specific constellation aligns with them, stirring up their "central spirits" to reveal the full extent of their hidden or secret <note>original: "arcane"</note> natures and conditions.

At that very instant, he gathers the herb or stone, or makes use of the animal’s body parts. Or, he teaches sorcerers to do it, even though they do not understand the mystery of why the constellation’s alignment at the time of collection is necessary for the creature's power. Consequently, when these sorcerers attempt to use the same <term>Simples</term> <note>original: "Simples" — medicinal herbs or medicines made from a single natural ingredient.</note> at another time, they find them weak and ineffective. This is because the spirits of every herb, animal, or mineral are at their weakest when the star—which is their "nurturing celestial mother"—has the least power or dominion in heaven. 

Every true astrological philosopher knows from experience that this is true. By gathering a <term>Simple</term> at the moment when the constellation (whether fixed or wandering) that has essential dominion over it is at its greatest dignity and power in heaven, he finds an admirable efficacy in it, in both its hidden and obvious properties. Conversely, if it is collected at a season when its heavenly patron is weak and feeble, the plant's powers will appear faint and almost dead. From this, it is most apparent that it is the natural creatures themselves that work through their own essential natures—producing both sympathetic and antipathetic effects—which the devil merely exploits to carry out his plans, just as a physician, philosopher, or natural magician does to achieve their own ends. 

What shall we say then? Should we claim that whoever operates by using these same creatures—be they animals, vegetables, or minerals—are <term>Cacomagicians</term> <note>original: "Cacomagicians" — from the Greek *kakos* (evil) and *magos* (magician); practitioners of black magic.</note> and their work diabolical, simply because the devil sometimes uses their subtle and hidden actions to make a name for himself among fools? Is it not God who works such effects in these, His creatures? Did He not, by His Word, bestow such virtues on them at their Creation and continue them through their succession by generation? Why, then, is it not just as possible for Man—who is framed after God’s image—to know the true time for collecting these creatures and understanding their uses and virtues as well as the devil? 

Is it because, forsooth, Man has been blinded with ignorance since the fall of <insert>Adam</insert> and cannot distinguish light from darkness? We gather partly from Scripture that <insert>Adam</insert> knew the virtues of the stars and of every particular earthly creature subject to them; otherwise, he could not have assigned a proper name to each of them that agreed with its nature. But if the descendants of <insert>Adam</insert> are blind and cannot distinguish colors, and are therefore ignorant of these hidden treasures of God, how (I ask you) did the devil gain such a deep insight into them? After all, he fell for his rebellion far deeper than Man and is clogged with a darker veil than he, which is why he is called the "Prince of Darkness." 

"Oh," you might reply, "the devil is a spirit without a body, and therefore he is able to discern the hidden things of God in nature sooner and better than Man, who is a heavy, physical creature. Furthermore, Man dies every generation, but the devil, because of his long life, has great experience." 

I answer: Though Man dies and does not live long, and though his understanding is obscured because of his forefathers' fall, and though he is clothed in a dark and cumbersome body, he still has the revelation of the Truth. He has a discovery of the hidden mysteries of natural things, first bequeathed to him by God and left to him through succession—that is, by a <term>Cabalistical tradition</term> <note>original: "Cabalisticall tradition" — here referring to an oral or mystical tradition of knowledge passed down from antiquity.</note> starting from our forefather <insert>Adam</insert>, and by the revelation of God’s Wisdom, or the good Spirit, which He has bestowed upon the Elect.

For by this Wisdom (as <insert>Solomon</insert> himself testifies), he came to know the disposition of the earth; the virtues of the elements; the beginning, end, and middle of times; the change of customs; the division of seasons; the course of the year; the position of the stars; the natures of living creatures; the behavior of beasts; the force of the winds; the differences between plants; the virtues of roots; "yes," he says, "and I discovered all hidden and secret things. For Wisdom, who is the worker of all things, taught it to me," etc. And again, it is said that he knew and was instructed...

# Mosaicall Philosophy. Book 2.

...instructed in the mysteries of all plants, even from the lowly hyssop to the lofty cedar of Lebanon. Was it then a diabolical action for **Solomon** to look into and practice upon the obscure <note>original: "abstruce"</note> natures of plants and animals? Was it evil for him to find out, through his skill in **astrology**, the specific stars which are their true patrons and "charitable mothers" in heaven, and to choose the proper times and seasons for gathering them? Since the Divine Wisdom that created them operates within them and through them, it was that same Wisdom that taught him this skill. Just because the devil, through his own sharp observation, has also gained knowledge of these things and uses them for his own purposes, does that make the knowledge itself evil? 

What? Because the devil has the knowledge to choose every <term>simple</term> <note>original: "Simple" — a medicinal herb or a medicine made from a single natural ingredient.</note> when it is at its full strength and season by observing the relationship between the stars and the plants, must we conclude that man cannot share in their natural virtues or become skilled in collecting them without the aid and revelation of the devil? When the **Scriptures** plainly state that God made them all for the use of man, must everyone who uses them be considered diabolical? Should they be forbidden just because the devil sometimes makes use of them? It is as if one were to say that God created things only for the devil’s use and not to serve man in every necessity according to his free will—especially since it is said that He gave man power and made him lord over all His creatures. Even if an animal, vegetable, or mineral <term>simple</term> is harmful or poisonous in some cases, it can be life-saving in others. There is no wind so bad that it does not blow some good to someone.

The *colocynth, scammony, euphorbium, squirting cucumber, spurge, bear's-foot, spearwort, garlic*, and such like in the vegetable kingdom prove poisonous in some respects, and yet they may be applied in a healthy way to the human body. Also, *arsenic, orpiment* <note>original: "Orpiment" — a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral.</note>, *antimony, quicksilver* <note>mercury</note>, and similar substances in the mineral sphere can kill if they are applied maliciously and without correction. The toad, the viper or adder, the spider, the scorpion, the *cantharides* <note>original: "Cantharides" — Spanish fly, a type of beetle used medicinally but toxic in high doses.</note>, and such like in the animal region are deadly poisons to mankind; and yet they may be so prepared that they prove to be wholesome medicines and even become antidotes <note>original: "counter-poysons"</note>. 

But besides all this, just as there is nothing in the world that works more effectively through **sympathy** and according to nature than one wholesome and sound nature does with another; so truly is there nothing that operates more **antipathetically** <note>Antipathy: a natural opposition or hostility between things.</note>, or contrary to nature and destructively, than the corruption of a poisoned or infected spirit does when it meets a healthy spirit of its own kind. 

The reason for this is that the infected spirit craves and desires—through an earnest communication of its "beams"—to receive help and relief in its distress from the sound spirits. It applies itself to the healthy radiations for relief. We see this in times of contagion: the spirit emanating from an infected person greedily attaches its infected beams to the emanating spirit of a healthy person of the same species. Thus, by joining one to the other, the fiery venom of the one poisons and defiles <note>original: "co-inquinateth"</note> the healthy nature of the other, but only within its specific kind. For commonly, the plague that infects humans does not stick to or affect the spirit of beasts, such as sheep. In the same way, the *murrain* <note>A plague or infectious disease affecting domestic animals.</note> in beasts does not infect the human spirit; rather, a specific nature is always ready to embrace and apply its beams to its own kind. 

For this reason, it is evident that just as a **spiritual mummy** <note>original: "spirituall Mummy" — in early medicine, this referred to the vital essence or "spirit" extracted from a human body, believed to have great healing power.</note> can be obtained from a healthy person—which is wonderfully healthful and healing for mankind, so much so that it may be esteemed as a **panacea** or universal medicine to preserve health—so also can there be extracted from a person (through a strange corruption of their spiritual mummy) a venom more malignant and deadly to mankind than anything else in the world. 

Regarding this, a certain **Jew** (as I was credibly informed by a merchant who recently came to **Leghorn** <note>original: "Ligorn" — a port city in Italy.</note> from **Fez** in **Barbary** <note>Fez, Morocco.</note>) observed an **English mariner** on a ship who had red hair. Feigning to be very fond of him, the merchant worked on the sailor until the sailor agreed to sell himself as a slave for 300 pounds, thinking he would eventually give his master the slip and run away. A short while later, as the ship was preparing to return, the other sailors went to take their leave of their captive companion. They went to the merchant's house, and after they asked for their friend, the merchant led them into a back courtyard. There they found the red-headed captive: his back was broken, he was gagged, and his jaws and throat were swollen. This, the merchant said, was caused by the stinging of vipers, which were...

When the toads were full, that milk became (so he said) so venomous and deadly that it infected anyone who touched it; it was incredibly subtle and piercing. 

Furthermore, as the previous story goes, the woman was dug up, her back was broken, and she was hung by her legs toward the sun. With this, the Cardinal intended to poison another Cardinal who stood as an obstacle between him and the Papacy. The reason why a red-headed man or woman is chosen as most fit for this purpose is that they are naturally subject to the influences of the sun. Therefore, they are more capable of—and susceptible to—corruption. For this reason, their "spiritual mummy" <term>spiritual mummy</term> <note>original: "spirituall Mummy" — In the medical theories of Fludd and Paracelsus, "mummy" refers to the vital life force or spiritual essence that remains in the body after death or can be extracted from living tissue.</note> is contaminated by the animal poison. After it ferments and rots, it is made incredibly subtle and exceedingly malicious. 

Even though the "specific mummy" naturally desires to join with its own kind through sympathy, it is now infected and intoxicated by the "antipathetic" (opposing) spirit of the venomous beast which has taken mastery over it. Therefore, it cannot embrace its own kind sympathetically. Instead, it infects them through this added venom, and so the accidental poison converts both into its own nature. 

Everyone in that area still talks about a certain hermit who lived not far from *Aix* in *Provence*. Using a similar <term>philtre</term> <note>original: "philtre" — usually a love potion, but here used for any magical or chemical preparation or "potion."</note>, he infected the entire city with a plague so desperate that it destroyed most of the people. They were only preserved and cured when this hermit pleased, and for that reason, he was called the "Holy Hermit." Just as he had poisoned the door knockers <note>original: "hammers"</note> of every house so that anyone who knocked was immediately infected, he also had the "counter-poison" to cure them. This devilish person was finally discovered and burned alive, as he well deserved. 

By a similar strategy, just before my arrival in *Provence*, the plague was brought into *Turin* in *Piedmont* <note>original: "Piamont"</note> by certain wicked people. They suffered for it, having their flesh torn from them with red-hot pincers. Also, recently, the plague was spread in *Milan* by the scattering of a venomous powder. The conspirators were discovered and executed. Through these wicked inventions, the internal spirits of men were infected, and the external air was polluted. 

This should not seem strange to a true student of nature <term>Naturalist</term> <note>original: "Naturalist" — a person who studies natural philosophy or the physical world.</note>. Experience proves that healthy air is often converted into a contagious state by a venomous blast of the southern wind. Pure air can be made venomous by the diseased breath of a plague victim, or by an infectious <term>carbuncle</term> <note>original: "carbuncle" — a painful, pus-filled boil, a common symptom of the bubonic plague.</note>, or both. That corrupted air will also corrupt its next airy neighbor, even if it was healthy before. 

We can observe how the infected spirit of a person with the plague, smallpox, measles, <term>phthisis</term> <note>original: "Ptisick" — a wasting disease, usually tuberculosis.</note>, or <term>ophthalmia</term> <note>original: "Ophthalmy" — an inflammation of the eye.</note> (sore eyes) infects the spirit of a healthy man even from a distance. Other diseases like leprosy, epilepsy, or the "French Pox" <note>original: "French-Pox" — a common historical term for syphilis.</note> infect through direct contact. We find that what was created to be healthy and helpful in humans has become contaminating and venomous through disorder. 

What should I say then? Must we conclude that we must abandon our own nature because it *can* be made infectious and deadly to us? Must we believe human nature is abominable and to be hated just because witches and sorcerers use the devil's instructions to use human flesh, hair, nails, waste, and blood—as well as the spiritual and physical "mummy"—to carry out their wicked purposes and enchantments? Mosaical Philosophy. Book 2.

The author <note>Likely referring to Lucius Apuleius, author of *The Golden Ass*, who was famously accused of practicing magic.</note> (who was thought to be a witch) tells how his sweetheart, *Fotis*, was sent secretly into a barber's shop by her mistress, a notorious witch, to get men's hair to use in her witchcraft. He also shows that it was so common in those days, because of the abundance of sorceresses living in *Thessaly*, to have watchmen with many lights attend to dead bodies immediately after death. This was to hinder and prevent the witches who used to come in secretly by night in the form of weasels and similar shapes to steal away some part of the carcass to serve their purposes in their wicked art. 

Moreover, it is a common thing among them and the necromancers to frequent churchyards and visit the graves of the dead, either for some part of the bodies, or else for a piece of their winding-sheet or the coffin in which they were buried. They do this because of the **spiritual Mummy** <term>A vital, magnetic essence or residual life force that Paracelsian philosophers believed remained in the body, its parts, or objects it touched after death or separation.</term> which sticks to these items, helping them to perform their ceremonies and wicked devices. 

It has been confessed by a witch who destroyed a nobleman's children in this land that she could have no power over one of them until she had recovered an old glove that the child wore; afterward, she had power over the child. The reason was because of the relationship which the spiritual Mummy of the child (which entered the glove through sweat) had with the Mummy of the body. This is no different than the relationship the spirit upon a weapon has with the spirit of a wounded body. As the one fares, in either hot or cold conditions, so it also fares with the spirit in the wound. This was proven when an axe or weapon was accidentally uncovered; the wound would become painful and affected by the cold. When part of the ointment was purposely scraped off the weapon, that part of the wound corresponding to it would ache and be troubled. Similarly, when witches apply their wicked venom to the Mummy in a glove, shoe, or part of a worn shirt, smock, sock, or such, they produce their poisonous effect from **at a distance** <note>original: "ad distans"</note>.

We also read in **cacomagical** <term>Related to "cacomagic," or evil/black magic.</term> books how highly the members of young children were esteemed among enchanters, especially their skin. From this skin, after many diabolical and necromantic consecrations, they create their "virgin parchment" on which they write the names of God, the names of the angels they invoke, and the character of the planet or star to which they belong. 

Must the magnetic effect of human nature, or the spiritual Mummy and its like, therefore be considered damnable and diabolical just because its mystery is revealed by the devil to witches, and its secret properties are converted to an evil sense and unchristian use? Must air be refused and banished from mankind because it may be corrupted by bad means and made to kill? Or is fire to be excluded as condemnable because, when ill-applied, it proves destructive—yet when rightly applied, it cherishes and comforts? 

If, by contaminating or changing our spiritual Mummy into a contagious and venomous state, we infect another—just as one person with the plague poisons another **at a distance** <note>original: "ad distans"</note>, or as one house on fire sets fire to another even if they are not touching—must the use of air and fire therefore be condemned and banished from human use? Or must God’s fire from heaven be abhorred because *Satan* used it in a destructive way to ruin *Job’s* possessions? Shall the hidden property of the spiritual Mummy and the admirable power of the human spirit in wholesome and healthy uses be avoided and hated simply because, through infection, it may be converted to a poisonous state? Shall a good sword, which is intended for the defense and safety of its master, be broken and cast away because a bad man kills another with it? 

A good thing, when ill-applied, may do harm. The influence and light of the heavenly Sun, in which is the **breath of life** <note>original: "spiracle of life"</note>, sometimes breeds unnatural effects when poorly received. Even the devil himself makes use of it to serve his purposes at various times; yet neither the Sun nor its virtues can be considered diabolical for that reason. In the same way, if we descend from the animal sphere to the vegetable and mineral spheres, we find that the notorious enchantress *Medea* made special use of herbs, stones, and minerals in her enchantments (as is also told of other sorcerers and witches). Without the help of these natural things, neither they nor the devil—who revealed their secret virtues to them—could accomplish their desires. For this purpose (as *Ovid* tells the story), she searched the lofty tops of **Mount Oeta** <note>original: "Ata"; likely referring to the mountain in Greece where Medea gathered magical herbs in Ovid's *Metamorphoses*.</note> to find herbs for her goals. Many perform their feats by the powerful properties of stones which the devil delivers to them, even though the witches themselves know neither the starry influence that gives the stone its force, nor how they should be prepared to produce such strange effects. ### Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

At her trial <note>original: "arraignment"</note>, she confessed that by the property of a stone taken from her, she could discover anything. Specifically, if a thing were true, the stone would sweat; if it were false, it would not sweat. It would also reveal other things to her by changing colors. Furthermore, when they desired to see some demonstrations from her, she said that if they would let her have her stone, she would show them some. But they, fearing that she would escape by that means, did not dare let her have it, and instead burned her at **Queensferry** in *Scotland*. 

Some are instructed by the devil <note>original: "him"</note> to take a metal and prepare it under its proper constellation, and to engrave on it the characters of the star and the angels belonging to it, at such a time when the star is most potent in heaven and well-aligned <note>original: "encountered"</note> with other planets. They then find these plates to have a strange effect in many magical operations <note>original: "executions"</note>. What then? Just because the devil knows the virtue and properties of these natural things and can instruct his ministers in the evil use of them, does it follow that *Adam*, *Solomon*, the wise Magi <note>original: "Magitians"</note> of the East, and many other good and godly persons do not also know their virtues, their proper times of collection, and how to apply them for goodness? 

Indeed, what if they see a just cause to use them in an opposite way, yet do so without transgressing the bounds of **natural and lawful magic**, whose true subject is the **Spirit of Wisdom**, which is the basis or foundation of true Natural Philosophy? What do we make of the means which *Moses* used when he, by dispersing ashes, brought the plague of boils <note>original: "the botch"</note> over all *Egypt*? Some will say that this was done supernaturally; let them but look into the hidden secrets <note>original: "occult Secrets"</note> in the nature of other animals, vegetables, and minerals, and they shall find mysteries as great as these contained naturally within them, setting aside all suspicion of dealing with the devil. 

Was the reverend Father *Albertus Magnus* a wicked magician <note>original: "Caco-magician"</note> because he described the abstruse, hidden, and mystical virtues of animals, plants, and stones? *Hermes*, *Plato*, and many other profound philosophers did the same. Or must these men be the pupils of the devil because they knew the times and hours for collecting these things and the manner of their preparation, even though they kept those secrets to themselves? No, truly; for they received them from tradition—namely from the mystical and profound philosophers or natural wise men, such as *Solomon*, *Hermes*, and the wise men called *Magi*, or natural magicians of the East, who revealed them to the worthy through succession from one age to another.

Was it not a wondrous property in the ring of *Gyges* <note>A mythical ring mentioned by Plato that granted its owner the power of invisibility.</note> that it could make him walk invisible by its natural property? And yet, forsooth, the "blind buzzards" <note>An insult meaning people who are willfully ignorant or lack spiritual insight.</note> of our age—such as Mr. *Foster* <note>William Foster, a parson who attacked Fludd’s use of "weapon-salve" as witchcraft.</note> and his associates—insist that all these miraculous effects in creatures proceed from the devil. In doing so, they deprive the Omnipotent Spirit of God and His Nature of their right. 

*Solomon* plainly confesses that all the knowledge of the secret times for choosing materials <note>original: "Election"</note>, of the mystical natures in the stars, of the hidden virtues and properties of man, beasts, plants, and roots, and all other things known or unknown, proceed from the Spirit of God. Therefore, he concludes with these words: *Omnium enim opifex me docuit Sapientia*: **"For Wisdom, the worker or maker of all things, taught me"** <note>original: *Omnium enim opifex me docuit Sapientia* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:22).</note>. 

In these words, he implies two things:
1. First, that the Spirit of Wisdom teaches and discovers to man the abstruse mysteries of Natural Philosophy, which consists in the knowledge and discovery of natural virtues, both in the heavens above and on the earth beneath. 
2. Second, that it is the same Spirit that created those virtues in every specific thing—namely in the stars above, and in the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms beneath. 

Since this is so, what can the devil—being merely a rational creature as well as man—do in creating these essential virtues by which he works his feats, any more than man can? Or why should we attribute to him that which rightfully belongs to the all-creating and acting Spirit within the internal creature? If a person wishes, he may attribute the *wickedness* of the action to the devil, who incites man to evil and teaches him the means to carry out his bad intent; that, truly, belongs to the devil. For he was created to be a destroyer, as the Prophet *Isaiah* <note>original: "Isaias"</note> testifies to us; and to achieve this, he makes use of God's natural creatures. He used God’s fire from heaven to destroy *Job’s* cattle, and the corrupt air to kill the *Israelites* with the plague <note>original: "Pestilence"</note> for *David’s* sins. It has never been observed that he could do anything against man by himself, except for temptation; rather, he operates to destroy or cause sickness by such natural, antagonistic <note>original: "antipathising"</note> means as God has designed for a more upright use. Although he also reveals to some of his poisonous scholars <note>original: "veneficall schollers"</note> a counter-poison, by which they may, through a stronger sympathetic <note>original: "sympathericall"</note>...
