<meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s argument that "magic" is often just the manipulation of natural properties. He explains that even when witches or wicked people cause harm, they are using physical substances—powders, herbs, and ointments—rather than purely supernatural power.</meta>

# Mosaical Philosophy. Book 2.

...synthetic operation <note>original: "thetical operation"; here meaning the active application of a substance</note>, drown or extinguish such antipathetic <note>opposing or harmful</note> effects as they have imposed upon man's external spirit. This happens when they are moved either by fear of punishment, for gain, or out of compassion to do it. This is the reason that some witches can undo those afflicting maladies which they themselves, or other witches, have laid on persons; however, they must always operate by a real and manifest natural substance, such as powders, ointments, herbs, and the like.

<margin>Nicolas Rémy, *Daemonolatreiae*, book 1 <note>original: "Nichol. Remigius Demonolo. lib. 1." Rémy was a famous judge and demonologist in Lorraine.</note></margin>
As for example: *Claudea*, *Fellea*, *Joan*, *Banno*, and *Nicola Piscatrix*, with all their society in *Lorraine*, confessed on May 9, 1581, that the devil had delivered to them subtle powders of three natures, which were distinguished by color. For (said they) the powder of a black color kills when it is strewed on meat, rubbed on the body, or sprinkled on clothing; and that of an ashen or reddish color causes diseases; but the white powder cured those diseases. And *Odella Boncuriana*, being arraigned on January 18, 1586, said that it was the manner of the witches of his faction to strew a poisoned powder in the path where those they wished to harm would pass. And *Francis Perine* confessed on November 4, 1588, that an herb was given to her by the devil to be laid in the path where *Riberianus* (who had beaten her for stealing some of his pears) would pass, which caused him to suddenly fall sick. *Francis Follers*, *Margaret Warny*, and *Jacobit Equine* confessed on January 15, 1584, that they had ointments with which they anointed rods and whips; so that if they touched even the garments of anyone with them, that person died not long after. They also said that if they anointed their hands with this magical ointment and merely touched someone's clothes, that person died within a short time. Thus you see how the devil cannot work except by natural poisons. For nothing proceeds merely from himself except "prestigious apparitions"—namely those things which seem real, but in effect are no more substantial than a painted image is compared to a true substance.

And therefore, let not the devil's ministers boast that this comes from his invention. For true Alchemists speak from their own experience when they say that their "Matter," when it is in a state of decay and blackness, is more destructive than a venomous Tyrian serpent, and therefore it kills suddenly; for this reason, they warn operators to beware of its fumes. But when it appears during the boiling process <note>original: "decoction"</note> as a color between white and black, it reduces the patient into a state between death and health—that is, into a sickly constitution. The white, which signifies the perfection of maturity, causes health, cures infirmities, and prevents the malice that the black and ash colors bring with them. So you see that the devil can do no more by himself than a man is able to do. 

Furthermore, regarding the strewing of destroying powder: the same was carried out by man's wicked invention in *Milan* in the year 1629. And as for the ointment which kills by immediate contact: a certain Jew and a Cardinal knew that wicked craft—namely, how to abuse God's creatures just as well as the devil does—for whosoever it touched, it killed. Again, a hermit achieved the same result by anointing the handles of doors, and he had his *Alexipharmacon* <note>original: "Alexipharmacon"; an antidote or counter-poison</note> for it, just as the devil does. So you may see that a wicked-minded man who abuses God's good creatures—altering them from the true purpose for which they were created by God for the benefit of man—may rightly be ranked with the devil. He may justly be termed a "devil incarnate" because, without the devil's help, he can carry out many devilish ways to destroy, just as the devil does without flesh and bones. 

I conclude, therefore, that it is a great absurdity—indeed, a gross foolishness or madness in ignorant men—to so lightly judge and censure the hidden *Great Works* <note>original: "Magnalia"; refers to the marvelous works of God in nature</note> or occult mysteries of God in Nature, as to affirm them to be the actions or inventions of the devil. This is true even if their effects are bad, and much more so when they are good and healthy, such as the **Weapon-salve** <note>A controversial 17th-century remedy where an ointment was applied to the weapon that caused a wound, rather than the wound itself, to heal the patient through "sympathy."</note>. It is commonly known to God and all truly understanding men that it is the animal, vegetable, or mineral creature which effects the one through abuse, and the other through its true property and virtue—that is, for the use for which it was created by God. For God created all creatures good, and consequently for a good use; it is only the malice of the devil that diverts them from their true use. This is also evidently confirmed by the Wise Man in these words:

<margin>Wisdom of Solomon 1:14.</margin>
"God created all things that they might exist, and he made the nations of the earth healthy; and there is no medicine of destruction in them, nor is the kingdom of hell on earth." And,
<margin>Wisdom of Solomon 2:24.</margin>
"He created man to be immortal, and made him in the image of his own likeness; but through the envy of the devil, death entered into the world." <note>original Latin: "Creavit Deus ut essent omnia... invidia autem Diaboli mors introivit in orbem terrarum"</note> God created all things that they might exist or be, and made all the nations of the earth wholesome, and there is not any deadly thing...

For from that hour, the mysteries of iniquity and righteousness began to reign in the world, and evil began—in the very first actions after the fall—to crowd out goodness. Vice first prevailed against virtue, and physical means were employed by the first fruits of wickedness—namely, the plant kingdom <note>original: "vegetable creature"</note>, or a piece of wood—driven by the envy of unrighteous **Cain**, to knock out the brains of his righteous brother **Abel**. Conversely, this "vegetable creature" was, in another sense, a piece of wood in the form of a cross (signifying the opposition made in this world between good and evil), an instrument of **Christ's** death, without which there was no assurance of salvation.

We see, therefore, that all hidden <note>original: "occult"</note> operations proceed from the secret virtues in natural things. These were discovered by God's Spirit for mankind, just as they were perceived by the sharp-witted observations of Satan. To good men, I say, they were revealed by the Good Spirit to do good and prevent evil—for unless the evil is known, a counter-poison will hardly be found. To bad men, they were provided to execute mischief and iniquity. I will list some of these secret virtues in each of the three kingdoms of living things: Animal, Vegetable, and Mineral.

First, therefore, for the **Animal**. The Owl is said by *Albertus Magnus* <note>A 13th-century German friar and philosopher known for his work on natural science.</note> to have many notable virtues. For, he says, if its heart and right foot are placed upon someone who is sleeping, they will immediately confess what they have done or answer anything you ask them; he says that this has been tested by some of his fellow monks and found to be most true. And again, if one simply puts it under their armpit, no dog will bark at them. 

Also, goat's blood is reported by him to turn glass into a soft and flexible state if the glass is boiled in the blood and vinegar; it becomes so soft that one may handle it like paste, and if it is thrown against a wall, it will not break. And if one makes an ointment of the same mixture and anoints his face with it, things will appear horrible and terrifying to him. If this same mixture is put in a fire, and someone is present who has epilepsy <note>original: "falling-sickness"</note>, and a lodestone <note>A naturally magnetized piece of the mineral magnetite.</note> touches them, they will immediately fall into a fit as if dead; if some cold water is given to them to drink, they will recover. 

So (he says), if a candle is coated with camel's blood, all men in the room will seem to have camels' heads. Thus he continues in his history with a description of admirable wonders which are achieved by the hidden properties of beasts, plants, and stones. 

If Mr. *Foster* <note>William Foster, a parson who attacked Fludd's ideas, specifically the "Weapon Salve."</note> and his followers say that all these are lies, I reply that it was a learned philosopher and famous theologian who recorded them. No doubt, if he were alive, he would tell Mr. Foster that he should learn to understand the "hours of elections" <note>The practice of choosing the most astrologically favorable time to perform an action.</note>, the stars that have dominion over the earth, and the times of their greatest strength <note>original: "exaltation or fortitude"</note> on the earth—and finally, over which creatures in the three kingdoms they have their specific influences. 

For my part, I know admirable secrets in man and beasts for which the Aristotelian <note>original: "Peripatetick"</note> philosophy can offer no explanation. For example: that the dried guts of a pike (or jack-fish) should powerfully stimulate urination; that sucking the blood from a mole whose nose has been cut off for that purpose will cure epilepsy (and that after taking it, the patient becomes exceedingly sick, as experience has taught us by the cure of a Lady in **Kent**); also, that if the mole is burnt into powder, it should, by a hidden nature, expel colic. Also, that the heart and liver of frogs are proven cures for epilepsy; that a snake's skin should accelerate and hasten a woman's labor; that menstrual blood <note>original: "menstrues"</note> should cause leprosy; and that a dried toad—as well as a spider applied to the nostrils of one who is bleeding—should stop the flow of blood <note>original: "stench blood"</note>, as I have often tested myself.

As for other hidden miracles in stones, metals, herbs, and animals, the true scholars of **Solomon**—I mean **Hermes**, **Plato**, **Albertus Magnus**, **Dioscorides**, and others like them—are full of examples. Surely they would not be so foolish and indiscreet as to publish lies and write of impossible things, claiming them to be true to their own knowledge, and thereby lose the reputation which they have

This is because life is within that Word, and that life is the essential light that gives life to all things and, consequently, works "all in all," as the Scriptures sufficiently testify. 

For if the Spirit of the Lord gives life, breath, and all things to the creature, and if that Spirit fills the earth and exists in everything (as Solomon confesses), then we must also acknowledge this: the central Spirit of every specific thing is that *Divinity* in which the essential root of all magnetic, sympathetic attraction and antipathetic expulsion exists. Because this universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> love gives itself to every particular being to provide action and motion, it allows that being to attract its own kind for proper nourishment, help, and comfort. The first of these rejoices or sympathizes with its own kind, and therefore allures or draws it near to comfort and assist it in its existence. The other avoids and drives away, through a hateful and repellent outlook, anything that might be harmful or offensive to it. 

And this is the work of that all-creating and sustaining Wisdom which made each creature exist through a kind of continuous preservation, which it draws from its like in the world. Consequently, Wisdom has given the creature a defensive faculty to protect itself from what is contrary to it. By this, we may see how this life-giving Spirit moderates all things with an impartial hand. All things shall be one in Him, and He in them; consequently, with all discord and hatred banished and set aside, *love, peace*, and *unity* shall erect the perpetual and never-dying trophy of this hallowed victory. This universal *magnetic virtue* is acknowledged by the Spirit of Christ in these words: <margin>John 12</margin> <note>original: "Si exaltatus fuero à terra, omnia traham ad meipsum"</note> "If I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw—or attract—all things to myself." But as of yet, we are subjected under contrary principles; for the whole world and its members are still composed of strife and concord, of enmity and friendship, of darkness and light, of evil and good. We are therefore under the protection of this Divine Wisdom, which governs all things and strives to achieve victory over confusion and dissension in this world so that a general peace and union may be established. Therefore, so that all things may return and live in Him, who is only *Love*, the creature has the power to create a sympathetic accord with its own kind and to repel its opposite through an angry <note>term: "irascible"; here used to mean a natural property of repulsion or rejection.</note> or antipathetic property.

Now, since this Spirit is "all in all" and is therefore present in every specific thing, it follows that it attractively draws (sympathetically) that which is preservative or of a similar nature and condition within the animal, vegetable, or mineral kingdoms. <margin>Colossians 1:13</margin> Conversely, it expels (antipathetically) that which is harmful, hateful, and detestable, or of a contrary disposition to it. 

This concludes my brief summary of the theory of sympathy and antipathy mentioned in my previous discourse. I will now enter boldly into the *practice* of them both. By this, you may be more easily led to believe that the things previously spoken of *theoretically* are actually feasible and easy to put into practice—and that they occur naturally, without any *evil magic* <note>original: "Cacomagicall act"; from the Greek 'kakos' (bad/evil), referring to black magic or sorcery.</note> or *diabolical assistance*. Many reckless and rash-headed fools in this world have scandalously spread such accusations abroad, not only in their empty and boastful words but also through their ill-considered writings. I will proceed, therefore, to my purpose and divide this present book into two distinct parts: the first shall handle sympathetic effects, and the second shall handle antipathetic events, as they are magnetically produced in the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms.

# The first part of this book, treating of the admirable effects of sympathy, which are brought to pass by the magnetic attraction of like to like.

## CHAPTER 1.

->Herein it is explained how, by comparing the mineral loadstone and its attractive virtues with those of the animal and vegetable kingdoms, we may discover and bring to a clear, demonstrable light the wonderful effects that lurk in both.<-

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'S' featuring scrolling floral and foliage motifs.</image-desc>Since it is highly notable among wise men that there is nothing in the celestial orb which does not have its likeness in the terrestrial; so truly, there is nothing in the mineral kingdom which does not have its likeness in the vegetable kingdom; and again, the likeness of the vegetable sphere is found in the animal kingdom—I mean in love and hatred, in attraction and expulsion, in union and divorce. But because in the mineral kingdom there is nothing in all the world found to be so close in virtue to the action and life of an animal as the magnet or loadstone, it is for this reason that we study it. Since it perceptibly affects that which is like it in iron <term>original: ferruginous</term>, it seems to woo and lust after it, attracting it eagerly, and finally uniting itself to it in a marvelous manner, just as the male and female do in the animal kingdom. For this reason, every similar particle in the animal or vegetable kingdom that works in the same manner is rightly termed "magnetic."

Therefore, the well-experienced doctor, Paracelsus <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a Swiss physician and alchemist who pioneered the use of chemicals and minerals in medicine.</note>, when he writes of the mystical mummies <note>In Hermetic medicine, a "mummy" is not an Egyptian corpse, but the vital spiritual essence or "spirit of life" extracted from a living or recently dead body for healing purposes.</note>—both physical and spiritual—and of the attractive means or methods to extract them from both living and dead bodies, expresses examples drawn from the loadstone and iron for the better instruction of his scholars (whom he calls "children of Art" <note>original: "filios Artis"</note>). By this example, he sufficiently declares the manner of extracting the said mummy, and consequently reveals in his own fashion what the "microcosmic" <note>The "Microcosm" is a common Renaissance concept where the human body is viewed as a "little world" that perfectly mirrors the "Macrocosm" or the universe.</note> or animal magnet is, by means of which it is extracted from the body. Namely, he suggests that it is a physical or substantial thing, as he seems to justify in these words: "The spiritual mummy does not work except through physical means" <note>original: "Spiritualis Mummia non operatur nisi per corporalia media"</note>. 

By "physical means," he implies those secret magnetic bodies which suck the mummy out of the living animal and make it operate, both nearby through immediate contact and at a distance—namely, at an unlimited distance—by way of a natural and suitable transplantation <note>Transplantation was a medical theory where a disease or vital spirit was "transplanted" from a human into a plant or a magnet to effect a cure.</note>. Therefore, whoever is wise and profound in these mysteries of Nature, and understands the sympathetic harmony, hidden properties, nature, virtues, and origin of the loadstone and iron, will know that this example may be aptly applied to man. For by it, he may easily discern the "microcosmic magnets" and understand the manner of extracting the spiritual mummy out of man, and also conceive its proper end and usage. 

So that these things may be better expanded and explained <note>original: "enucleated"; literally to take the kernel out of a nut, meaning to clarify or explain.</note> for the well-wishing reader, I think it fit in the first place to touch briefly upon the same theme of a harmonious agreement concerning the nature and origin of the loadstone and iron, which we mentioned more fully in the preceding book of this discourse. In doing so, we may more easily understand what the microcosmic magnets are.

### Sect. 2. Mosaic Philosophy.

The physical and passive mass appears evidently to be a common, Saturnine <note>original: "Saturnine"—associated with the planet Saturn; in alchemy, this refers to properties that are cold, heavy, stony, or lead-like</note>, stony, Mercury-like <note>original: "Mercuriall"</note> substance; and its father, or active form, a metallic or sulfurous Martial <note>original: "Martiall"—associated with the planet Mars and the metal iron; active and fiery</note> spirit. Now, I ask you to observe briefly the manner in which these two are mixed: When the Saturnine mercury-liquid of the stony nature was still in its "first matter" <note>the raw, unformed base substance of an element</note>, near to the mercury of iron (for these two are most commonly found together), namely, the magnetic nature and the iron mine; for this reason—because of their close alliance and proximity in existence—only a light and easy transformation <note>original: "transmutation"</note> was required to unite them into one body. Therefore, it seems to possess a middle nature, somewhere between a metal and a stone. 

It may well be called a Saturnine mercury half-transformed, into which the spirit of the Martial sulfur has entered as a metallic form. It receives this spirit as its passive mother, conserves it within itself, and is thickened <note>original: "coagulated"</note> into a stony body, which is called the Calamite <note>an archaic term for a loadstone or magnetic mineral</note>, Magnet, or Loadstone. Now, since every spirit primarily desires and seeks to be nourished by that which is nearest and most similar to its own nature, and since that nature and spirit is found only in iron, they are observed to come from the same mine or the same earthy womb <note>original: "terrene matrix"</note>. Indeed, the fact that the most perfect iron or steel is extracted from the body of the magnet arises from the consideration that the Martial and Saturnine spirit of the loadstone sucks and attracts the body of iron toward its center, drawing out its formal beams as if they were spiritual food. But because the iron body will not easily abandon its inward spirit, it follows it and is sucked into the magnet. 

And again, the iron, finding similar spirits in the loadstone, desires just as strongly to possess them through an equal attraction or desire; thus, a conjunction or union is made between them, no differently than between a husband and wife. But because the loadstone is fuller of the Saturnine stony mercury than the iron (which is purified from it by fire) and is consequently closer to the property of the male, the iron does not suck the loadstone to itself as greedily as the loadstone sucks the iron. For it is an old, confirmed axiom that Matter desires and longs after Form, and as eagerly draws and allures it as the female does the male. That the iron acts as the male is apparent in the strength it adds to the loadstone; for if the loadstone’s pole is capped with steel, it animates it so far beyond its own proper nature that it causes it to draw a much greater proportion of iron than it otherwise could. This being rightly considered, we may more easily understand what that human <note>original: "microcosmicall"</note> loadstone must be, which is able to extract the human spirit without any damage or weakening of the body.

If, therefore, we would attempt to achieve this excellent feat, we must do it by using such a physical Magnet as shall be taken out of the human "microcosm," whose production and generation must in every respect accord and agree with that of the universal <note>original: "macrocosmical"</note> or earthly mineral loadstone mentioned before. I intend to express this to you only through indirect language <note>original: "circumlocution"</note> and not in plain terms, so that so great a secret as this—the key to unlock the healing <note>original: "balsamick"</note> cabinet of man’s "Mummy" <note>original: "Mummiall"—referring to the vital life force or "Mummy" believed by Paracelsians to reside in the body and carry healing power</note> nature—may be hidden from the unworthy, yet made sufficiently manifest to the worthy and religious Philosopher by clear circumstances. For if such hidden mysteries in nature were commonly discovered, there would be no difference between a wise man and a fool. And therefore Solomon taught us, "It is the duty of a wise man to hide a matter" <note>original: *Quod sit sapientis celare rem*</note>. 

The wise Philosophers in their writings expressed the secrets of nature so carefully that they might hide them from the ignorant and incapable common people, yet speak plainly to those who are the "children of art" and sons of true learning. But this is not all; for I would have you understand that the property of the magnetic human work is so universal that it shows the way to infect the "Mummy" spirits of man with a poisonous and harmful nature of "antipathy," just as easily as it shows how to extract it in its wholesome and "sympathetic" condition for good and healing uses. For that reason—namely, because evil-minded persons, such as witches and sorcerers whom the devil has instructed in the abuse of this excellent mystery, as well as wicked-minded men (whom I call devils in the flesh), might do great mischief in the world by the public revelation of it—I think it the wisest course not to name the internal human Magnet openly, but only to express it in more general terms.

In the same way, the animal, vegetable, and mineral salt acts as the immediate container for this sulfurous spirit. Because of its pure, Saturnine <note>associated with the planet Saturn; cold, heavy, or lead-like</note>, and mercurial earth, this salt—driven by the action of the spirits within it—sucks and draws similar elements from its surroundings. This allows them to grow <note>original: "vegetate"</note> and multiply, both in their airy, volatile salt (which is condensed like snow or frost by "northern" or cold conditions) and in their ethereal or celestial fire. 

Furthermore, the sulfurous spirit retreats, reflecting its beams back into its central salt after it has flowed out to the body's surface. This happens due to "northern" events—namely, external cold. This is visible in the fiery or heavenly seeds contained within the air inside a Weather-glass <note>an early type of thermometer or barometer</note>. When the north wind blows, the air is contracted because the expanded spirits of the celestial sulfur (the heavenly fire within it) flee from their cold opposite. The spirit retreats to the center of the air, wrapping itself in a cloud, as it were, or building itself a shelter to resist the harshness of the northern blasts. For—as I will show you later in my magnetic demonstration—the sulfurous Equator is an enemy to the cold, mercurial poles. 

This also happens in the human body: when a "northern" or paralyzing <note>original: "stupid"—meaning numbing or dulling the senses</note> fear takes hold of it, the sulfurous spirits contract. This leaves the outward appearance pale, bluish, and wan, as the internal spirits of the body are pulled toward the center. However, this movement is antipathetic and caused by an unnatural passion. Conversely, when those same sulfurous spirits are at liberty, they dilate and expand themselves into the open air, having no obvious magnet to attract or squeeze them into a smaller space. 

To conclude, therefore, the microcosmic Magnet <note>the "magnet" within the human "microcosm," or small universe</note> must be generated from the microcosmic sulfurous spirits within its own salt (which is its "form") and from a more "strange" Mercury, which is closely related to it by proximity and "adoption" (which is its "passive matter"). 

Therefore, our secret Magnet is framed from these two microcosmic portions—the formal and the material. Through this magnet, the spiritual Mummy <note>original: "Mummy" or "Mumia"—a vital essence or spiritual force thought to reside in the body, used in Hermetic medicine</note> is extracted out of the living man. By this means, wonderful cures and even deadly harms may be achieved, whether at a distance <note>original: *ad distans*</note> or near at hand through immediate contact. 

Moreover, this same internal Magnet (the attractive salt in man where the sulfurous, life-giving spirit dwells) will perform these same healing effects and many other rare experiments if it is conveyed into the blood by "transplantation" <note>a Paracelsian medical technique of moving a disease or vital force from one body to another</note> from a living person via an outflow—or even through nails and hair separated from the person and moved to another subject. 

There is also another microcosmic Magnet taken from a dead man. By using this, the spiritual Mummy may be drawn out of a living man and applied to human health, either by direct application or by transplanting it into a vegetable plant, herb, or tree, as will be more fully explained as this book progresses. 

However, because it is most convenient for the common person's understanding to demonstrate these things from the effect to the cause <note>original: *à posteriori*</note>, I will begin my explanation by ascending from the grosser elements toward more subtle, complex, and hidden things—as if I were climbing by degrees from the earth into heaven. I intend, therefore, to first describe and demonstrate to you those magnetic things that are achieved only by the physical contact of two different bodies of the same natural condition. But before I begin with the "Mummy" taken from a dead human body, I believe it is first necessary to discuss the mystery of the dead carcass itself, so that we may proceed with our plan in a methodical way.

## CHAPTER II.

->*That there are four sorts of corporal Mummy, of which only one is useful and necessary*<-

Those who have profoundly considered and deeply respected both the external and internal nature of man have perceived that the microcosmical <term>Mummy</term> <note>original: "microcosmicall Mummy"—in early medicine, "Mummy" referred to the vital essence or "balsam" extracted from human bodies, believed to have healing properties</note> exists in two conditions: namely, corporal or spiritual. I intend to speak of the first in this present chapter; the second shall be handled later, and at length. 

Regarding corporal Mummy, it is either naturally sympathetic or unnaturally <term>antipathetic</term> <note>repulsive or conflicting in nature</note>. We find through experience that natural Mummy is only medicinal and healing after its proper preparation. This preparation is achieved chiefly by its own magnetic property. The rest are more likely to breed diseases and to infect healthy persons than to afford them any healing relief or comfort. 

Just as there are four kinds of corporal and substantial Mummies according to the nature of the four elements, they are also distinguished by the elements whose natures they have adopted. Of these, three are corruptible and induce death and sickness: namely, the earthly, the watery, and the fiery. Only that which is airy is useful to man's life and friendly to his nature. 

Concerning those three kinds of Mummy which breed corruption, the reason why they prove corruptible is this: we must first hold it as a general axiom in Philosophy, *that the thing corrupted takes on the nature of the thing corrupting* <note>original: "Quod corruptum corrumpentis naturam in se induit"</note>. 

For example, if the dead carcass of a man is corrupted in the earth, it is changed and passes into the nature of the earth. It becomes useless for man's health and is indeed destructive rather than constructive or wholesome. Again, if the corruption occurs in the water, then the corrupted flesh or dead body will acquire a watery and mucilaginous <note>original: "musseluginous"—slimy or jelly-like</note> disposition. This will also prove very inconvenient or unprofitable for the preservation of the vital spirits. And lastly, by the excessive violence of fire, the spirits in the Mummial body will be consumed, wasted, or exhaled. 

Now, the reason why these corporal Mummies in those states are inconvenient for the preservation of health is because the three aforementioned elements so destroy and corrupt the body that they force its earth, its water, and its fire to return to their first matter. The earth and water were ordained to be the receptacles of two life-giving elements—namely, fire and air—which can only be preserved in a body that is uncorrupted. Therefore, it must necessarily follow that in the three aforementioned Mummies, those life-giving spirits must vanish and fly away for lack of a natural body, which has now become corrupted, destroyed, and therefore unnatural. 

Seeing, therefore, that nothing is required in the true Mummy more than that which is fit and proper for the preservation of life—indeed, for life itself, which is the air—and seeing that this air is banished and expelled from the three aforementioned Mummies, nothing can be extracted from them but sickness, death, and destruction. Consequently, they produce antipathetic effects. So, if a healthy, murdered, or strangled body rots under the earth or in the water, it is not fit or proper for the wholesome use of a man's body. 

The very same regard must be had for bodies that die through infirmities and diseases. Although they are not visibly corrupted by the three external elements mentioned, it nevertheless happens that a certain invisible, corruptible influence and impression is made from the external elements into the internal ones. From this proceeds that "internal war" in the human body, by which the elements kill and corrupt one another. This happens in different ways—one way in one body and another in a different body—depending on which element or elemental alteration is said to have dominion or rule over the others. 

This is the reason that such a variety of diseases haunt the human body. For example, <term>Dropsy</term> <note>an old term for edema or swelling caused by excess fluid</note> comes from the strong impression of water; the <term>Hectic</term> <note>a wasting fever</note> or burning fever comes from fiery attacks; and Leprosy comes from the dominance of earth, and so on. Therefore, wherever any such elementary corruption happens to the body, the wholesome spirit of the corporal Mummy, along with its dwelling place <note>original: "habitacle"</note>, is utterly overthrown, and the spirit is forced to de-

This is true once it is extracted, prepared, and correctly applied after preparation. I will, therefore, briefly move to our magnetic experiments regarding this mummial subject.

### *The Proposition.*

If this healthy kind of airy mummy is chosen or selected rightly with its vehicle or magnetic instrument, it will—due to the absence of actual life and the dominance of cold—take on the condition of the **Northern pole**. Consequently, those included airy spirits, which were of a hot **equinoctial** nature <note>original: "æquinoctiall"—representing the warmth and expansion of the sun at the equator, associated with life</note> while the body was living (and therefore more likely to expand from the center to the edges than to attract), are now made by death to act from the edges toward the center. 

If they are stimulated by similar spirits that are equinoctial and lively, they then become attractive to the living equinoctial mummy by contracting themselves into the center. Consequently, this airy microcosmical mummy must be endowed with the magnetic property of the Northern pole. Therefore, by applying it directly to a similar living man, it will greedily suck and attract his like nature; having drawn it in, it will retain it. Thus, through proper preparation, it may be made sympathetic and turned into a remarkable medicine for man's health and preservation. Alternatively, it may be contaminated and made "antipathetic" using the impure and infectious mummy of a sick creature, so that it may heal the sick person by extracting the poison that infected them—though it might then infect a healthy body if given to them internally.

### *An Experiment upon this.*

I collected a portion of this "Northern mummy"—specifically the flesh of a man strangled in the air—in which the spiritual mummy was centrally contracted by cold. I applied it <term>typically</term> <note>topically, or applied to a corresponding part of the body</note> to the part of my body that was nearest to it in natural position. Upon contact, I found it to be piercingly cold, like ice or the North. After it had remained on for a certain time, I found that as my body’s equinoctial heat stimulated its frozen and northern-contracted spirits, they greedily drew off my own mummial and vivifying spirits. At certain times, almost in fits, I sensibly felt them in their magnetic operation; in a somewhat painful fashion, they seemed to tug and pull at the nearby parts close to the application. 

In conclusion, after a certain time, I took it off and found it much altered in smell and appearance because of the quantity of my own spirits that it had attracted. I then extracted both of these mummial spirits, thus magnetically joined together, and prepared them in my own way for the use of my own body. But because my claim may perhaps carry little credit, I will prove its feasibility and the probability of every part of this argument through many different examples and demonstrations.

## II. Demonstration.

That the dead spirits in a body will not attract other dead spirits, nor will lively spirits in a body magnetically suck in other lively spirits (except very moderately), is argued by the operation of the loadstone in this manner.

### Problem 1.

The southern pole of one loadstone flies from and avoids the southern pole of another with a certain hatred, and they will by no means be joined together in friendship, but avoid contact with one another through a natural antipathy. But if the northern pole of one is applied to the southern pole of the other, they will stick and cleave together by a strong attraction.

### Problem 4.

There is a magnetic attraction from the equator of the magnet <note>original: "Load-stone"</note>, but it is far different from that of the northern pole, both in its force and in its manner of attraction. For the equinoctial <note>equatorial</note> attraction is more naturally mild, acting as a middle ground <note>original: "mean"</note> between the two poles. And yet, in substance, it is all one earth, though varying in its formal execution. For example, the uprightness of a piece of iron will be less perpendicular, and the attraction will be weaker, the closer it approaches the equator from the pole. Again, all those who have written the history of magnetism ascribe the greatest force of attraction to the northern pole of the magnet, as shall also be declared and proved more at length hereafter.

I will conclude with a demonstration taken from the similar "mummy" <note>original: "Mummy"—the vital essence or preserved spirit found in flesh, used in sympathetic medicine</note> of beasts; and it is this:

## *The fourth demonstration, which is Animal.*

It is a common thing, and widely in use, to take a piece of raw beef and apply it to the nape of the neck to draw away rheums <note>excess fluids or humors</note> or discharges <note>original: "defluxions"</note> from the eyes. I was informed by a person of credit and learning that when a simple fellow, who was troubled with sore and watering eyes, was advised to apply raw beef behind his neck to draw back and divert the humor, he misunderstood the business. He applied the raw, cold beef directly upon both his eyes; and it was his misfortune that it attracted so strongly that instead of drawing out the rheum, it pulled out his eyeballs <note>original: "eye-holes"</note>. 

Also, a worthy gentlewoman of my acquaintance told me that she had raw beef applied to her neck to divert the rheum from her eyes; but she confessed that it drew so strongly that she felt her eyes were, as it were, sucked or drawn into her head. To this day, she will not be persuaded otherwise than that her eyes are deeper in her head than they were before. By this it is argued that the experiment mentioned above is demonstrated to be true with even greater reason, since its "magnet" is composed of subtle air and mummial spirits, coagulated by an internal and central power <term>virtue</term> within the magnetic mass.

## *Another relative Animal Demonstration.*

A nobleman of Bohemia named Burgravius used this medicine for his gout: He took a piece of beef, moistened it a little with wine, and laid it on the affected area, renewing the medicine every six hours. It drew out a great deal of filthy and foul <note>original: "sordid"</note> matter. If that same meat is afterward given to dogs to eat, it will infect them with the same gouty disease the man had. This was tested upon a couple of that Lord’s dogs, as Hans Tanker, the minister of the Lord Hoffman, related from the said Burgravius’s own mouth; he also saw it performed on a dog himself.

### CHAP. III.

*How natural things, through their relationship to one another, operate wonderfully after a physical contact or touch is made between them; and how this occurs by a* magnetic harmony <note>original: "Magneticall concent"</note> *or* spiritual continuity, *both after a contact is made in the curing of maladies, or by the wasting away of its like through a mutual operation at an unknown distance.*

---

I will proceed as I began, moving from a general proposition to a variety of experiences, which I will afterwards prove to be feasible and possible through various demonstrative accounts.

#### The Proposition.

It is possible that two "mummies" of opposite conditions—that is to say, one being of a deadly Northern <note>original: "Boreall"</note> condition and the other of a lively and Southern (or equatorial) property—may, after physical contact is made between them, operate upon one another from a far distance. This happens through a spiritual relationship that is maintained between them, acting both through antipathy and sympathy.

#### Experiment to confirm the same.

An Italian Lord by accident had his nose cut off. On the advice of his physician, he made a wound in the arm of one of his slaves and pressed his mutilated nose into it, holding it there until the flesh of the slave and the Master were perfectly joined. Afterward, a chunk <note>original: "gobbet"</note> of the slave's flesh which had grown onto the nose was cut out and shaped into the form of a nose. The servant's wound was healed, and for his painful service during this exploit, he was freed <note>original: "manumitted"</note>. With a large amount of money in his purse, he went to Naples, which was over a hundred miles from where his Master remained. 

The Master's "adopted" flesh on his nose flourished and was nourished by his veins as long as the freed man remained alive. However, it happened that the freed man eventually died at Naples; immediately upon his death, the adopted flesh on the Master's nose began to decay and turn gangrenous. It reached the point that if he had not cut it off, it would have ruined the rest of his face and killed him. 

This story is known to be so true and certain that to this day it is famous throughout all Italy and is in every man's mouth in that country. It is testified to by some German writers and maintained by both Scottish and English men who have been in that country. By this history, therefore, we may see that as long as the two bodies that had made contact were of one disposition—namely Southern or vital—they operated spiritually and were present in spirit even though their bodies were far removed from one another. That is, they worked together through the alignment of their sympathetic beams, and the flesh was spiritually kept alive from the slave’s living fountain, just as a grain of wheat receives its nourishment and comes to life by the application of the sun's beams to it. 

But when the Southern, equatorial, or lively property of the servant's spirit was changed into a deadly, Northern, and cold disposition <note>i.e., when he died</note>, then the life-giving spirit ceased to sustain the adopted flesh. Instead, the deadly Northern spirit sucked or drew away that which the Southern spirit had previously bestowed upon it—no differently than how the Northern frost in the world kills and draws out...

But if that fountain becomes cold and icy, instead of adding Southern life, it brings about a mortifying and depriving withdrawal of life. As you can see in the weather-glass, this occurs through a spiritual connection—or rather, an invisible and imperceptible continuity—that exists between both extremes.

### A second experiment, confirming the previous proposition.

When I was preparing to give my public lecture on anatomy at the College, I had (as is our custom) the body of a man who had been hanged to be anatomized privately at my house. At that time, I was asked by Mr. Kellet, the apothecary, to allow a gentlewoman who had a scirrhous tumor <note>original: "Scirrhous tumor"; a hard, fibrous, and often cancerous swelling</note> in her belly to be touched and stroked by the dead man's hand. He claimed that experience had shown this to be very effective for removing such horrific swellings in others. The gentlewoman, along with her husband and brother, came to my house, and as they requested, the treatment was performed. 

A short while later, the apothecary and the woman's husband came to thank me for that favor, assuring me that it had helped his wife and removed the tumorous swelling. Now, this shows how the contact of this northern "mummy" <note>original: "Mummy"; in this context, it refers to the spiritual essence or vital power remaining in a corpse</note> in the dead man's hand caused the southerly growing and vegetating tumor—which was spreading its influence from the center to its edges—to decrease and vanish. It caused the tumor to rot and moulder away through the central continuation or union of the "Northern" spirit in the dead with that "Southern" spirit which was growing unnaturally in the living woman, even though they were eventually at a great distance from each other.

### A third experiment, expressing the same effect.

It is well known and often proven by common folk that if warts are rubbed with a piece of fresh beef, and that beef is taken to a field and buried in the earth, then as the beef wastes away and rots in the ground, the warts will also wither and pine away. In the same way, it has often been observed that if a piece of bacon is rubbed on warts and then nailed to a post in the sun, as the bacon wastes and diminishes, the warts will also fade and waste away. Likewise, if a dead body's hand touches warts, they will die.

By this, it is clearly proved that just as things are maintained sympathetically in their being—that is, in their growth or vegetation—so too can they be affected by an antipathetic gaze or spiritual continuity. When a physical contact is made between two remote natures, where one is Boreal <note>Northern; associated with cold, contraction, and death</note> and the other is Southern or Equatorial <note>original: "Æquinoctiall"; associated with heat, growth, and life</note>, the one that was touched will be forced to fade and vanish according to the nature of the toucher. 

So, just as the Northern property is an enemy to life and Southern heat, its contact causes unnaturally growing things to fade away. It changes the growing nature of the thing touched into its own decreasing, contracting, and mortifying nature. The experimental glass <note>A thermoscope or early weather glass used to show how air expands and contracts with heat and cold.</note> teaches us that the action of cold is the exact opposite of heat in the same spirit. And Scripture tells us (if we will not rely on experience) that the very same Word of God, in its Southern property, melts and destroys the snow and ice which it created in its Northern condition.

## The First Experimental History

My mathematical master, who was excellent for his knowledge in the art of engineering (and who stayed with Cardinal St. George at Rome), assured me of this: if someone had a withered or consumed member, such as a dried arm, leg, or foot (which physicians call an atrophy <note>original: "An Atrophy"; a wasting away of body tissue or an organ</note> of the limbs), they could seek a cure through nature. If one were to cut the nails and hair and take scrapings of the skin from that member—be it a foot or an arm—and then pierce a willow tree with an auger or a wimble <note>original: "wimble"; a hand tool for boring holes</note> all the way to the pith, and afterward thrust those pared nails and cut hair into the hole, stopping the hole tightly with a peg or pin made of the same wood, a cure would follow. 

He noted that this action must be carried out when the Moon is increasing (waxing) and the "good" planets are in "multiplying" signs like Gemini, and while Saturn (who is a great drier) is low in the sky. If these conditions are met, the wasted limb shall little by little begin to grow again, just as the tree (in which the clippings <note>original: "excrements"; in this period, this term referred to anything the body cast off, such as hair, nails, or skin, rather than digestive waste</note> are enclosed) shall daily increase, grow, and flourish. 

He also declared to me that I would find the exact same effect if I put those clippings into a hole made in the root of a hazel tree, closed the hole again with the bark of the same tree, and afterward covered it with earth. He assured me that it has been tested: as the tree grows, so will the member prosper. But above all, he wished me to observe the proper order of the heavens and such secret and appropriate constellations as he had instructed me in; for without them, the cure or improvement will be less effective.

## II. Another Magnetic Experiment to Confirm the Preceding

<margin>From a small book, lately printed in the German tongue.</margin>
Johannes Rhumelius Pharamundus cures the gout by the very same method of transplantation. He cuts off the hair from the feet, legs, and thighs, and also pares the nails of the feet. Then he makes a hole in an oak tree, even into the very center or pith of the trunk, and puts the hair and the nails into it. Afterward, he stops up the hole with a peg or pin shaped from the same tree, and finally, he daubs the outside with cow dung. 

This author says that by this magnetic experiment alone, he has cured many people. But if it happens (he says) that the gout returns again within the space of three months, then it is an argument that the oak is insufficient to draw the disease out magnetically. In that case, he proceeds as follows: he bores another similar hole in a second oak; after this, he takes the pieces of the oak which fell out during the boring of the hole, bruises them, sews them into a little bag, and applies it to the painful or infected member. He does this three days before the New Moon. 

Then, in the very hour of the New Moon, he removes the bag from the affected part and thrusts it into the hole of the same tree, stopping it with a pin of the same wood as before. He affirms that by this second practice, when the first has failed, he has cured many. But if it happens, despite all this, that the pain returns within another three months, then he cuts off the hair and pares the nails a second time, ties them upon the back of a crab or crayfish, and casts it into running water, and the sick person will be cured. He concludes there that he has cured many by the first experiment; many others by the first and second; and many by the first, second, and third.

All of this must be carried out in the proper order and time. And he tells us that when the bark...

## IV. A Magnetic Demonstration

We may rightly compare the mass of these superfluous outgrowths to a smaller lodestone armored with steel. For when it is transplanted into the plant, it acquires a greater force of attraction. This causes them to become vegetative and to increase and grow, where before they pined and withered. For the spirit, drawn and continued by extension from the limb to the vegetative nature of the tree, adopts that same nature. Lastly, if the hernia is still not soldered or healed <note>original: "glued"</note> up, he then drills a hole in the oak and puts in the nails and hair from the patient’s hands and feet, as well as the hair from his private parts, sealing it as previously described. For he claims that when the hole has grown shut, the hernia will also be closed. He also explains the reason why he is forced to use more or fewer of these operations in his cure, according to the nature of the hernia: namely, for a beginning <note>original: "incipient"</note> hernia one operation will suffice, but for a chronic <note>original: "inveterate"</note> one, more will be required. And he says that in this cure, the time, the size of the tree, and the depth <note>original: "profundity"</note> of the hole are chiefly to be observed.

### Another Experiment by him.

He also says that if we take the nails of the feet and hands of a dropsical <note>original: "Hydropick"</note> person <term>someone suffering from "dropsy" or edema, an accumulation of fluid in the body</term> and transplant them onto a river crayfish <note>original: "Crey-fish"</note>, binding them to its back and casting it into the river, it will cure the dropsy. By this, you may plainly observe through proven experience that the core <note>original: "marrow"</note> and strength of the previously mentioned proposition is confirmed in every respect. Furthermore, if we simply burn the nails, hair, and scrapings of the skin, and collect the vapor <note>original: "fume"</note> using an alembic <term>a chemical apparatus used for distilling</term> without a bottom, we shall find a kind of balsamic oil issues from them. This oil is very effective at attracting, drying, and healing <note>original: "agglutinating"</note> wounds. Therefore, it appears that there is a balsamic virtue in these kinds of growths <note>original: "Excrescences"</note>, though to the ignorant they appear to be of little value. But this magnetic power <note>original: "virtue"</note> of these waste products <note>original: "Excrementitious parts"</note> may, in some way, also be demonstrated by the properties of the mineral loadstone <note>original: "Load-stone"</note>. ## IV. A Magnetic Demonstration.

We may rightly compare the mass of these superfluous growths to a smaller loadstone capped with steel. For when it is transplanted into the plant, it acquires a greater force of attraction. For just as iron, when added to the pole of a loadstone, strengthens it even if the stone is weak—making it able to attract a far greater weight because the iron gives it strength—likewise, if magnetic growths are grafted into the body of the "Magnetic Tree," then that tree will suck and draw its like—namely, the spirit of the defective limbs—more strongly unto itself. This causes the limbs to become "vegetative" <note>growing or healthy</note> and to increase and grow, whereas before they pined and withered. For the spirit, drawn and maintained by expansion <note>original: "dilatation"</note> from the member into the vegetative nature of the tree, takes on that same nature. Through this continuity, it animates the fading spirits in the limb to increase and flourish in its growth. Now, to prove this magnetic relationship, I will produce certain problems <note>logical or scientific propositions</note> regarding the nature of the loadstone.

### 1. Problem.

<margin>William Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, Book 2, Chapter 19.</margin>
There is a strong union in a loadstone armed with steel, and a heavier weight may be lifted by it than if it is not armed.

### Application.

The reason is because **united force is stronger** <note>original Latin: *vis unita est fortior*</note>; for the iron adds force to a loadstone that is weak, as is confirmed by this problem.

### 3. Problem

<margin>Paracelsus, Treatise 3 on Philosophy.</margin>

### 4. Problem

Now, the fact that the connection between the tree and the limb is caused by a spiritual continuity is made clear by this magnetic problem.

### CHAPTER VI.

*How the feasibility <note>original: "seisibility"</note> and possibility of the magnetic manner of cure by the weapon-salve is produced and demonstrated to be natural. To do this more effectively, we will first set down our main proposition regarding this kind of cure; afterward, we will clarify and clearly demonstrate it with evident proofs, derived especially from the power of the lodestone <note>original: "Load-stone"</note>.*

->The Proposition.<-

If, after a wound is made, a portion of the blood from the outside of the wound—along with its internal spirits—or simply the internal spirits themselves that have penetrated the weapon (or any other object that searched the depth of the wound) is carried away from the wound to any reasonable but unlimited or unknown distance and applied to an ointment with a healing <note>original: "Balsamick"</note> composition that specifically matches the nature of the wounded creature, and if it is properly adapted and, as it were, transplanted or grafted into it; then the ointment, now animated by those spirits, will immediately become magnetic. 

It will then align itself with a magnetic focus <note>original: "aspect or regard"</note> toward the radiating <note>original: "beamy"</note> spirits that stream forth invisibly from the wound, being directed toward it by those spiritual, bloody spirits on the weapon or other object that first received or contained them. The lively and "southern" beams <note>In Fludd’s magnetic theory, "southern" refers to active, outgoing energy from the center, while "northern" refers to attractive, cooling, or indrawing energy.</note> streaming and flowing from the wound will join with the "northern" attraction of the ointment so magnetically charged. They will unite themselves with the northern and congealed (or fixed) bloody spirits contained in the ointment and stir them to act "southernly"—that is, from the center toward the circumference. 

By this mutual action, union, or continuity, the lively southern beams will act upon and revive the cold, fixed, or northern beams that animate the ointment with magnetic power. The revitalized spirits of the ointment—empowered by the spirits of both the wound and the salve and directed by the spirits first transplanted into it—impart their healing <note>original: "sanative"</note> virtue to the spirits in the wound, which were first magnetically attracted. These spirits then, by an inseparable harmony, transfer that healing back to the wound itself. 

This is the reason for that sympathetic and antipathetic relationship <note>original: "reference or repect"</note> which experience shows exists between the ointment and the wound. Thus, if the entire part of the weapon that made the wound is covered and anointed with the salve, and the salve is well-wrapped and kept warm, the wound will find relief and be at ease. But if a part of the ointment is scraped away or wiped off from the weapon, it has often been tested and found that pain <note>original: "dolour"</note> will immediately follow and afflict the wound. Moreover, if the designated place is kept moderately warm, the wound will also remain stable; but if it is uncovered and left in the open cold air, the wound will also be disturbed and bothered by the cold.

The details of the aforementioned proposition are easily proved and maintained by such visible demonstrations as may be produced from the powerful operation of the mineral lodestone. We may rightly compare all magnetic bodies and their actions to the lodestone because they take their names from the mineral magnet; therefore, this weapon-salve is termed by some men the *Magnetic Ointment* <note>original: "Unguentum magneticum"</note>, and the cure is also called magnetic. I proceed, therefore, in my purpose to prove the proposition point by point, and for that reason, I divide it into parts.

This applies not only to the spirit of the whole thing but also to every particular part of it, since the formal spirit is present in the whole and in every part.

## *The fifth Member of the Proposition, with the Proofs.*

<margin>5.</margin>
Fifthly, that the magnetic act and operation of celestial, astral <note>original: "astralicall" — relating to the stars or celestial influences</note>, and influential spirits are not to be limited, nor yet to be impeded or hindered in their motion, if we look into the mystery of this business with intellectual eyes.

We must distinguish this Member, for your better understanding, into two several articles or branches. The first must show that the extension of the emanations made from two astral spirits are not to be limited by human understanding, however much it may be guessed at randomly by an external effect. The second shall prove that such influential starry beams, or quintessential <note>original: "quintessentiall" — referring to the "fifth element," the pure, heavenly essence of a thing</note> emissions, as are sent forth from the lodestone to the iron, or from one lodestone to its like in nature—and consequently from all other magnetic bodies of a similar condition in essence—cannot be hindered by the interposition of any solid or well-compacted bodies, as some "fool-losophers" <note>original: "Fool-losophers" — a pun by the author mocking "Peripatetic" (Aristotelian) philosophers</note>, rather than philosophers, have recklessly claimed in their writings.

Touching the first, which includes the imaginary termination or bounding of beam-like or formal extensions, or emanations from magnetic bodies, within a settled or known limited sphere of activity: the impossibility of this (however much our Peripatetic <note>Aristotelian</note> philosophers have imagined the contrary) is argued by these following problematic demonstrations.

### *Certain Problematic Demonstrations, confirming the contents of this Member's first Article.*

### *1. Problem.*

The vigor in heavenly bodies, by which they move themselves, argues that there is a soul in them. For that reason, they are esteemed by the wisest philosophers to be endowed and animated with a divine act or spirit, by means of which they move. This being so, the extension or application of their beams must also prove uncertain, and therefore without limit; for their spirits, after the emanation is made, concur sometimes in the air, sometimes in the water, and sometimes, without resistance, they pierce even to the center of the earth to operate upon the mineral kingdom. They bestow on the earthly subjects that are under them that very formal act and virtue <note>power or essence</note> by which they operate in their sharp penetration. And therefore, these inferior creatures of a like nature are able to send forth and extend their astral or beam-like virtues as far, and to apply their beams at as an intermediate distance, as their stars in heaven are observed to do.

->*Example*<-

<margin>Gilbert, Book 2, Chapter 4.</margin>
If two magnets are placed facing each other in small boats <note>original: "barkes" — small vessels or boats used in experiments to allow magnets to float and move freely</note> upon the water, they will not immediately rush together. Instead, they first align themselves with one another, or else the smaller magnet obeys the larger one, moving itself in a circular fashion. When they are finally arranged according to their natural position, they run or join together.
The same effect will also appear between a magnet and iron, and between two pieces of iron, as shall be explained hereafter.

->*An Addition*<-

By this, it might be replied that this action of one lodestone <note>original: "Load-stone"</note> with another, or with iron, seems to be limited within a certain distance, and therefore what I say does not yet prove the unbounded dimension of the magnetic body's emanation <note>original: "emanation" — the outward flow of spiritual or physical force</note>. I answer that the sensible action between two lodestones does not mean that because these two heavy bodies only move at a certain distance, their spirits cannot extend themselves or apply their beams any further. For it is one thing to operate sensibly by the violent attraction of a heavy mass, and another thing for one Form <note>original: "Form" — the essential, spiritual nature of a thing in Aristotelian and Hermetic philosophy</note> alone to embrace and join in a natural, joyful sympathy with another. This distinction is confirmed even by those who are well-practiced in the properties of the lodestone, through the following problem.

### 3. *Problem*

<margin>Gilbert, On the Magnet, Book 2, Chapter 33.</margin>
The sphere <note>original: "Orbe"</note> of the internal or spiritual magnetic power extends itself to a much larger distance than the sphere of any sensible, external, or visible motion can prove. For a magnetic object is affected at its furthest extremity far away, even though it does not move with physical motion. But if the lodestone is brought closer to it, then the entire magnetic mass will move physically toward it.
By this, it is acknowledged that the powerful extension of the magnet is far beyond the limits of the sphere of visible magnetic motion. But I will prove it more clearly by degrees: namely, that the star-like influential power in the magnet extends itself beyond the limits of any sensory capacity.

### 4. *Problem*

<margin>Gilbert, On the Magnet, Book 2, Chapter 33.</margin>
A magnetized <note>original: "incited" — meaning 'excited' or stimulated by contact with a magnet</note> needle will face the North Pole even from the equatorial point <note>original: "æquinoctiall point"</note>, which is an argument for the unlimited extension of the lodestone's power. For example: Let a long lodestone be prepared, and directly in the middle upon the equator **B**, where the axis runs, place a magnetized needle, and it will look directly toward the North Pole **A**. Also, if within the sphere you place another magnetized needle outside the stone at **C**, it will also look directly upon the said Pole. By this, we may discern the long distance between the focus of the magnet and that of the magnetized body—namely, 90 degrees.
Again, every part or fragment that is divided from the magnet (whether it be animal, vegetable, or mineral) has the very same dimensions because it is as well-endowed with its polar powers as the whole. This is sufficiently proven by this problem.

For example: If a smaller part or piece is taken out of a larger lodestone, it will be endowed with the same life and vigor which the whole magnet had—just as a child's life will wholly correspond with the father’s in life and parts. # Application.

The first and second problems teach us that there is a celestial or astral subtle spirit in all magnetic bodies on Earth, just as there is in the heavenly bodies. Consequently, the beams of each may penetrate just as far—even if they are not perceived by the senses—as the beams of every star. By this, therefore, we may be assured that man’s heavenly spirit, being of a more pure and subtle substance than that of the lodestone <note>original: "Load-stone" — a naturally magnetized piece of the mineral magnetite</note>, may send forth the astral beams of its virtue <note>original: "vertue" — its inherent power or efficacy</note> not only to the target that the lodestone aims at, but also unto the highest throne of divinity. Again, by this it is argued that the spirit in transplanted blood <note>A reference to the "weapon salve" or sympathetic magic, where a wound is cured by treating the blood on the weapon that caused it, or moving the blood to a separate vessel</note> is able to operate at any distance upon the wound; and the radiant spirit of the wound, in turn, co-operates and maintains a continuous union and connection with the blood.

The third problem instructs us that though the ointment and the blood within it do not appear to be mobile or movable at a great distance, they may still co-operate and be joined with the spirit of the wounded person across an unknown proportion of space.

By the fourth and fifth, we learn that the extension of the "northern blood’s" orientation <note>original: "aspect"</note> toward the "southern" may be as far as the equator <note>original: "æquinoctiall"</note> is from the pole—namely, 90 degrees. But I say that just as the northern and southern emanation of the Soul of the World <note>the vital spirit that animates the entire universe</note> fills the entire cavity of the world, so also by it, and in it, may this act of that soul in man extend itself far beyond the capacity of flesh and blood; therefore, it is only to be understood intellectually.

<margin>Ezekiel 36.</margin>
By the fifth, we learn that each particle of man’s blood, or spiritual mummy <note>original: "Mummy" — in Paracelsian medicine, the vital force or essence remaining in a body or its parts after separation</note>, being divided from the whole, has all the parts or proportions in it ideally described that the whole has. Therefore, it operates as well with a northern as a southern orientation, and consequently draws down from the heavens a similar property as the occasion arises. For it is said that this one Spirit comes from the four winds, and yet it is but one spirit in essence, though fourfold in property; for it was by the power of it that the dead mentioned by the Prophet Ezekiel did rise again. And therefore, as far as the extension of the north or south winds may reach, so far is this spirit in man able to send forth its spiritual beam.

I will come now to the proof of the second point.

Regarding the second Article, which shows the sharp penetration of this spirit and that it is effected without any hindrance—contrary to the opinion of some ignorant persons who think that castles, stones, woods, hills, and such like may hinder the penetration of this subtle and all-penetrating spirit: the proof is made by these problematic demonstrations.

### The Sixth Part of the Proposition, with Proofs

Sixthly, after a body (whether animal, vegetable, or mineral) is made magnetic—or turned into a magnet for another body—by the transplanting of that other body’s spirits into it, it then attracts the spirits of its "beloved" toward itself. In doing so, it shares its own power and properties with them. Thus, just as the lover shares in the nature of the beloved, the beloved also shares in the condition of the lover—especially if they are of the same kind and feel a mutual attraction.

### 2. Magnetic Problem <note>original: "Problema Magneticum"</note>

The lodestone has no quality, nor can it perform any action, that iron—once it has been stimulated <note>original: "excited"</note>—cannot also do; and this is true not only by direct contact, but also at a reasonable distance.

->*Application*<-

Likewise, the spirit of a living man can perform no action that the dead blood, when transplanted into the salve, cannot also perform through the magnetic assistance of that salve. Indeed, it goes even further: it breathes a healing <note>original: "Sanative"</note> influence back into the wound.

<margin>William Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, Book 2, Chapter 4.</margin>

### 3. Problem

When iron is touched by a magnet, it re-energizes other iron and instructs it in magnetic motions, so that it draws a third piece toward it. For example: if a lodestone is applied to piece A, it draws the wire B toward it; then after B, it draws C, and after C, it draws D.

->*Application*<-

In this comparison, the iron B represents the spirits that are first animated by the living spirits in a man. These then animate the spirits of the ointment, which are of a "microcosmic" <note>relating to the human body as a miniature version of the universe</note> nature because of the volatile salt in the *Usnea* <note>original: "Uznea" — a type of moss, specifically moss grown on the skull of a person who died violently, a common ingredient in "weapon salves" of this era</note>. This moss is the container for the growing and life-giving spirits that sustain human life—except in the salve, they are of a "Northern" <note>in this context, "Northern" refers to a cold, fixed, or contracted state, while "Southern" refers to a warm, active, or living state</note> property and are essentially dormant. These spirits in the ointment are referred to as C, which work and operate when stimulated in D—which represents the spirits sent out from the wounded man. Thus, we see that it is only one and the same continuous Spirit that puts these three different subjects and their spirits into action: namely, the transported blood, the ointment, and the body of the wounded person.

<margin>William Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, Book 2, Chapter 4.</margin>

### 4. Problem

The lodestone and the vein of iron ore are one and the same; they share the same source <note>original: "matrix"</note> and are found in one mine like twins. Indeed, even a powerful magnet contains iron within it. Therefore, the iron extracted from either of them possesses all the magnetic virtues—both when it is still in the ore and after it has been separated—though it is weaker unless it is stimulated by a lodestone and reinforced by "capping" <note>original: "capping" — a technique where iron plates are fitted to a magnet's poles to increase its strength</note>. When prepared this way, the iron's magnetic power will be even stronger than that of the lodestone itself.

->*Application*<-

In the same way, the blood within the wounded person and the blood that is transplanted to be purified and comforted in the ointment both came from the same "vein" and share one source. Therefore, that extracted blood possesses all the magnetic virtues, though they are weaker and exist more as a potential power than an active one—unless the blood is stimulated by the "Southern" fountain of living blood and reinforced by the healing nature of the ointment. Once it is prepared, incited, and directed, it will have its own "Northern" power. The healing and attractive virtue of the *Usnea* moss is so powerful in its Northern, "Saturnine" <note>cold, slow, and binding</note> condition that it suddenly seals up and stops the flow of the "Southern" blood through coagulation—just as a Northern wind turns the air into fixed and unmoving snow or hail.

<margin>William Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, Book 1, Chapter 16.</margin>

### 5. Problem

Among all the bodies known to us, the lodestone and iron are the most similar in nature and condition to the earth itself. They contain a substance that is most genuine and "homogeneous" <note>original: "homogeniall" — meaning of the same kind or nature</note>, closely approaching the nature of the earth. Therefore, these three—the magnet, iron, and the earth—agree in nature together.

Attraction occurs between primary bodies that are closest to one another and share a mutual agreement because they are identical in their condition. For this reason, lodestone draws lodestone, iron draws iron, and the earth in all of them draws earth; and again, each of them draws the other.

By a similar proportion in the **animal kingdom**, the transplanted spirit—being first animated by its southern or living fountain <note>In Fludd’s cosmology, the "southern fountain" represents the warm, life-giving spirit of the heart, while the "northern" represents the cold, separated remains.</note>—animates and recreates the ointment magnetically. -> 3rd Problem <-

<margin>Mark Ridley, *Treatise of the Loadstone*, Chapter 16.</margin>
If you place a loadstone of no perceivable force or strength upon a loadstone of good strength and vigor—especially upon its poles—it will show a vigor as if it were as strong as the other loadstone to which it was united. However, after it is taken away, it will be as weak as it was before, unless the process is repeated often. The exact same effect follows if a piece of iron is placed on a strong loadstone; but once removed from the stone, almost all the virtue will be lost.

-> *Application* <-

However, if the ointment is either scraped off the weapon where the spirits had penetrated (as **Sir Bevis Thelwall** proved with the ax that wounded the wheelwright), or if it is struck or wiped off (as happened to the ax that wounded the shipwright when **Sir Nicholas Gilburne’s** sword hilt accidentally struck it), then it will lose the virtue it received from the bloody spirits of the living man and the healing unction of the ointment. Therefore, because of that separation, the wound will become as painful <note>original: "dolorous"</note> or even more painful than before. But if the ointment is reapplied to the place again and wrapped warmly, the magnetic connection will be renewed, and the pain will immediately cease, as many have experienced. 

This distress is not caused by cold air alone, which creates a chilly pain in the wound; rather, if the ointment is exposed to the heat of a fire, the wound becomes inflamingly or burningly painful. For **Mr. James Vivot**—formerly my servant, but now Apothecary to the Queen and living in Blackfriars—made some of this ointment last year. As a trial, he wounded a man in the arm with his lancet, then anointed the lancet and held it to the fire so that the ointment melted and the lancet grew hot. At that exact moment, the wounded person felt such a great burning pain in his wound that he could not endure it. Then, Vivot immediately anointed it again, and the wound was quickly calmed and healed immediately. The apothecary is still living and is ready to confirm this. This reputation is better confirmed by the following problem.

-> 4th Problem <-

<margin>Ridley, *ibid*.</margin>

-> *Application* <-

Even so, the potential or "northern" nature of the spiritual, bloody Mummy is extracted and brought into action by the oily earth, or magnetic ointment.
