### 5. Problem.

<margin>Ridley, chapter 19.</margin>
If a magnetic needle, having first been touched by a loadstone, is made red-hot in a fire, it will lose all its polar power <note>original: "puissance"</note> or virtue and its ability to give direction. However, if it is freshly touched by the stone again, it will recover its virtue and act once more.

->*Application.*<-

By reversing this proposition—because the logic of contraries is the same <note>original: "eadem est ratio contrariorum"</note>—the reasoning behind opposites points to the same truth. If transplanted blood, which was magnetically touched with the spirit of life, is frozen or congealed with cold, it loses all its strength and its functional and directive virtue. But if it is comforted by the ointment and re-animated with the "Southern" or vital spirit as before, it will not only come alive and act again, but it will also make the ointment magnetic and direct it in its course toward the affected limb.

### 6. Problem.

<margin>Ridley, *Treatise of Magnetic Bodies*.</margin>
If a thin plate of steel is fastened to the lower <note>original: "neather"</note> pole of a magnet or loadstone—specifically, between the loadstone and the path it follows—then the magnet will lift double, and sometimes tenfold <note>original: "decuple"</note> or ten times as much as it did before. From this practice began the "capping" or "arming" <term>The practice of attaching steel end-caps to a loadstone to concentrate and increase its magnetic pull.</term> of the loadstone with steel or iron in various ways.

->*Application.*<-

In the same way, the "Northern" blood <note>In Fludd's system, "Northern" refers to the cold, separated blood, while "Southern" refers to the warm, living spirit in the body.</note> that has been moved is rightly compared to the loadstone, and the ointment to the "capping" or "arming" with iron. By uniting the frozen blood with the ointment, the attractive power and magnetic force become far greater; it is then able to suck and strongly draw toward itself the "Southern" spirit of living blood in the wounded person. I will prove this further with the following problem.

### 7. Problem.

If two loadstones "armed" with two steel "teeth" each are set before us—one being strong and the other weak or much smaller, but both having an axis or diameter between the teeth of equal length—and you set the teeth of these together (joining the contrary poles and parts), the stronger will catch and lift up the weaker. Furthermore, once the weaker is united and incorporated with the stronger, the virtue it receives from the stronger allows it to lift up and firmly hold the stronger and larger stone from the ground, even though the large stone is much heavier than the weight the small stone normally lifts.

->*Application.*<-

By this mineral example <note>original: "type"</note>, we are taught (by converting measurements of weight into proportions of the spirit’s vigor) that the frozen, drained, and transported spirits of the blood—when "capped" and "armed" with the ointment, whose nature is as close to the spirits as the blood itself—is made into a magnet so powerful that it can attract the larger and stronger nature of the blood to itself. This is done by applying the "Northern" nature of the smaller magnet (as if it were its North Pole) to the "Southern" nature of the larger magnet. By that means, a natural union is made in the mineral kingdom, as is proved by this problem.

### 8. Problem.

Consequently, when blood takes on a Northern and freezing <note>original: "congelative".</note> faculty, it must necessarily become highly attractive and contractive toward its own kind. <margin>Ridley, Chapter 6.</margin>
The North Pole is always the most vigorous and strong pole for all magnetic purposes, provided it has the same mass <note>original: "quantity".</note> that the South Pole has.

#### *Application.*

Therefore, the bloody spirit, taking on the nature of the North, is most effective at operating magnetically or attractively upon a Southern nature.

The lodestone draws iron more strongly from its North Pole than from any other point on the stone.

#### *Application.*

This confirms the previously stated problem. To conclude, the magnetic attraction of the "Northern" blood is the cause of planting the light of more spirits into the oily magnet <note>original: "unctuous Magnet"; referring to the ointment or substance prepared for sympathetic healing.</note>, whereby it is made stronger in its operation.

#### *3rd Problem.*

<margin>Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, Book 2, Chapter 4.</margin>
The lodestone has its specific points—that is to say, its true poles—in which its greatest virtue resides. For this reason, it does not attract iron with equal force from every part; likewise, the magnetic subject does not move or flow toward every part of the magnet.

#### *4th Problem.*

The parts that are nearest the North Pole are the strongest in attraction, and the parts that are remote are observed to be weaker and more feeble in their drawing power.

### *Demonstration.*

Now that the greatest attractive virtue comes from the North, I demonstrate it in many ways. First, if we hang up a long piece of iron by a thread (as was said before), the Northern part of the world will attract one end of it, so that it will stand directly North and South.

Secondly, if a wire of four or five inches in length is thrust through a cork and touched by a lodestone <note>original: "Load-stone"</note>, and the cork is put into water, the North Star will pull <note>original: "suck"</note> the end of the iron toward it.

<margin>Ridley, chapter 17.</margin>

If hung by a thread or placed in a boat on the water, it will move in the air, drawn by the North, and will have a kind of union <note>original: "coition"; a term used in early magnetism to describe the coming together of magnetic bodies</note> with the North Star.

<margin>Ridley, ibid.</margin>

After that, burn it again in the fire, and let that end which first cooled toward the North now cool toward the South; its nature will be changed into that of the South, and the other end into the nature of the North.

### CHAP. VII.

*How it is possible through natural and sympathetic operation <note>The theory that things sharing a "vital spirit" can influence each other across a distance.</note> for a disease in the blood to be cured solely by the "transplantation" of its waste products—at a great distance—into a vegetable-based earth. This earth does not grow plants, but rather strengthens the infected patient by killing the disease.*

->The Proposition.<-

It is possible for an infectious disease in the blood and body to be cured by transplanting the "excrementitious whey" <note>original: "excrementitious whay"; meaning the liquid waste products of the blood.</note> of the blood—namely, the sick person's urine—at a great distance into the ashes of a plant. This plant matter is suited to strengthen the body's nature and to kill the infection that weakens it.

->An experimental history to confirm this.<-

There is a nobleman of high rank, very wise, religious, and highly esteemed, who commonly cures "yellow jaundice" <note>original: "yellow Jaundies"; a condition where the skin and eyes turn yellow due to liver or gallbladder issues.</note> at a distance of sometimes—as he has told me—a hundred miles. He does this solely by means of the sick person's urine sent to him. This is the method: he takes the ashes of a certain tree common here in England and mixes the urine with them. He has his servant mold this into a paste, which is divided into lumps and shaped into three, seven, or nine balls. In the top of each ball, he makes a hole, places a strand of saffron in it, and fills the hole with the patient's urine. He then places these balls in a secret spot where no one can disturb them. Immediately, the jaundice in the patient—whether they are far away or near the medicine—will gradually fade and vanish.

This experiment has been tried on over a hundred people, both rich and poor, many of whom were cases where physicians had given up hope. Not only he, but also the noble ladies his daughters—who have helped many poor people for God's sake—confirm this to be true. I can confirm this myself: in 1637 <note>original: "Anno, 1637."</note>, I was called to the wife of a surgeon <note>original: "Chirurgion."</note> who was severely infected with this disease. Other doctors had treated her with little success. At her request, I sent her servant into the country with a letter to that noble person to ask for his help. 

However, while the urine was being sent, some "sincere fools" persuaded the woman that this was witchcraft. This made her half-mad with worry; she raved and treated her servant harshly upon his return. Consequently, I sent a messenger immediately to ask his Lordship to undo what he had done because of the woman's ingratitude. He sent word back that he would, but said, "It will be in vain, for it will cure her regardless of what I do now." And indeed, she recovered immediately after that.

There was also a noble lady, the daughter of a lord, who was badly infected with the same disease. Finding that usual medical remedies <note>original: "usuall remedies in Physick."</note> did her little good, I sent her "water" <note>Urine.</note> to the same noble Earl, who did his best. When I found the disease still persisted—though her urine had improved in color—I traveled by horse to inform that nobleman of the medicine's limited effect. He asked me to send it again. The sick lady sent her water a second time and immediately began to recover; within a few days, she was perfectly well. There is another person I know who has cured forty people of this disease simply by boiling their urine away over a gentle fire. These things, as God knows, are far removed from either superstition or witchcraft.

## *Certain Problematical Demonstrations, to confirm the probability of this Proposition.*

### *1 Problem.*

Taking the nails and hair of a sick party and putting them into a hole bored into an oak tree, and then stopping the hole with a peg made of the same wood, cures an <term>atrophic</term> <note>original: "Atrophicall"; referring to atrophy, the wasting away or thinning of a limb or body part.</note> or wasted member, as was proved before.

->*Application.*<-

Therefore, this works much more effectively with the <term>serous matter</term> <note>The watery portion of the blood, or serum.</note> which is separated from the blood. This is because the essential "vegetable salt" of the blood—which contains certain <term>scintills</term> <note>original: "scintills"; meaning sparks or tiny traces.</note> or sparks of life—is mingled with it. By virtue of these sparks, there is a continued sympathy or connection between the salt and sulfur in the medicinal balls and the infected blood. For (as I proved in the preceding chapter) the spirit in the urine is as continuous with the spirit in the blood as the spirit of a wounded person is with the weapon-salve ointment. 

So, through a continuity and union of "consent" <note>A term in early medicine meaning a shared physiological or spiritual reaction between different parts of the body or related substances.</note>, the curative faculty of the plant ashes operates spiritually upon the infected blood in the body just as it does upon the urine. This is the reason that as the salt in the ashes works on the salt in the urine, both of them communicate their forces by mutual consent to the blood because of that same spiritual continuity. Just as the plant matter and the saffron kill and poison the infection in the urine, so also—by the mutual connection between the two infecting extremes, namely the blood and the urine—the infection in the blood is observed to gradually die, wither, and decay. But I will provide you with a magnetic problem to confirm the possibility of this proposition.

### *2 Problem.*

Two <term>lodestones</term> <note>original: "Load-stones"; naturally magnetized pieces of the mineral magnetite.</note> correctly joined at opposite poles will be forced apart by the arrival of a stronger lodestone or magnetized iron. The newcomer will easily drive away the one with a contrary face and will dominate it, so that the union of the original two will cease or end.

->*Application.*<-

In the same way, the union that was made between the infected spirit (the corrupting fluid) and the corrupted blood is broken. That which is unnatural is forced to flee and depart from the natural by the help of another force that is more potent than the unnatural one. This stronger force is better suited to rectify and purify the impurity in the natural blood through the union of its spirit, and to kill and neutralize the corrupter in the urine.

I do not need to say much more to prove this, as the preceding chapter fully confirms it by referring to the lodestone and the <term>weather-glass</term> <note>An early form of thermometer or barometer; Fludd often used it as a metaphor for how the human "vital spirit" expands or contracts in response to the environment.</note> in every part of this proposition. Just as blood is transplanted from a wounded person's "fountain of blood" and, as it were, grafted onto the ointment, so also is the urine (containing bloody spirits) transferred from the "bloody fountain" in the <term>icteritious</term> <note>original: "icteritious"; suffering from jaundice (icterus).</note> person. It is then planted or placed in a bed of healing ashes, from which it operates on the living blood in the same way that the blood or spirits in the ointment operate on the veins of a wounded person.

I will now proceed to the "microcosmic magnet," which is taken out of the living man. I intend to describe to you briefly, and in general terms, the wonderful effects of sympathy which it produces by extracting the "spiritual <term>Mummy</term>" <note>In this context, "Mummy" does not refer to an Egyptian corpse, but to the "vital balsam" or life force inherent in living human tissue and fluids, believed to have great healing power.</note> out of a person's body and by its transplantation and correct application.

### CHAPTER VIII.

> *In which the secret Magnet, which is extracted out of the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>Literally "little world"; the philosophical idea that man is a miniature reflection of the entire universe (the macrocosm).</note>, or Man yet living, is mentioned in general terms; along with the manner of its attraction or extraction of the spiritual Mummy out of Man, and its application; and both its antipathetic and sympathetic operations.*

I will now briefly relate to you a history of the hidden manner of healing by <term>Transplantation</term> <note>A method of sympathetic medicine where a disease is supposedly "transplanted" from a human into a plant or the earth to be neutralized.</note>. If this is rightly considered, it far surpasses the <term>Weapon-salve</term> <note>A famous 17th-century remedy where an ointment was applied to the weapon that caused a wound, rather than the wound itself, to heal the patient through a sympathetic connection.</note>. This is because it does not only cure at a distance, as that does, but it performs that feat by the vegetative spirit of the plant. And yet I hope that my story shall in no way sound to wise men's ears as <term>Cacomagical</term> <note>original: "Cacomagicall"; derived from the Greek *kakos* (evil), meaning black magic or evil sorcery.</note>, but only naturally magical. Therefore, it was ordained by God to be used in the right way for man's good and healthy benefit. For to that end did the Spirit of Wisdom teach those who were inclined toward wisdom (as Solomon witnesses) both those things which are occult and hidden, as well as those things that are manifest and apparent to man's senses. And because good things may, by abuse, be converted to evil and unlawful purposes—just as a sword can be used to kill as well as to save, as shall be told to you hereafter—it is therefore God's will that these mysteries should be hidden from the unlearned, or at least from those of the common people who are wickedly minded. He ordained them to be revealed only to those who are honest, wise, and discreet. But leaving all preambles aside, I will come to the point and proceed with the same style and method in which I began.

### The General Proposition.

There may be extracted out of a living man, without any harm to his health, a **Magnet**. By various applications of it to specific parts of the body, this magnet will draw or suck out—according to the pleasure of the person applying it—the animal, vital, or natural spiritual <term>Mummy</term> <note>In early modern medicine, "Mummy" (or *mumia*) refers to the vital life force or spiritual essence residing in a living person's tissues or blood.</note> out of that same living man. This is done without any detriment to his person. When this Mummy is rightly transplanted with the Magnet that absorbed it and is made "vegetative" (growing like a plant), it will operate both through internal administration and at a far distance, or by a spiritual radiating relationship. Once it is duly ordered and adapted, it can be used both for health and preservation, as well as for the infection, damage, and destruction of mankind.

### *An Explication of every Member of this Proposition.*

This Proposition consists of many members. The first concerns the generation, condition, and preparation of the Magnet. The second concerns the manner of application for the extraction of the spiritual Mummy. The third reveals the method of a manifold transplantation of that Mummy once it has been extracted. And lastly, it covers both the proper uses and the abuses of it. Of all these articles or members, I will speak in order.

### *Of the Microcosmical Magnet.*

We call this the **Microcosmical Magnet** because it has the properties of the mineral loadstone. It may, therefore, be easily conjectured and guessed by those who are wise in their understanding what it is, by comparing the animal Magnet with the mineral one. For the mineral Magnet is not of a natural but a "monstrous" birth, because it is not engendered of like and equal parents. Instead, it is begotten in the manner of a mule: its "Mother," or passive physical mass, is a common <term>Saturnine</term> <note>Related to the qualities of lead or the planet Saturn; cold, heavy, and passive.</note> and stony Mercury; but its "Father," or active Form, is a metallic, sulphurous, <term>Martial spirit</term> <note>In alchemy, "Martial" refers to the properties of iron or the planet Mars, signifying heat and strength.</note>. So also, this our Microcosmical Magnet consists of a sulphurous Martial spirit as its formal Father, and of a strange or foreign Mercury as its passive or Mercurial matter—which is nevertheless a near neighbor in position and condition to the Microcosmical Mercury. As for the mine from which it is extracted, it is the living Man, and it is taken...

# The Second Part or Member of this Book, which handles the practice of Antipathy.

## CHAP. I.

*In this chapter, the author explains how the same internal spirit in a creature can produce both antipathetic and sympathetic effects. Here, the reason is also established why a spirit that is infected and corrupted with a poisonous condition is most venomous and contagious to its own kind.*

<image-desc>Large ornamental drop cap 'A' featuring a serif-style letter set against a background of foliage and scroll-like decorative patterns.</image-desc>

As it is certain that like naturally affects its like—for nature rejoices in the presence of its own nature, and nature corrects and strengthens its own nature if it is found to be healthy and full of life-giving and wholesome spirits—so also nature, if it is poisoned and infected by a venomous nature, will quickly corrupt and <term>pollute</term> <note>originally "inquininate"; to contaminate or defile.</note> a sound and wholesome nature by uniting with it. Through such an unnatural and depraved union, antipathy takes the place of sympathy. 

Now, I will briefly relate to you how this is possible in nature. Just as nature magnetically attracts and lures its own like toward it, if that "like" which it sucks in is polluted with corruption, the attracting spirit—no matter how healthy it may be—will quickly taste the bitter with the sweet. That is, it will taste the poison, and so will become equally corrupt as the spirit in which the infection dwells, since they are of the same kind. Thus, the healthy spirit is forced to unknowingly welcome strife, dissention, and antipathy into its own "tabernacle" (the body). 

We see this in a healthy spirit within a living creature: while thirsting for its similar spiritual, celestial food (which hovers hidden in the air to refresh it), it unknowingly draws in an enemy—namely, a pestilent and corrupt vapor—by which it is oppressed and inflamed with a rotting fire. In this case, it was not the desire of the healthy spirit to draw in that poison, but rather it sought the spirit that was similar to itself, which happened to be poisoned. 

Furthermore, every spirit burdened with any antipathetic and unnatural condition desires to shake off that contentious antipathy and return to the peaceful sympathy it enjoyed before. However, finding itself unable to do so, it is prone to cling and adhere to good and healthy spirits for relief, following the principle that "united strength is stronger" <note>original: *vis unita fortior*</note>. If more healthy spirits of its own kind were joined to it, it might more easily conquer and expel its antipathetic adversary. 

We also see this when a person with <term>bleary eyes</term> <note>Refers to "blear-eyed," a term for eyes affected by inflammation or infection, which was historically believed to spread disease through "visual rays."</note>, by darting infectious beams for relief at a reasonable distance, becomes like a flame that sets fire to the healthy spirit to which it is applied; for spiritual poisons are like secret flames of malignant fire. Therefore, just as spirits are joined together and multiplied by union—like oil added to oil—so does the infectious flame increase and feed equally upon them both. For as the healthy spirit desires the society of its like for comfort, the corrupted spirit also craves the healthy spirit to assist it against its enemy. In this way, corruption is sucked in by both of them, and antipathy is forced to <term>roost</term> <note>originally "roust"; to take up residence or settle.</note> among them. It does not leave them until it has penetrated and gnawed into their very bowels and poisoned their very entrails. And we must note that there is no poisoned spirit that takes hold of another spirit faster than one that is of the same species, and...

Likewise, the <term>Murrain</term> <note>originally "Murren"; a general term for infectious diseases in domestic animals, especially cattle or sheep.</note> rages primarily in the spirits of sheep and does not meddle with the spirits of men. In conclusion, there is nothing more powerful for checking or correcting a blockage in a spirit than applying that same specific spirit, once it has been altered from its nature by a contrary state. Likewise, there is nothing that infects a sound nature faster than a nature homogeneous to itself which has become corrupted. This is the reason why the infirm and corrupted <term>Mummy</term> <note>In this context, "Mummy" refers to the vital life force or spiritual essence of a living being, which was believed to linger after death or in bodily fluids.</note> of one man is so apt to putrefy and corrupt that of another, as we may discern from these words of Paracelsus:

<margin>From the Treatise on Philosophy, Tract 3.</margin>
*The corrupted Mummy also corrupts the healthy body that it touches and with which it is united; however, the corruption of that healthy body becomes the health and well-being of the other body from which the Mummy was taken.* <note>original: "Corrupta Mummia, corpus etiam sanum quod atingit, & cum quo unitur, corrumpit; ea autem sani corporis corruptio, est corporis alterius, ex quo Mummia sumpta est, valetudo & sanitas."</note>

As an example: If a man has leprosy, and I extract the "Mummy" from him by using a "Microcosmic Magnet," and give it to a healthy man, it will restore the leprous person to health again. However, it will foully infect the healthy man who took it with the same disease, as shall be explained to you later in more detail. But before we come to the main part of this business, it is most fitting that I make an "apologetic transgression" <note>A defensive detour or explanation.</note>, lest some people—possessing more envy and lack of judgment than depth in true natural **Magic**—unworthily accuse me of <term>Cacomagy</term> <note>Black magic or "evil magic."</note>. This accusation would only arise because they are completely ignorant of the mysteries of those lawful acts of nature. These were taught to **Solomon** and revealed to the wise men of this world for the good and benefit of mankind by the good Spirit of God. Nor should these practices be shunned just because evil men might convert them to evil effects, diverting them from the true uses for which God ordained them. Instead, a skillful natural magician—which is what a true physician ought to be—should first know the good uses of such hidden mysteries in nature so they might employ them with better effect for the benefit of mankind. Then, they should not be ignorant of the abuses that can be produced by them, so they may better prevent and counteract all such wicked effects as malicious men might produce to the damage and destruction of God’s creatures.

...instruct his ministers about the abuses of this <term>microcosmical</term> <note>Relating to the "microcosm," the idea that the human body is a miniature reflection of the entire universe.</note> kind of corruption; and therefore, for this reason, they claim the very knowledge of such a thing is not to be endured, and so on. Or what of hemlock, which was the sign of death among the Athenians, for they poisoned condemned persons with its juice? For just as they may produce sympathetic effects by their right use and application, so by their abuse they produce nothing but antipathetic actions and rebellious conflicts with man's nature. God, I say, ordained them for a good use—namely, for man's health—but the Devil applies them destructively and maliciously. # Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

Does the evil which the properties of natural things may cause—through an unnatural or <term>antipathetic</term> <note>Referring to "antipathy," the natural repulsion or opposition between certain substances.</note> adaptation—necessarily mean that evil is being put into action to the prejudice of human health? Truly, if things are considered rightly, the knowledge of both good and evil in creatures well befits the science of a physician. For unless he is acquainted with the evil as well as the good, how is it possible to cure the harms caused by the bad? Since unless the cause is known, the effect will hardly, if ever, be cured.

As for example: if the nature of the spiritual potion <note>original: "philtre"; often used for love potions, but here meaning a spiritual or medicinal influence.</note> that infects someone is not discovered, how should the cure be performed, or the cause be extinguished or taken away? The true magician does not study the venomous nature of <term>simples</term> <note>original: "Simples"; individual medicinal herbs or plants used as ingredients in medicine.</note> to do harm with them, but to discern the counter-poison which should prevent the mischief they cause—just as the Scorpion cures the scorpion's sting, and the Viper cures the viper’s harms. Must every man who has a sword necessarily kill or do mischief with it? May he not defend another from being killed or harmed? 

So also, it does not follow that a physician must poison his patient because he knows the poison and the manner in which to correct or amend its malice, which has deprived his patient of health. Unless the poison is known, the <term>alexipharmicon</term> <note>original: "Alexipharmicon"; a medicine used to ward off poison or infection; a counter-poison.</note> or counter-poison will hardly be found. If the Hermit of Aix (of whom I have spoken before) had not known the specific antidote to cure those whom he had poisoned and infected with the pestilence, many of those whom he afterward cured would have died with the rest. 

If there are "devils incarnate" whose delight is to destroy (just as some men who wear swords delight in quarreling and killing, and others who know the good use of fire employ it wickedly, like the man who destroyed the Temple of Diana at Ephesus with it), God forbid that such natural things as fire, iron, and the like should be abandoned and not used in their proper ways simply because they do harm when they are abused. There are Saints as well as devils on the earth who, being acquainted with the impious inventions and devices of these devils and their arch-master Satan, are able to challenge and combat them with their own weapons. Scholars learn the art of sophistry and fallacy from Aristotle, not so they should deceive, but so they should prevent deceit. Likewise, the honest, most skillful, and faithful physician pries into the mystery of the most spiritual poison, not with an intent to poison or do any evil, but so that he may attempt the cure with greater assurance and vigorous efficacy, and take away the cause after it is known; for when the nature of the poison is well understood, the cure will be more certain. 

The venomous wound of the Viper (as I have said) is cured by the <term>theriacal</term> <note>original: "Theriacall"; relating to Theriac, a famous ancient "universal antidote" that often included viper's flesh as an ingredient.</note> antidote, in whose composition the flesh of vipers is included. The oil of scorpions, or the scorpion itself being bruised, cures the sting of the scorpion, and that by a magnetic attraction of its like. Since all this is true, why should the wise physician not look into the nature of spiritual venoms as well as the spiritual counter-poisons that are in man? We find that the venom that wounds is, by reason of its similar nature, the most perfect magnet to suck and draw its like to itself. If by the healthy <term>mummy</term> <note>original: "Mummy"; in early modern medicine, this referred not to an Egyptian corpse, but to the vital essence or "balsam" found in human remains, believed to have healing properties.</note> in man, I can cure or take away the corruption or venom which a similar nature has accidentally absorbed, is it not a fit and convenient thing to know the one as well as the other?

I must confess that there are "fleshly devils" upon earth—I mean, abominable ministers and children of Satan—who, being abandoned to their master and head, commit (as I have told you before) many insolencies and treacherous schemes using the blood, hair, bones, skin, and bodily "mummy" of a man’s body. But above all the rest, the wickedness of certain thieves, hangmen, and others of that necromantic faction is abominable before God and man, and worthy to be driven out with iron or wiped away with fire from every good commonwealth. By their diabolical tricks, they make use of a man’s last breath as he dies to serve their wicked employment, treating spirits as if they were obedient to their wills, and so disturbing the quiet rest of the dying man's spirit. Of these kinds of wicked persons, Paracelsus speaks thus:

<margin>From *On Philosophy*, Treatise 3.</margin>
> Through these three kinds of Mummies, many things have been achieved and performed in various places, especially by those who prepared them themselves, such as executioners, bailiffs, thieves, etc. These people not only took the lives of men and turned the slaughtered into Mummy, but they also captured the spirit of those killed—which they called the spirit of man—and subjected or subjugated it to themselves at the final moment of death, tormenting it with various burdens they imposed. From this, the art of Necromancy was born. <note>original: "Per triplices hasce Mummias multa passim praestita & confecta sunt, ab iis cumprimis qui illas ipsimet prepararunt, ut sunt carnifices, lictores, latrones, &c. qui non solum vitam hominibus ademerunt & jugulatos ipsos Mummiam fecerunt, sed etiam jugulatorum spiritum, quem spiritum hominis vocaverunt, exceperunt; illumque sibi in extremo mortis momento subjecerunt, seu subjugaverunt, ac variis impositis oneribus exagitârunt. Hinc ars enata est Necromantia,"</note>

I am informed that the executioners of Germany are commonly practitioners in this devilish kind of trade, and can perform wonders through it—it is a great pity that they are tolerated. 

Thus, every man may discern a manifest difference between the true use and the abominable abuse of a good thing. As I said before, there are "devils incarnate" as well as saints or good and pious men upon the earth; some use God’s creatures for the benefit of man, and others for his ruin and destruction. Consequently, it is lawful for a physician to be familiar with both extremes, though his practice should only be employed in doing good. I will now move on to my main subject.

### CHAP. III.

->**How Sympathy may, by accident or disorder, be changed into Antipathy. Here also certain magnetic demonstrations, useful to prove each proposition concerning this subject, are expressed.**<-

I intend in this chapter, which deals with the effects of <term>Antipathy</term> <note>The natural repulsion or opposition between things; the opposite of sympathy.</note>, to proceed according to the very same method I observed in my previous discourse on Sympathy. Therefore, in the first place, I will propose to you certain principles, which for that reason I call "Propositions," and then afterward I will demonstrate them in many ways.

->**1 Proposition.**<-

>Just as by sympathy in natural spirits each member of the body may be strengthened and fortified, so by their antipathy, those members may be weakened, corrupted, and infected.

->*An experimental example or demonstration.*<-

If the spiritual "Mummy" extracted from a man is mixed with poisonous things and allowed to rot, or else is mixed with the Mummies of sick or infected persons, or with the poisonous menstrual blood <note>original: "menstrues"; considered in this period to be a potent and often harmful spiritual substance.</note> of a woman, and then a herb is planted in it—or the "magnet" is so soaked and kept in a state of continuous growth—it may cause the disease to be of long duration. 

Also, if one gives the herb or fruit which carries the essence <note>original: "favoureth"</note> of a sick man’s Mummy to an animal that is of a stronger nature than the sick person, then the animal will be infected with that disease, and the sick person will be cured. From this experiment, many terrible abuses could be carried out by wicked men if this way of diverting the power of nature from good to bad were known to them; for by it, they could spread fevers <note>original: "agues"</note> and the plague over a whole country. The plant will suck out the spiritual Mummy of such persons as are infected with such poisonous diseases because of its natural growing activity. Also, if the spiritual Mummy is extracted by means of this <term>microcosmic magnet</term> <note>A term used by Fludd to describe a substance or device that can attract vital spiritual forces from the human body (the microcosm).</note> out of a body infected with leprosy, and is applied or in any way administered internally to another person who is healthy and sound, it will infect the sound person and cure the infected one, as has been proven by some.

### 2 Proposition.

The antipathetic <term>Mummy</term> <note>original: "Mummy"; in early modern medicine, this refers to the vital spiritual essence or physical extracts of a human body believed to carry the "signatures" of health or disease.</note> of a sick person may be extracted and then used to infect or infuse the illness into another person who is healthy.

->*A demonstrative Example.*<-

This is confirmed by the preceding proofs and is further supported as follows: If one sows seeds or herbs pertaining to the three principal organs <note>Usually understood as the heart, liver, and brain.</note> in the "Mummy" of a corpse, or in the "Mummy" extracted from a sick or infected person, and the fruit of these plants is given or administered to a man or beast, then the disease will be transplanted onto that man or beast. By this means, wicked men may also cause infection and poisoning. But because these evils are horrific to a religious spirit, I do not dare to further describe the effects of antipathy in spirits, which can be accomplished by the abuse of God's blessings. I will instead move on to another kind of antipathetic practice, which focuses on the preservation of humanity rather than its destruction.

### 3 Proposition.

If two pieces of living flesh that are wounded are applied to each other, they will sympathize and be united, assimilated, and made into one continuous piece of flesh. As a result, as one piece prospers, the other will do the same—provided that the person from whom the added flesh was borrowed remains in a healthy and "vegetative" <note>Early modern philosophy used "vegetative" to describe the basic biological power of growth and healing shared by all living things.</note> state. However, if the "animal tree" from which the graft was taken—I mean the body from which the flesh was lent or cut—should wither or die (that is, ceases to live and act), then that borrowed flesh will also fall into conflict and discord with the living and growing flesh of the borrower. Consequently, antipathy will spring out of that union which was previously sympathetic. Unless the dying flesh is amputated or taken off from the living flesh onto which it was grafted or transplanted, it will cause the living flesh to develop <term>gangrene</term> <note>original: "gangrenate"</note> and decay along with it.

->*An experiment to confirm this.*<-

This is well-proven and supported by a certain experiment in *Italy* mentioned earlier. A certain nobleman had lost his nose from a wound; on the advice of a physician, he made a wound in the arm of one of his slaves and pressed it against his own wounded nose. The flesh of the one was bound fast to the flesh of the other, continuing in that way until, by a sympathetic bonding <note>original: "agglutination"</note> and union, both pieces of flesh became one. Then, a small piece <note>original: "gobbit"</note> of the slave's flesh was cut out of the arm and shaped into the form of a nose on the nobleman. The slave was then granted his freedom <note>original: "manumitted"</note> and given money for his pains. It happened some time later that the slave died. Although he passed away far distant from his master, the borrowed flesh on the master's nose withered and became gangrenous. The antipathy between these two pieces of flesh, though united into one substance, became so great that if that dead flesh had not been immediately cut off, it would have corrupted and destroyed the rest of the nobleman's face.

->*A Problematic Demonstration from the Loadstone.*<-

One <term>loadstone</term> <note>original: "Load-stone"; a naturally magnetized mineral.</note> attracts another when in its natural position, but when positioned unnaturally, it drives away or resists the other. The demonstration of this problem has been shown by a loadstone divided and placed in small boats, as well as by two pieces of iron floating on corks.

If a plant is cut off (for example, a willow branch) and if it is planted correctly

->The Application.<-

So, if the spirits of two pieces of flesh are unnaturally disposed toward one another—turned from their sympathetic union into an antipathetic duality, disunion, or natural discord—then a general corruption will follow after unequal clashes. For, as was said before, "a corrupted thing very easily takes on the nature of the thing corrupting it" <note>original Latin: *Corruptum corrumpentis naturam facillime induit*</note>.

->4 Problem.<-

If a spiritual <term>Mummy</term> <note>In early modern medicine and "Mosaic" philosophy, this refers to the vital essence or spiritual life-force that resides in the blood and tissues.</note> is corrupted by some foreign or strange infectious nature, the healthy and wholesome Mummy of a body that is not infected will still magnetically attract it. However, it will not do so as affectionately, but more slowly, because the strange venom adheres to it. This causes a mixture of antipathy with sympathy. 

The reason for that slowness in repelling the antipathetic attack is because the healthy and homogeneous <note>original: "homogeniall"; meaning of the same nature or substance.</note> Mummy partly attracts its sympathetic "like" through its desiring <note>original: "concupiscible"</note> act, and partly expels its contaminating "unlike" through its repelling <note>original: "irascible"</note> property. But because this antipathetic "unlike" clings so tightly to its infected "like," the resistive expulsion is only slow. Thus, the healthy spiritual Mummy becomes just as corrupted and infected as the other, and by that means, sympathy is turned into antipathy.

->An Experiment to confirm this.<-

There are many proofs to maintain this. For instance, when a corrupted spiritual Mummy is carried through the air from someone infected with a <term>pestilent fever</term> <note>A highly contagious, plague-like fever.</note> or smallpox, the Mummy so infected unites itself—being of the same nature—to the healthy man's spirit. In that regard, the one embraces the other. 

However, when the healthy Mummial spirit perceives and "tastes" the heterogeneous <note>original: "heterogeniall"; meaning of a different or foreign nature.</note> or infected nature which clings to its "like," it only slowly expels or resists it. This is because it simultaneously craves its "like" (and therefore attracts it sympathetically) and hates its "unlike" (and therefore expels it antipathetically). For this reason, the process is slow, and this is why the expulsive crisis does not happen suddenly after the poisonous infection is received. Neither will sweats, fluxes, or nosebleeds—which are signs of the resistance and expulsive faculty fighting the contagious antipathy—suddenly appear. This process is completed sometimes by the healthy spirit's victory, and sometimes by its failed attempt.

->1. A Problematical Demonstration derived from the Lodestone.<-

When a small piece of iron is put into a small boat along with other materials and floated upon the water, and a <term>lodestone</term> <note>original: "Load-stone"; a naturally magnetized mineral.</note> is placed in another vessel on the same water nearby, the union <note>original: "coition"</note> made between these two magnetic bodies will be depraved, weak, and unnatural. This is because the magnet affects and draws its "like" (or its best-beloved) most strongly when that object is not weighted down or mixed with materials of a contrary nature that do not agree with it in sympathy.

->An Application.<-

To conclude, a Mummy that has an antipathetic infection joined to it, when applied to a strong and healthy Mummy, is like a piece of the stone called *Theamides* <note>A legendary stone mentioned in classical texts (like Pliny) said to have the opposite property of a lodestone: it repels iron.</note>. This stone is antipathetic to the magnet, for it repels iron or the magnet itself, just as the magnet attracts them. Because of this attraction, its expulsion would be slower. Therefore, magnetic philosophers also hold this as a maxim:

### 2 Problem.
The joining <note>original: "coition"</note> or union between two magnetic bodies is quicker and more agile than the flight or "divorce" from one another. Experience teaches that magnetic bodies are more sluggishly repelled than they are allured or drawn toward one another. The reason is that there is some antipathetic invasion which causes that hatred, creating that angry <note>original: "irascible"</note> resistance between the homogeneous spirit of the Mummy and the heterogeneous poison or infection within it. We must consider that magnetic bodies naturally crave sympathetic union.

### 5 Proposition.
Consider two <term>Mummies</term> <note>The vital life force or "spiritual essence" found in tissues and blood.</note> from different bodies, where one is healthy and the other is infected. In their first meeting, they may seem to agree because of the homogeneous respect between them (since in their pure state they are of one and the same essence). However, because one is infected, it has taken on a heterogeneous disposition contrary to the essence of them both. For that reason, the second Mummy strives to be divorced from them both. This is proved by the following problematic demonstration drawn from the properties of the loadstone.

### 3 Problem.
<margin>William Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, Book 3, Chapter 8. Mark Ridley, Chapter 21.</margin>
If you place two small wires on the poles of a <term>loadstone</term> <note>A naturally magnetized piece of the mineral magnetite.</note>, you will observe that these wires stick together at their lower ends on the point of the pole. However, at their tops, they will be in discord and turned away from each other. You will see them form a fork, as if one end were avoiding and fleeing from the company and society of the other.

---

-># THE CONCLUSION.<-

I could, wise reader, have created a entire volume of experimental propositions with their problematic proofs regarding the infinite abyss of sympathetic and antipathetic effects in the three kingdoms—namely, Animal, Vegetable, and Mineral. This includes how they interact within each species and from the individuals of one kind to another. 

But it is not my intention to express my bolder and more settled opinions regarding the true philosophy and its related subjects in a longer English work. I consider the roughness and harshness of my writing, due to my own defects and the insufficient polish of my style. Furthermore, I know that polished words and phrases are but superficial flashes and flying shadows of a wealthy and rich subject. Just as these words are like Proteus—changeable into an infinity of colors—so also are men's fancies and judgments variable. As the proverb says, *So many men, so many minds*. 

I imagine, and my mind tells me, that no matter how careful I am in my writing, or how laborious I am in my phrasing, my best endeavors will appear faulty in the nitpicking eyesight of some men, though perhaps they will be acceptable enough to others. I consider it sufficient, therefore, that I dare to be hardy and bold in the fundamental subject of essential philosophy. It has Truth itself to maintain and defend it, without needing any decoration made by the gilded tresses of superficial speeches or verbal explanations. Therefore, just as "Truth does not seek out corners" <note>original Latin: *veritas non quærit angulos*; a maxim suggesting that truth is open and does not need to hide in shadows or use deception.</note>, she also does not need the expression of eloquent words or refined sentences to illustrate her and make her clearer in the eyes of wise and learned men, being that it
<meta>The text continues on the next page with "is".</meta>

<meta>This page concludes the final book of the work. It transitions from the specific discussion of magnetic "Mummy" (the vital essence) to a grand theological conclusion, identifying the source of all natural and spiritual phenomena as Divine Wisdom and the "Spiritual Christ."</meta>

<page-num>300</page-num>
<header>Mosaic Philosophy: Book 3.</header>

...it is not unknown to them that she <note>The author is referring to Wisdom (Sophia), often personified as a female emanation of God.</note> conquers everything, for she is the bright splendor or emanation that springs from the all-powerful and eternal fountain. She enlightens everyone, she acts essentially in all things and over all things, and reveals herself in her effects to all. Therefore, she is so manifest in all her works that she does not need any golden-tongued orator, nor any smooth and methodical rhetorician, or philosopher learned only in speech <note>original: "lip-learned"</note> to honor her by expressing her excellence or recording the perfection of her graces. 

These graces are revealed to the entire world, though the unworthy people of this world will not acknowledge or receive her with the reverence they ought to. Instead, they try their best to hide her perpetually behind a veil of obscure ignorance. In doing so, they do not stop daily persecuting and crucifying that spiritual Christ, who is the only truth <note>original: "verity"</note>, true wisdom, cornerstone, and essential subject of the true Philosophy. May his Name be blessed forever and ever. He alone has made the heavens and the earth and everything within them, and he sustains and preserves them by the life-giving power <note>original: "vivification"</note> of his Spirit. This Spirit operates in all things and reigns in power and glory with the Father forever and ever. He will defend his servants from the oppression of evil-minded men and stand as a shield of defense to preserve the proclaimer of his truth from the snake-like tongues of malicious backbiters and the venomous criticisms of the cynical and satirical *Momus* <note>In Greek mythology, Momus was the personification of satire and mockery.</note>.

<margin>Luke 21:15.</margin>
It is he who says to those who adore his truth: "I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries will not be able to resist or contradict" <note>original: "Ego dabo vobis os & sapientiam cui non poterant resistere & contradicere omnes adversarii vestri."</note>. And therefore I will say as the Prophet *David* did: "In the shadow of your wings I will sing" <note>original: "In alarum tuarum umbra canam"; see Psalm 63:7.</note>. O Lord, in you do I put my trust; keep and preserve me from my enemies, for your mercy's sake, AMEN.
